title: Permanent Substitute (2026-2027 SY) - IMMEDIATE VACANCY
description:
JEFFERSON RISE CHARTER SCHOOL

Harvey, Louisiana | Grades 6-12 | 2026-2027 School Year



School Overview

Founded in 2014, Jefferson RISE is a tuition-free public charter school serving nearly 800 students in grades 6-12 in Harvey, Louisiana. At Jefferson RISE, we believe every student deserves a real path forward. Whether that means a four-year university, a skilled trade, the military, entrepreneurship, or something else entirely, our job is to make sure every student graduates prepared and ready. We get there through rigorous academics, strong relationships, consistent accountability, and a genuine commitment to each student's individual success.


Our student body reflects the diversity of the Westbank:

  • We have a diverse population of students based on race and ethnicity:
    • 61% Black/African American
    • 16% Hispanic
    • 14% Middle Eastern
    • 6% White (Non-Middle Eastern)
    • 2% Asian
    • 1% Other
  • 87% qualify as economically disadvantaged
  • 13% Students with Disabilities
  • 4% English Learners



Recent Achievements:

  • Top Gains Award - Louisiana Department of Education (2023-24 SY)
  • Average graduation rate of 98% since our first graduating class in 2022
  • #6 for SPS Growth in Louisiana - High School: B rating, Middle School: C rating (2022-23 SY)
  • Continued SPS growth: 72.5 in 2023-24 and 73.9 in 2024-25



Schedule and Calendar:

As a charter school, Jefferson RISE sets its own academic calendar and daily schedule based on the needs of its students. Teachers generally work from mid-July (beginning with professional development before students arrive) through late May.


Workdays are generally 7:10 AM - 3:45 PM, Monday through Friday. Mondays extend to 4:30 PM and include mandatory Professional Development time. Anticipated school hours and days vary annually based on changes to the school calendar.



Position Title: Permanent Substitue


Position Information:

  • Department: Substitutes
  • Reports to: Coordinator, School Logistics and Substitutes
  • Work Schedule: 10-month (mid/late July - mid/late May)
  • Employment Type: Full time, Exempt
  • Location: Harvey, LA


Position Summary

At Jefferson RISE, instruction doesn’t pause when a teacher is absent. The Permanent Substitute plays a critical role in ensuring continuity of learning by delivering strong, consistent instruction across classrooms. This role goes beyond coverage—it requires a confident instructional presence, effective classroom management, and a commitment to maintaining a positive, productive learning environment.

This position is well-suited for someone who thrives in a fast-paced setting, adapts quickly, and approaches each day as an opportunity to support student growth and uphold high expectations.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Instruction & Classroom Management

  • Deliver clear, engaging instruction aligned to teacher lesson plans and school expectations
  • Maintain a safe, structured, and respectful classroom through strong management practices (e.g., active monitoring, circulation, positive narration)
  • Build quick, positive relationships with students across grade levels and subject areas
  • Provide in-the-moment feedback to support student learning and behavior
  • Ensure continuity of learning by keeping students engaged and on task throughout the class period

Adaptability & Problem Solving

  • Transition seamlessly across classrooms, subjects, and routines with minimal preparation time
  • Navigate unexpected challenges with professionalism and a solutions-oriented mindset
  • Uphold consistent expectations and procedures across all assignments

Professional Responsibilities

  • Take accurate attendance and ensure completion and submission of student work
  • Communicate effectively with staff to support smooth classroom transitions
  • Reflect on performance and actively seek feedback to strengthen practice




CANDIDATE PROFILE

Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degreee preferred, not required
  • High School Diploma required
  • Strong classroom management and communication skills
  • Flexible, solutions-oriented, and quick to adapt
  • Reliable, professional, and student-centered
  • Committed to maintaining high-quality instruction at all times
  • Open to feedback and driven to grow

Culture and Fit

  • Believes every student has a path worth investing in - college, a skilled trade, the military, entrepreneurship, the arts, athletics, or something entirely their own
  • Holds students to high expectations because they see possibility in every student
  • Open to feedback and accountable for outcomes
  • Collaborative, dependable, and a consistent presence for students, families, and colleagues



COMPENSATION

Jefferson RISE offers competitive compensation tied to performance and qualifications. We do not follow a traditional salary schedule - annual salaries reflect the outcomes teachers drive and the value they bring to students and the school.

  • Annual Salary Ranges: $35,000 - $50,000 starting salary depending on degree level, certification, content, previous student outcomes, and experience
  • Additional Stipends Available: Employees may be eligible for stipends or supplemental compensation for approved responsibilities that extend beyond the regular duties of their position. Examples may include athletic coaching, club sponsorship, leadership, special projects, additional workdays, extended hours, or other assigned duties. Eligibility and amounts are determined by the school and may vary from year to year.
  • Raises and Bonuses: We believe exceptional performance should be recognized. Employees may be eligible for performance-based raises and bonuses. Eligibility and award amounts are determined based on demonstrated results, contributions to the organization, available funding, and other relevant factors.
  • Paid twice monthly on the 15th and last day of each month


Benefits

All full-time employees receive the following employee-only coverage:

  • Medical: RISE covers 85% of employee-only premiums; employee covers 15% (spouse and dependent costs are the employee's responsibility)
  • Dental and Vision: 100% of employee-only premiums covered
  • Short and Long-Term Disability: 100% of premiums covered
  • 401(k): 100% employer match on first 3% deferred; 50% match on contributions from 3% to 5%; no vesting period

Jefferson RISE reserves the right to offer different or additional benefits at any time.

Our end-to-end operational workflow enables automation, standardisation and cost transparency on all FX transactions and cash movements.


A highly secure platform centralises all client FX and cash activities to enhance oversight whilst increasing control, all at no additional costs. It offers quick onboarding routes, multi-bank best execution and hedging management services.


Headquartered in London, the world’s largest FX hub, MillTech provides services to clients in the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Switzerland, Belgium, Denmark, Ireland, Luxembourg, Norway and Liechtenstein. MillTech is authorised and regulated by the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA FRN 911636) and registered with the USA’s National Futures Association (NFA).


Your responsibilities in this role will include:

The role is in the Quant Solutions Group within the firm and involves:

  • Conducting research on FX markets and currency risk management using advanced quantitative, statistical, machine learning and AI techniques.
  • Analysing structured, semi-structured and unstructured data to identify insights, signals and opportunities to improve risk management strategies and analytics.
  • Researching and evaluating the latest developments in quantitative finance, AI and machine learning and applying relevant techniques to real-world financial market problems.
  • Developing robust research prototypes and analytical workflows in Python.
  • Providing occasional support in deploying successful research into production, working with technology teams where required. The primary focus of the role is quantitative research rather than software engineering.
  • Staying up to date with developments in financial markets, quantitative research, AI and machine learning.


Requirements:

A recent graduate in a quantitative field from a reputable university, ideally in a subject involving substantial quantitative, statistical and programming components. Proficiency in Python is essential, alongside experience with, or strong interest in, machine learning and AI.



Required Skills:

  • Education: BSc/MSc in a technical degree, including but not limited to Mathematics, Quantitative Finance, Physics, Computer Science, Statistics or Engineering.
  • Machine Learning and AI: Experience with machine learning and AI techniques, or a strong ability and willingness to learn new techniques quickly.
  • Python and Data Structures: Strong Python programming skills, including familiarity with NumPy, Pandas, scikit-learn and core concepts such as data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
  • Quantitative Research: Strong analytical skills and the ability to formulate hypotheses, test ideas rigorously and interpret empirical results.
  • Financial Markets: Demonstrable interest in FX, financial markets, quantitative investing or risk management.



Desirable Skills and Experience:

  • Experience with financial time-series analysis or quantitative research.
  • Experience with agentic frameworks such as LangGraph.
  • Understanding of RAG, graph databases or knowledge graphs.
  • Experience with cloud services, preferably AWS.
  • Familiarity with Docker and basic deployment workflows.
  • Understanding of relational and NoSQL databases.



What we offer in return:

Our commitment is to help you flourish in this role, through support with your professional development, opportunities to be involved in key projects, and exposure to challenges that you may not be offered in a larger organisation. We will provide:

  • A competitive salary with annual reviews;
  • 25 days’ paid annual leave plus an additional day per year of service;
  • Excellent staff development and training opportunities;
  • Flexible working arrangements including remote working;
  • Medical insurance;
  • Dental insurance;
  • EV Scheme and Cycle to work scheme;
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity leave;
  • 1 day off for charity work per quarter and many other benefits!

How to apply?

At MillTech we believe that diversity and inclusion are essential for fostering innovation and building a strong, supportive work environment. We are committed to embedding the best equality and diversity practices into all our activities, making us an inclusive, welcoming, and exciting place to work. We would welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences.


We would love to hear from you if you think that you’re a good fit for this role. To apply you should upload your CV. One of the team will then be in touch with you to discuss the next steps.

title: Senior QA Analyst
description:
NOTE:

  • Work Schedule: 8 to 5 Mon thru Fri; Remote but at minimum once a quarter, but more frequently as needed based on project needs.

Short Description:

Under broad supervision, will provide adequate testing feedback to ensure enhancements and changes are operating effectively within the testing environment.

Complete Description:

Position Overview:

  • The Child and Protective Care Services division (CAPS) Senior UAT & Business Analyst reports to the CAPS Sr. Manager of Technical Solutions. Under broad supervision, this role is responsible for leading User Acceptance Testing (UAT), test strategy development, business analysis activities, and quality assurance coordination across CAPS systems and related enterprise applications.
  • This position serves as a senior-level quality and business analysis resource responsible for ensuring systems, data, integrations, reporting solutions, and business processes meet business requirements, Federal/State policy standards, and operational expectations. This role bridges the gap between business stakeholders, SMEs, Business System Owners (BSOs), developers, vendors, and testing teams to ensure successful solution delivery and release readiness.
  • The ideal candidate is a highly skilled and versatile professional with strong expertise in manual and automated testing, test strategy development, regression suite optimization, defect management, business process analysis, and requirements management. This role requires the ability to operate both strategically and hands-on, shifting between UAT leadership responsibilities and Business Analyst functions based on project and operational needs.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Participate in Joint Application Requirements (JAR) and Joint Application Design (JAD) sessions for assigned Change Requests (CRs) and Maintenance & Operations (M&O) initiatives to support requirements gathering, solution validation, and testing readiness.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), Business System Owners (BSOs), vendors, technical teams, and project managers to analyze, document, refine, and validate business and functional requirements.
  • Serve as an individual contributor performing both Business Analyst and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) responsibilities based on project, operational, and organizational needs.
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive UAT strategies, test plans, test scenarios, and testing approaches aligned with business objectives, operational priorities, regulatory requirements, and project timelines.
  • Review business requirements, functional specifications, system designs, interface documentation, and business workflows to ensure complete and risk-based test coverage.
  • Create, execute, and maintain manual and automated test scripts for functional, integration, regression, end-to-end, data validation, and user acceptance testing activities.
  • Lead and coordinate UAT activities across assigned projects, including test execution, issue tracking, test evidence documentation, business validation, and release readiness support.
  • Partner with vendors responsible for Unit Testing and System Integration Testing (SIT) to improve testing alignment, strengthen overall quality coverage, and reduce duplicate testing efforts between SIT and UAT processes.
  • Collaborate with project managers, testing teams, business users, and external partners to manage testing timelines, dependencies, risks, deliverables, and implementation of readiness activities.
  • Facilitate requirements of walkthroughs, knowledge-sharing sessions, and testing reviews to ensure a clear understanding of business expectations, system functionality, and testing objectives.
  • Manage the full defect lifecycle including defect identification, logging, triage, prioritization, escalation, retesting, resolution validation, and status reporting utilizing approved enterprise testing and defect management tools.
  • Track, analyze, and communicate testing metrics, execution progress, defect trends, test coverage, quality risks, and UAT results to leadership, stakeholders, and project teams.
  • Analyze, review, refine, and enhance existing regression test suites to improve testing efficiency, business-process validation, and overall regression coverage across CAPS systems.
  • Lead test automation initiatives by developing automation strategies, identifying automation opportunities, recommending appropriate frameworks and tools, and implementing automated regression testing solutions to reduce manual testing effort and improve quality outcomes.
  • Support post-implementation validation, production issue analysis, continuous process improvement initiatives, QA/UAT best practices, and additional CAPS Program Administration activities as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, Engineering, Mathematics, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in Quality Assurance (QA), User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and/or Business Analysis roles supporting enterprise systems.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in test automation, including automation strategy development and transitioning manual testing processes into automated solutions.
  • Strong experience developing test strategies, test cases, test scripts, and executing functional, regression, integration, end-to-end, and UAT testing.
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing business and functional requirements, developing use cases, and translating business needs into testable scenarios.
  • Experience in performing data quality validation, data reconciliation, and testing across enterprise applications, interfaces, and reporting solutions.
  • Hands-on experience with QA and test management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Smartsheet, or similar platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with automation tools such as Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, TestComplete, Power Automate, UFT, or similar technologies.
  • Experience working with Microsoft reporting and analytics tools including Power BI and/or Microsoft Fabric.
  • Proven ability to work independently as a senior-level individual contributor while effectively collaborating with business users, internal teams, external partners, and vendors in a cross-functional environment.

Preferred:

  • Experience working with data systems and automated business processes.
  • Experience creating or using systems for automated testing.
  • Experience organizing and analyzing data to inform decision making.
  • Knowledge of Georgia Gateway Integrated Eligibility System.
  • Knowledge of system development and configuration.
  • Advanced skills in Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies
  • Familiarity with data warehousing, ETL processes, or data pipelines

Technical Competencies:

  • Knowledge of eligibility requirements and systems.
  • Understanding of automation processes and business needs.
  • Deep understanding of test types such as black box, regression, and negative testing.
  • Experience with testing frameworks and tools (Selenium, Power Automate, jUnit, Azure Test Plans).
  • Ability to deliver high-quality customer service and maintain positive work relationships.
  • Ability to organize and evaluate data to drive decision making.
  • Ability to collaborate with diverse communities and demonstrate cultural sensitivity.
  • Understanding of eligibility systems and requirements.
  • Experience with .NET applications, Angular front-ends, and relational databases.
  • Intermediate to advanced skills in Microsoft Word, Excel, and SharePoint.
  • Ability to develop user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Effective communication, collaboration, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to collaborate with diverse communities and maintain positive work relationships.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management
  • Ability to translate business requirements into technical test artifacts.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Physical Requirements:

  • Office-based work with intermittent sitting, standing, and walking.
  • Ability to speak clearly and hear at a normal conversational level.
  • Visual acuity for data analysis and computer work.
  • Full range of hand and finger motion for data entry.

This outdoor, full-time, seasonal, skiing/riding position will help provide the highest level of operations for winter training and events. Seeking active, rugged, personable individuals, who have a strong work ethic and love being outdoors in a high alpine winter environment. This opportunity includes pre-event preparation work, event operations, construction, and disassembly of venues. Candidates will help implement major races, competitions, events, and training providing world-class venues and operations.   • Add value to Copper Mountain and its Resort partners.

  • Ability to work long hours, most of it spent outdoors in a high alpine environment.

  • Be forward thinking, efficient, punctual and follow the plan when involved in operations. Ensure our team is creating the best events possible.

  • Maintain a professional profile with event officials, employees, and competition guests. Handle all inquiries and complaints in a professional and competent manner with a solution-based approach.

  • Demonstrate problem solving with a professional demeanor when under pressure.

  • Supports Managers and Supervisors with goals and objectives.

Risk Management:

  • Follow all Corporate and Department SOP’s. View the work environment in a way to ensure the safety of our staff and competition guests. Completely know and follow company policies and procedures.

Other Duties as Assigned:

  • This job description is an overview of the scope of responsibilities for this job and is not intended to be an inclusive list of job tasks and expectations. With the evolution of POWDR-Copper, the responsibilities of this position may change. The applicant must be prepared to accept new responsibilities and transfer others.

  • Functions as an ambassador of Copper Mountain, modeling and sharing the Copper "culture" with our guests and employees. Uphold the most professional image. Continually strives to exceed our guest's expectations and create memories for our guests and staff.

  • Ability to independently lead a small part of the crew to complete a task.

  • Career and goal oriented.

  • Team player, able to work productively in a team environment.

  • Is honest and has the highest integrity.

  • Can handle confidential information.

  • Displays excellent communication skills.

  • Expects and produces quality work and develops creative, positive ideas and suggestions for the department.

  • Always operates in the best interest of the department and resort guests. Takes time to understand general guest issues, questions, and problems.

  • Follows established policies and procedures. Is supportive of Company Core Values. Sets the example for others.

  • Is organized in tasks. Sees projects through to the finish.

  • Makes it a habit of responding to people as soon as possible.

  • Can handle fast-paced, potentially high-pressure environment.

  • Is flexible with hours and days of work. Can work any hours of the day, days of the week, including holidays. (There will be some OT during major events.)

  • Works well with little supervision.

  • Able to separate business and personal life (professional boundaries)

Basic Requirements:

  • EXPERT skiing or riding skills with the ability to lift and ski / ride with an excess of 50 lbs.

  • EXPERT skiing or riding ability on all terrain, all conditions, and all locations on the mountain.

  • Proficient in the operations of snowmobiles, wheeled and tracked rangers and power equipment.

  • Must have the ability to work in an extreme high alpine winter environment (10,000’ – 13,000’) for 8+ hours.

title: Driver - CDL B
description:
POSITION SUMMARY: A Driver- CDL (B) is responsible for safely operating a collection truck, and providing prompt, courteous and complete waste removal services for customers. In addition, a Driver – CDL (B) is responsible for ensuring his or her vehicle is in compliance with the Company’s safety standards prior to operating the vehicle, ensures that all Company, state and federal regulations are adhered to at all times while operating the vehicle, and completes vehicle condition reports (“VCRs”) on a daily basis to ensure that any vehicle defects are repaired in a timely manner.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform complete pre- and post-operation inspection of the vehicle in accordance with Company policy to ensure tire pressure, fluid levels, safety equipment, gauges, and controls are in proper working order. Report any safety issues on standard reports.
  • Safely operate his or her heavy truck along his or her designated route and to the disposal site; read route sheet, follow map and service each customer as identified on the route sheet or as assigned by the dispatcher and/or supervisor.
  • Operate manual and/or automatic controls in accordance with Company safety policies and procedures to lift and load refuse, operate compactor and dispose of collected material at the designated facility.
  • Courteously interact with all customers, dispatchers and others on a daily basis to ensure all customer routes are serviced in a timely and professional manner.
  • Identify unsatisfactory waste containers and tag containers in accordance with applicable departmental procedures.
  • Continuously monitor waste for evidence of unacceptable waste.
  • Clean area around an accidental waste spill, ensuring adherence to all applicable safety standards and policies.
  • Continuously monitor the condition of the vehicle to ensure it is operationally ready at all times to minimize down time; clean waste from the packer blade and truck body (where appropriate) on each disposal trip.
  • Complete required route/productivity sheets, VCRs and other reports, as required.
  • Maintain adherence to required productivity standards for the department to ensure all customers are serviced in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Follow all required safety policies and procedures.
  • Actively participate in the Company’s ReSOP program.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

title: University & Careers Counselor
description:
About Canadian Academy:

Canadian Academy is a not-for-profit, secular, gender-inclusive international school located in Kobe, Japan’s seventh largest city. CA is accredited by CIS (Council of International Schools) and WASC (Western Association of Schools and Colleges), is an authorized three-programme International Baccalaureate World School, and is a member of TABS (The Association of Boarding Schools). While most of the 700 students at CA are day students, our campus is also home to a small High School boarding program with a current enrollment of 40 students in Grades 9-12.


Canadian Academy faculty and staff inspire minds and nurture compassion by providing a rich and engaging programme that develops students’ skills, promotes curiosity and love of learning, and prioritizes well-being. All students follow the International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP) in Grades 6-10, and most students pursue the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in Grades 11 & 12, although 10-20% each year opt for a more personalized pathway to graduation that includes a mix of DP and other courses and leads to a CA Diploma. Some of our areas of focus over the next few years will be to further develop our graduation pathways to better meet the needs of our diverse learners, and to ensure that students have access to a broader range of opportunities for career exploration.



Position Overview

This is a new role at Canadian Academy, created to strengthen the alignment between CA’s academic pathways and students’ post-secondary opportunities. The post-holder will report to the High School Principal and work closely with the Vice Principal, Learning Leaders (MYP and DP Coordinators), and schoolwide Director of Learning.


As CA expands its high school program beyond the traditional IB Diploma, this position will play a pivotal role in providing post-secondary guidance that reflects the diverse needs and aspirations of our students. Working in partnership with two High School Personal and Academic Counselors, the post-holder will ensure that every student has a clear, personalized, and well-supported route from high school to appropriate post-secondary destinations.


Core Responsibilities

University and Post-Secondary Counseling

  • Lead the university and careers counseling program for Grades 9–12, with direct responsibility for the application cycle in Grades 11–12.
  • Support students and families in exploring diverse global options, including universities in Japan, North America, the UK, Europe, Australia, and Asia.
  • Provide individualized guidance on future course of study, program choices, application strategies, and gap-year options, and other post-secondary opportunities.
  • Oversee standardized testing guidance (PSAT, SAT, ACT, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.).
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with university representatives and professional associations; host visits and represent CA at university fairs, conferences, and networks.
  • Curate and manage the school’s university counseling resources and communications, ensuring accurate, timely information for students, families, and faculty.
  • Support students and families in exploring a range of academic and other scholarship opportunities.
  • Work collaboratively with the Personal and Academic Counselors to ensure alignment between student choices, graduation requirements, and post-secondary goals.


Leadership and Collaboration

  • Serve as a member of the High School Leadership Team, contributing to school improvement planning, policy development, and communication around academic and counseling initiatives.
  • Work in close partnership with Counseling Team colleagues to ensure a holistic, integrated approach to student guidance and well-being.
  • Support faculty professional learning related to academic advising and post-secondary readiness.
  • Maintain accurate records of student applications, admissions outcomes, and matriculations, using data to improve programs and outcomes.
  • Strengthen community understanding of academic pathways, graduation requirements, and post-secondary outcomes through regular communication and workshops.


Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Education, Counseling, or a related field.
  • Professional certification or licensure in counseling or college advising preferred.
  • Minimum of five years of university admissions or counseling experience, ideally in an international or independent school context.
  • Deep understanding of university systems and admissions processes across multiple regions (Japan, North America, UK, Europe, Asia, Australia).
  • Experience with the International Baccalaureate (MYP and DP) and other high school programs.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and use data for program development and continuous improvement.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and family-engagement skills across diverse cultural contexts.
  • Proficiency in Japanese is desirable but not at all required for this role.


Desired Personal Attributes

  • Warm, approachable, and student-centered.
  • Culturally sensitive and globally minded communicator.
  • Strategic thinker who balances systems-level leadership with individualized support.
  • Collaborative and collegial team player who thrives in partnership with other counselors and academic leaders.
  • Highly organized, efficient, and detail-oriented, able to manage multiple priorities calmly and effectively.
  • Proactive, reflective, and committed to continuous professional learning and program improvement.


HOW TO APPLY


Interested candidates should prepare and upload an updated resume. In lieu of a cover letter, please submit a short video introduction (via an unlisted YouTube link) that covers:


  • A brief introduction of yourself
  • Why you’re interested in this role
  • Why you believe you’d be a good fit, based on your experience


Please share your video link on Bamboo in the “Website, Blog or Portfolio” field.

title: Product Manager - PEAK Learning Platform
description:
Help Build Canada’s Next Generation Personalized Learning Platform

Every learner deserves individualized support that helps them reach their full potential. At Learn. Develop. Succeed., we are building PEAK, an AI-enabled platform that enables educators to deliver more personalized, effective, and scalable learning. By combining AI, workflow automation, and data-informed insights, PEAK enhances the human relationships at the heart of exceptional education. Learn. Develop. Succeed. is one of British Columbia’s fastest-growing education nonprofits, supporting more than 1,250 learners annually. Through RISE Next Generation, we aim to expand that impact to more than 10,000 learners annually within five years and ultimately more than 100,000 learners across Canada. We are looking for an exceptional Product Manager who wants to help build a category-defining platform with meaningful social impact.


About PEAK

PEAK is a custom-built operational and learning platform that supports every stage of the learner journey, including:

  • learner admissions and onboarding
  • learner assessments
  • individualized learning plans
  • instructor workflows
  • scheduling and operations
  • family communication
  • learner progress monitoring
  • AI-assisted educational support



Why This Role Is Unique

This is an opportunity to help define the future of individualized learning in Canada. You will help build one of Canada's most ambitious education technology platforms while working directly with educators, researchers, software engineers, and organizational leaders. This is a highly unique opportunity to build, test, innovate and see the impact of your work. Your work will directly influence how individualized learning is delivered across Canada and help shape a platform with national impact.


Why You Will Love This Role

Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to innovation, impact, and inclusion. You will have the opportunity to:

  • Build a product with meaningful social impact
  • Help define the long-term vision of PEAK
  • Work alongside a growing team of software engineers
  • Apply AI to improve educational outcomes
  • Influence product strategy from discovery through delivery
  • Build a platform from the ground up
  • Work directly with end users every week
  • Join one of Canada's fastest-growing education nonprofits


Purpose of the Position

The Product Manager serves as the bridge between educators, operational teams, software engineers, and organizational leadership. You will lead product discovery, roadmap development, prioritization, release planning, and continuous improvement while ensuring every investment in PEAK creates measurable value for learners, educators, and the organization.


Working closely with the Senior Manager, Technology, developers, operational leaders, and frontline educators and admissions team, the Product Manager will translate organizational needs into clear product direction, guide prioritization and planning, coordinate implementation and rollout, and lead the measurement of whether new features achieve their intended value.


This is not solely a project management role. The Product Manager will be responsible for helping ensure that PEAK remains coherent, useful, scalable, and closely connected to both our mission and organizational workflows. The successful candidate will be an exceptional communicator and systems thinker who can navigate ambiguity, build trust across technical and non-technical teams, and balance immediate operational needs with long-term product direction.


The Product Manager will also have an understanding the landscape of competing and complementary products in the market, defining our position, and identifying opportunities to partner.


Success in Your First Year You will know you are succeeding when you have:

  • Built trusted relationships across the organization
  • Established a structured product discovery process
  • Created a prioritized product roadmap
  • Improved communication between operational teams and developers
  • Successfully launched multiple major PEAK releases
  • Introduced measurable product metrics
  • Increased user adoption and satisfaction
  • Helped define the long-term vision of PEAK

Principal Roles and Responsibilities

Product Discovery and Requirements Development

  • Act as the primary bridge between operational teams, program teams, organizational leadership, and PEAK development.
  • Gather and document workflows, user needs, operational pain points, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Distinguish root operational problems from isolated feature requests or proposed solutions.
  • Translate complex needs into clear product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process maps, and implementation guidance.
  • Facilitate discovery conversations, workshops, interviews, and feedback sessions with staff and other users.
  • Continuously validate assumptions through user interviews, observation, experimentation, and data.


Product Strategy and Ecosystem Stewardship

  • Develop and continuously refine the PEAK product vision.
  • Develop and maintain a deep understanding of PEAK’s current capabilities, operational workflows, active development streams, technical dependencies, and future opportunities.
  • Define measurable product outcomes
  • Help leadership assess the operational value, organizational impact, complexity, urgency, and cost-benefit of potential initiatives.
  • Ensure that individual features contribute to a coherent and sustainable platform rather than a collection of disconnected solutions.
  • Balance short-term operational priorities with longer-term platform scalability, maintainability, and user experience.


Planning, Prioritization, and Roadmap Management

  • Organize, maintain, and refine the product backlog in collaboration with technical leadership.
  • Consolidate requests from across the organization into clear, structured product initiatives.
  • Evaluate and prioritize work based on user impact, organizational value, urgency, effort, technical dependencies, risk, and strategic alignment.
  • Break large concepts into manageable phases, releases, and minimum viable product requirements.
  • Coordinate roadmap priorities with organizational leadership and development team capacity.
  • Support release planning, sequencing, sprint preparation, and longer-term product planning.


Development Coordination and Execution

  • Provide ongoing coordination among developers, operational stakeholders, and organizational leaders throughout implementation.
  • Ensure that developers have timely access to the context, decisions, information, and user input required to move work forward.
  • Identify blockers, unresolved questions, scope concerns, and potential misalignment early.
  • Monitor whether development remains aligned with approved requirements and intended outcomes.
  • Support decisions when requirements need to be clarified, adjusted, or reduced during implementation.
  • Maintain visibility into development progress and communicate relevant updates to stakeholders.
  • Foster efficient communications across Teams, Github, email, and other collaboration tools.


Testing, Rollout, and Adoption

  • Coordinate user acceptance testing and structured feedback collection before releases.
  • Develop testing plans, scenarios, success criteria, and processes for documenting feedback.
  • Work with developers and stakeholders to assess and prioritize issues identified through testing.
  • Ensure operational teams are informed and prepared before significant product or workflow changes.
  • Coordinate rollout plans, release communications, documentation, training materials, and adoption support.
  • Monitor early adoption and help resolve issues that arise following release.


Product Measurement and Continuous Improvement

  • Establish feedback and evaluation processes following product releases.
  • Define key product metrics including user adoption, engagement, workflow efficiency, satisfaction, and educational outcomes.
  • Define measurable indicators of success for significant features and initiatives.
  • Assess whether product changes have improved workflows, reduced staff time, increased consistency, enhanced service quality, or achieved other intended outcomes.
  • Monitor whether features are being used as intended and identify barriers to adoption.
  • Use evidence, feedback, and product data to inform future prioritization and improvements.
  • Help shift the organization’s focus from completing implementation to achieving meaningful and measurable impact.


Communication and Organizational Alignment

  • Translate effectively between technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Provide clear, concise updates about product priorities, decisions, timelines, dependencies, and risks.
  • Build trusted relationships with developers, frontline staff, managers, leadership, and other stakeholders.
  • Facilitate productive conversations when stakeholders have competing needs or expectations.
  • Contribute to a collaborative, respectful, neuroaffirming, and learning-oriented workplace culture.
  • Tasks outside those explicitly outlined may be expected during periods of increased organizational need.


Competencies

  • Exceptional product planning, prioritization, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong strategic thinker that can also own operational details; has the ability to understand how workflows, features, teams, and organizational priorities interconnect.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate between technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Strong judgment and comfort making recommendations in ambiguous or evolving situations.
  • Ability to distinguish high-impact needs from lower-priority requests.
  • Thoughtful, structured, and user-centred approach to problem-solving.
  • Genuine empathy for frontline staff and the day-to-day realities of operational and program teams.
  • Strong relationship-building, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Clear sense of ownership and pride in delivering excellent work.
  • Strong product judgment and customer empathy
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution
  • Outcome-oriented product mindset
  • Alignment with LDS’ mission, values, and commitment to inclusion.


Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced university degree in product management, business, technology, education, design, information systems, or another relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 5-8+ years of directly related product management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience managing or contributing to the development of complex software products or digital platforms.
  • Experience conducting product discovery, gathering requirements, developing user stories, and managing product backlogs.
  • Experience working closely with software developers including those using AI-enabled and agentic coding, technical leaders, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience prioritizing competing needs and making clear product trade-offs.
  • Experience coordinating testing, product releases, rollout communications, and user adoption.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with excellent attention to detail.
  • Ability to thrive when managing multiple priorities, deadlines, and evolving requirements.
  • Exceptional ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
  • Sufficient technical fluency to communicate effectively with developers and understand software constraints, dependencies, and development processes.
  • Eligibility to work in Canada.
  • Ability to complete a criminal record check with vulnerable sector screening.


Considered Assets

  • Experience working in education, educational technology, nonprofit organizations, or another mission-driven environment.
  • Experience with AI-enabled products, workflow automation, data-informed tools, or custom organizational software.
  • Experience with accessibility, inclusive design, universal design, or neuroaffirming practices.
  • Experience supporting organizational change and the adoption of new technology.
  • Experience working with platforms such as GitHub, Jira, Azure DevOps, Linear, Asana, or similar product and development tools.
  • Experience working in an Agile or iterative software development environment.
  • Product management, Agile, Scrum, or PMP certification.
  • Familiarity with user experience research, service design, business analysis, or process improvement.


Start date: September 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter


Reports to: Executive Director


Hours of work: 40 working hours per week, Monday to Friday

  • Approximate schedule from 8:30am to 5:00pm Pacific time  Ability to work flexible hours including occasional evenings or weekends


What We Offer

  • Salary range: $75,000 - $110,000 per year, commensurate with experience and a forty (40) hour work week. While our compensation may differ from that offered by larger technology companies, this role provides exceptional opportunity to build a nationally significant product with meaningful ownership and lasting social impact. The top of the pay range is for a successful candidate who is a product manager expert with a combination of experience and competencies to perform these job duties at an expert level.
  • Opportunities for team-wide and individual professional learning throughout the year
  • Inclusive culture and innovative workplace with opportunity for new approaches and growth
  • Neuroaffirming and inclusive workplace
  • Financial support for relocation available.
  • Paid vacation commensurate with experience (starting at 5-6%), plus paid office closure from December 25 - Jan 1 each year, which does not count toward your vacation entitlement
  • Benefits entitlement after three months, which includes Extended Health and Dental, and Travel as well as AD&D, CI, LTD and life insurance
  • $1,000 RRSP contribution (2026). For reference, our organization is currently researching whether and how we may participate in retirement savings/pension plan options. Updates on this may be offered during the interview process.
  • On-site vehicle and bicycle parking and on major SkyTrain and bus routes

Learn. Develop. Succeed. Is proud to be a certified Living Wage employer!


Location: Vancouver Learning Centre – 3292 East Broadway, Vancouver, BC, hybrid work from home on scheduled day(s) available after the probationary period.


Job Type: Full-time, permanent


Equity: We are committed to employment equity and believe that a workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve strengthens our ability to achieve our mission. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ethnic and cultural backgrounds, sexual orientations, abilities, and a range of life experiences to apply. To complete your application, you will need to, on our system:

  • Upload a resume and cover letter about your experience.


Expectations & Working Conditions

  • Position will involve long periods of sitting and using office equipment  Frequent interruptions from team members/donors depending on working location  Depending on time of day, working location may be loud and busy


Every year, thousands of learners never receive the individualized support they need to realize their full potential. We believe technology can change that. If you are excited by the opportunity to build an exceptional product that combines AI, education, and human-centred design to improve lives across Canada, we would love to hear from you. Thank you to all applicants for your interest.


Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and early applications are encouraged.

title: Principal Rail Corridor Access Engineer
description:
At UGL Transport, we deliver critical infrastructure and essential services that help connect communities and support the environment in which we live. Our capabilities span whole-of-life transport solutions, underpinned by innovative, sustainable technologies and strong partnerships with government, industry, and community stakeholders.

Part of the UGL Group, UGL Regional Linx (UGLRL) manages the NSW Country Regional Network (CRN), ensuring the safe and reliable movement of people and goods throughout regional New South Wales. Headquartered in Orange, NSW, with depots across the state, we are proud that more than 85% of our workforce is based in regional communities.

At UGLRL, we believe that diverse teams create better outcomes. We foster a workplace where people feel valued, supported and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Whether you're advancing your career in rail or bringing experience from another infrastructure sector, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role
As Principal Rail Corridor Access Engineer, you will provide technical leadership across corridor access engineering activities, supporting projects and developments that interact with the CRN network.

This is an influential role where you will work collaboratively with engineers, planners, government agencies, developers, local councils, and industry partners to ensure safe, practical, and sustainable outcomes for the network and the communities it serves.

You will lead a team of specialists, guide technical decision-making, and help shape the future of corridor access processes while supporting the continued growth and development of your team.

What You'll Be Doing
Lead and support the Corridor Access team to deliver consistent, high-quality engineering outcomes.
Provide technical leadership and assurance for third-party works, development applications, corridor access proposals, property activities, and related projects.
Review engineering proposals against CRN standards and asset management principles, applying sound judgement to identify and manage safety and operational risks.
Coordinate multidisciplinary assessments involving track, civil, structural, signalling, telecommunications, geotechnical, maintenance, and operational stakeholders.
Oversee Heavy Vehicle application assessments with the support of the Heavy Vehicle Coordinator and Structures Engineer.
Collaborate with applicants, designers, utilities, councils, and internal stakeholders to resolve technical challenges and develop practical, safe solutions.
Provide clear engineering advice and recommendations that support informed decision-making.
Mentor and develop team members through coaching, knowledge sharing, and capability-building initiatives.
Champion continuous improvement across systems, processes, templates, and engineering practices.
Identify opportunities to improve efficiency while maintaining safety, compliance, and asset integrity.

About You
We're looking for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, working collaboratively, and supporting the development of people and processes.
You may have experience in rail, transport, civil infrastructure, construction, utilities, or a related industry and bring\:
A tertiary qualification in Engineering (Civil Engineering preferred).
Strong technical and engineering assessment skills.
The ability to build positive relationships with a broad range of stakeholders.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Experience coordinating or influencing multidisciplinary teams.
A collaborative mindset and a commitment to safe, sustainable outcomes.
Strong organisational, systems, and reporting capabilities.

Why Join UGL Regional Linx?
Play a key role in maintaining and improving critical regional infrastructure.
Work with experienced and supportive technical professionals.
Lead meaningful projects that benefit regional communities.
Enjoy opportunities for professional development, mentoring, and career growth.
Contribute to an inclusive culture where different experiences and perspectives are valued.
Be part of an organisation committed to safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Diversity & Inclusion
At UGLRL, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome applications from women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, mature-age workers, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Research shows that many people, particularly women, may only apply when they feel they meet every requirement. If this role excites you and you believe you have the capabilities to succeed, we encourage you to apply, even if your experience doesn't perfectly match every qualification listed.

Our recruitment process includes relevant screening checks, including a national criminal history check and pre-employment medical assessment, which includes drug and alcohol screening.

title: Driver CDL B
description:
POSITION SUMMARY: A Driver- CDL (B) is responsible for safely operating a collection truck, and providing prompt, courteous and complete waste removal services for customers. In addition, a Driver – CDL (B) is responsible for ensuring his or her vehicle is in compliance with the Company’s safety standards prior to operating the vehicle, ensures that all Company, state and federal regulations are adhered to at all times while operating the vehicle, and completes vehicle condition reports (“VCRs”) on a daily basis to ensure that any vehicle defects are repaired in a timely manner.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform complete pre- and post-operation inspection of the vehicle in accordance with Company policy to ensure tire pressure, fluid levels, safety equipment, gauges, and controls are in proper working order. Report any safety issues on standard reports.
  • Safely operate his or her heavy truck along his or her designated route and to the disposal site; read route sheet, follow map and service each customer as identified on the route sheet or as assigned by the dispatcher and/or supervisor.
  • Operate manual and/or automatic controls in accordance with Company safety policies and procedures to lift and load refuse, operate compactor and dispose of collected material at the designated facility.
  • Courteously interact with all customers, dispatchers and others on a daily basis to ensure all customer routes are serviced in a timely and professional manner.
  • Identify unsatisfactory waste containers and tag containers in accordance with applicable departmental procedures.
  • Continuously monitor waste for evidence of unacceptable waste.
  • Clean area around an accidental waste spill, ensuring adherence to all applicable safety standards and policies.
  • Continuously monitor the condition of the vehicle to ensure it is operationally ready at all times to minimize down time; clean waste from the packer blade and truck body (where appropriate) on each disposal trip.
  • Complete required route/productivity sheets, VCRs and other reports, as required.
  • Maintain adherence to required productivity standards for the department to ensure all customers are serviced in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Follow all required safety policies and procedures.
  • Actively participate in the Company’s ReSOP program.
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
  • Good customer services skills to meet and exceed customer expectations; acts in a professional, courteous and cooperative manner toward customers and co-workers; works with a sense of honesty and trustworthiness.
  • Good time management skills to ensure assigned responsibilities are completed in an efficient and safe manner.
  • Good follow through ability; adheres to work schedule and follows through on challenges as they arise.
  • Ability to adhere to Company policies and rules set forth; promotes the Company’s safety standards; does not take inappropriate risks.
  • Maintains a feeling of pride in work; strives to achieve all goals.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • Class B or higher Commercial Driver’s license with air brakes endorsement.

PAY RATE: $35.15

Rewarding Compensation and Benefits

EEO STATEMENT:Republic Services is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, relationship or association with a protected veteran (spouses or other family members), genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).


RECENT RECOGNITION

  • Barron’s 100 Most Sustainable Companies
  • CDP Discloser
  • Dow Jones Best-In-Class Indices
  • Ethisphere’s World’s Most Ethical Companies
  • Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies
  • Great Place to Work
  • Sustainability Yearbook S&P Global

title: Principal Equipment Engineer
description:
Job Summary:

Equipment Engineer provides continuous support to production of our unique 3D cell architecture by ensuring optimum equipment utilization through immediate equipment repair, problem solving and design improvement to minimize equipment downtime and practice collaboration with cross-functional group including sub-contractors. He / She may supervise and lead equipment technicians in the repair, troubleshooting, upgrade/conversion, qualification, and preventive maintenance of equipment.

Responsibilities:

  • Support 24/7 production scale up and escalation for critical/major repair of manufacturing equipment according to established procedure and parameter settings in the shortest possible time.
  • Drives analysis and debug of equipment availability/uptime, hardware and instruments preventive maintenance and repair data thru MTBF, MTBA and MTTR.
  • Interfaces with various suppliers to optimize machine design/performance and other ENOVIX site to acquire the needed resources and technical support.
  • Strong knowledge in electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, motion and temperature controllers will be added advantage.
  • Conducts and initiates spare parts review and cost saving initiatives without sacrificing maintenance, quality and equipment up time.
  • Actively involved in the review of new equipment design, hardware and instruments purchases. Perform machine buyoff at supplier site and in house machine commissioning.
  • Coordinates with other departments in the implementation of new manufacturing process and procedures
  • Reviews and controls the purchase of spare parts to be put on stock to prevent excessive inventory and to ensure its availability during equipment breakdown.

title: Safety Supervisor
description:
The Safety Supervisor is responsible for safety training, acting as a resource for risk assessments and management, permits, plans, and leads a safe work environment for all employees. This person will be the main safety point of contact for PNE’s Electrical division-comprised of AET and Taurus.

Pacific Northern Environmental, LLC consists of five divisions including Advanced Electrical Technologies (AET), Taurus Power and Controls (Taurus), Cowlitz Clean Sweep (CCS), Pacific Northern Environmental Construction (PNEC), and WasteXpress Environmental (WXE). Together, we specialize in commercial and petroleum construction, industrial and commercial electrical, industrial cleaning, and hazardous waste disposal. PNE LLC is a multi-state organization with operating offices in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Hawaii. In addition, we carry out projects across the United States.

PNE is “All About Solutions” for our employees, customers, and our communities through trust, honesty, accountability, family, and safety 24/7. While each staff member has clear responsibilities in fulfilling our core purpose, we promote and reward a business culture and work ethic where no task is above or below any individual.

Education and Experience Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Construction Management, or a related field (preferred), equivalent field experience considered in lieu of.
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in safety management within construction, industrial, or environmental sectors.
  • Professional safety certification(s) such as CSP, ASP, or CHST (preferred or ability to obtain).
  • OSHA Train the Trainer certification(s) (preferred)
  • In-depth knowledge of OSHA, WISHA, EPA, MSHA, and other relevant regulatory standards.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills; capable of engaging with personnel from field employees to senior leadership.
  • MSHA instructor certification (preferred)

  • Overnight travel required (when directed).
  • Driver’s license required and must meet eligibility requirements to be covered under the company’s vehicle insurance policy.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Safety Supervisor possessing the education and experience listed above performs the following:

  • Plans and attends monthly safety meetings at all assigned divisions.
  • Strong communication with Division Managers to discuss current jobs, conduct safety audits on said locations.
  • Safely operate and maintain company vehicles as required for job duties, ensuring compliance with all traffic laws and company policies
  • Complete site audits with remarks and findings, communicate these to the appropriate parties.
  • Complete inspections involving work sites and other related equipment.
  • Develop Health and Safety Plans for various projects.
  • Mill shutdown coordinator, including employee count, night shift-safety meetings, equipment selection, job walks, etc.

  • Move about the jobsite as needed.
  • Move work related equipment up to 50lbs.
  • Remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.
  • Operate various technological devices, including but not limited to a computer.
