title: Director of Fleet and Compliance
description:
2626 W Beryl Ave Phoenix Arizona, 85021,

Position Description:


Manages the Fleet to include overseeing maintenance of all vehicles, industrial machinery and associated equipment. Provides guidance to the Transportation Department in Driver Training, Safety and onboarding for Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona (GCNA) and its affiliated entities. Ensures that all Team Members and the department are aware of Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) guidelines and ensures GCNA stays in compliance. Maintains the required Driver Qualification (DQ) files in accordance with government regulations. Ensures new hire drivers are vetted per current DOT and FMSCA rules. Coordinates the orientation and training process for new or promoted Fleet Drivers. Manages the FMSCA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse process as well as the DOT random drug tests. Collaborates with Safety and Risk Management regarding DOT requirements and changing regulations.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Executes plan to ensure drivers are trained in safe operation of vehicles.

  • Proactively promotes a culture of safety to prevent accidents and injuries.

  • Ensures timely accident/incident investigations that involve property, equipment, and/or personnel.

  • Develops safety strategies in partnership with Safety, Risk, and Asset Protection.

  • Oversees the Driver Safety Committee, including facilitation of safety meetings and/or safety related classes.

  • Provides driver safety training to the Transportation Department. Coordinates with Director of Transportation, ROC VP, and other departmental Senior Managers, Directors, and VPs to analyze, identify, and execute strategic goals and objectives regarding safety, training and driver retention.

  • Oversees and manages all aspects of the organization’s vehicle and industrial machinery fleet.

  • Oversees and manages leased fleet vehicle accounts for vehicle returns, allocation and billing in conjunction with Finance.

  • Maintains all licensing, registration, insurance, emissions, and government permits on all vehicles in the GCNA fleet. Processes registration renewal/original titles at DMV and ensures each vehicle or individual has the appropriate insurance cards and are reported to the broker.

  • Oversees internal and external requests for service and forwards to applicable vendor for timely processing of vehicle transportation, repairs and maintenance.

  • Ensures preventative maintenance schedules for mechanical equipment is in place and followed per GCNA standards

  • Ensures that Team Members comply with all policies and procedures relating to Security, Health, and Safety; influences any changes necessary to meet statutory requirements, ensuring minimum risk to Team Members and the business.

  • Ensures all DOT reporting requirements are accurate and up to date.

  • Schedules and administers any testing or training for Team Members, as needed.

  • Investigates, addresses, and documents all safety violations; administers re-training if necessary.

  • Responsible for performance management (coaching, discipline, performance improvement plans, and annual reviews), staffing, compensation, and development of Team Members.

  • Ensures that leadership effectively manages performance of Team Members, discussing performance problems with Senior Leadership and HR Business Partner (HRBP) to identify causes and issues in order to work on resolving problems.

  • Models Goodwill Core Values – Trust, Collaboration, Engagement, Ownership, and Innovation.

  • Plays critical role in driving company safety culture change efforts and change management processes.

  • Focuses on the driver experience and assists transportation as needed for retention.

  • Coordinates efforts with various Goodwill divisions, as needed.

  • Performs other related duties, as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications (Education, Experience, Skills):

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience preferred.

  • Must have experience in development and growth of Team Members.

  • 7+ years supervisory experience in the transportation industry.

  • Familiar with FMCSA, OSHA, and DOT rules and regulations.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.

  • Valid driver’s license with clean MVR.

  • Ability to pass a background check and drug screen, where applicable for position.

  • Ability to speak and read English proficiently

You will be eligible for a comprehensive Total Rewards package, 1st of the month following 60 days of employment that includes the following:

  • 3 Medical Plans.
  • Employer Funded Health Reimbursement Account (HRA).
  • 3 Dental Plans.
  • Vision Plan.
  • 401K Traditional and Roth Plans.
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
  • Paid Time Off; Sick and Vacation.
  • Paid Holidays.

These are just a few highlights of our key benefit offerings!


Become a valued member of an organization where good work meets community impact. Our mission is: Empowering Individuals, Strengthening Families, and Building Stronger Communities. Goodwill provides no-cost career development, training, and education services to help individuals build a better life for themselves and their families. Our core values are Trust, Collaboration, Engagement, Ownership, and Innovation. Everything we accomplish as a team is centered around these core values. Together, we create an inclusive and welcoming environment for each other. With stores conveniently located near you, you can work for a company where team strength and success are valued and encouraged. Join our team and gain opportunities for job growth at Goodwill and beyond.


Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified individuals seeking employment are considered without regard to race (including traits associated with race, e.g., hairstyles), color, religion, sex (including pregnancy and related conditions, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, disability, military status, age, genetic information, or any other category protected by applicable federal, state and local fair employment practice laws.


Individuals with a disability may be entitled to a reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act and/or state or local laws. Please contact Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona at 1-833-624-0920 option 6 or leaves@goodwillaz.org if you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act.

For questions about your application or employment with Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona, please contact our Candidate Support Line at 1-833-624-0920, option 5.


PHISHING SCAM WARNING: Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona/Goodwill Industries of Monocacy Valley, Inc. (“GCNA/GIMV”) are among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. The imposters are creating misleading email accounts, conducting remote “interviews,” and making artificial job offers in order to collect personal and financial information from unsuspecting individuals. Please note that GCNA/GIMV only use company email addresses, which contain “@goodwillaz.org” or @gimv.org”, to communicate with candidates via email. location: FL - Orlando - Universal Stella Nova Resort

title: Chief People Officer
description:
Finora Bank is a specialized bank dedicated to accelerating growth for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises, and entrepreneurs. Licensed by the European Central Bank (ECB), Finora Bank offers innovative financial solutions, including loans, leasing, factoring, and guarantees, to help businesses achieve their full potential.


Based in Vilnius and Tallinn, Finora Bank has a team of 70+ professionals with extensive international experience in banking.


Join the journey of building a fast-growing bank!


CHIEF PEOPLE OFFICER (CPO)


Fixed-term maternity leave cover


Position Purpose


We are looking for an experienced, commercially minded, and pragmatic Chief People Officer to lead Finora Bank’s people agenda and oversee its HR and Administration functions across Lithuania and Estonia.

This is a senior strategic role with substantial personal execution. The CPO should be as comfortable making organization-level decisions as completing the detailed work required to implement them.

You will lead the HR and Administration team and work closely with senior leadership and the Head of Administration and the Chair of the Supervisory Board on key people and organizational matters.

The position is primarily office-based in Vilnius, with responsibility across Lithuania and Estonia.


What will you be doing?


People Strategy, Organization and Change


  • Lead the Bank’s people strategy in line with business priorities, financial objectives, and regulatory requirements.
  • Advise senior leaders on organization design, workforce planning, leadership, talent, and people-related risks.
  • Lead organizational changes, restructurings, role redesign, underperformance cases, and other complex employee matters with sound judgment and legal compliance.
  • Identify critical roles, capability gaps, succession needs, and key-person dependencies.


Performance, Leadership and Remuneration


  • Own the Bank’s performance management cycle, including KPIs, reviews, calibration, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Support managers in setting expectations, managing performance, and strengthening accountability.
  • Drive leadership development, succession planning, and targeted capability-building initiatives.
  • Maintain remuneration, bonus, benefits, and recognition principles that balance fairness, competitiveness, performance, and affordability.


Recruitment, Culture and Employee Experience


  • Personally lead the full recruitment process, including sourcing, screening, interviews, candidate assessment, selection decisions, and offers.
  • Oversee employment documentation, onboarding, probation, internal mobility, and offboarding processes delivered by the HR Specialist.
  • Use employee feedback, engagement surveys, and HR data to identify issues and turn findings into practical actions.
  • Strengthen an accountable and resilient culture and lead internal communication on people matters.


Labour Law, Governance and Daily Operations


  • Own and continuously improve the Bank’s HR policies, methodologies, and people-governance framework.
  • Ensure legally sound decisions and documentation across employment, performance, disciplinary, restructuring, and termination matters.
  • Manage people-related risks and maintain audit and regulatory readiness.
  • Oversee employee documentation, employee records, payroll inputs, HR systems, and employee lifecycle processes, ensuring accurate and timely delivery by the HR team.


Administration and Office Management


  • Lead and coordinate the HR and Administration team, including the HR Specialist and Office Managers.
  • Own the Administration function and its budget, approve expenditures, and ensure the responsible use of organizational resources.
  • Oversee office operations, capacity and space requirements, facilities, procurement, vendors, administrative contracts, company vehicles, and other office-related services.
  • Set priorities and provide direction to Office Managers while ensuring that day-to-day administrative work is delivered effectively.


What will help you succeed?


  • Proven senior HR leadership experience, ideally in banking, fintech, or another regulated environment.
  • Experience managing a broad people agenda across both strategic and operational HR.
  • Expert-level practical knowledge of Lithuanian labour law, HR governance, and policy development.
  • Strong judgment and decisiveness when managing complex and sensitive employee matters.
  • Experience leading HR and Administration teams and overseeing office operations, budgets, vendors, contracts, and administrative projects.
  • Experience working effectively with executive and supervisory-level stakeholders.
  • Strong business and financial understanding and the confidence to challenge constructively.
  • High ownership, integrity, discretion, resilience, and attention to detail.
  • Fluent Lithuanian and English.


What do we offer?


  • A High-Impact Role: Lead both the people and administration agenda of an ECB-licensed bank and directly influence its structure, capability, working environment, and execution.

  • An Experienced, Professional Team: Work with a cross-border team of banking professionals in Vilnius and Tallinn.

  • Competitive Salary: 5619 – 8265 euros gross per month, depending on experience and competencies.

  • Health Benefits: Access additional health insurance after the probation period.

  • Additional Benefits: Enjoy extra days off based on tenure, a pet-friendly office, complimentary snacks, company events, and branded gifts.

For more information see in our Privacy Policy: https://finorabank.eu/en/privacy-policy/

title: Director of Development (Faculty of Engineering and Desautels Faculty of Management)
description:
Please refer to the How to Apply for a Job (for External Candidates) job aid for instructions on how to apply.

If you are an active McGill employee (ie: currently in an active contract or position at McGill University), do not apply through this Career Site. Login to your McGill Workday account and apply to this posting using the Find Jobs report (type Find Jobs in the search bar).

University Advancement (UA) promotes McGill to its global community and to the public, engaging alumni, volunteers and friends of the University, and building on McGill’s record of fundraising success in support of University priorities.

By joining UA, you can be part of a dynamic and exciting team of professionals that is making an extraordinary impact on the world by advancing the philanthropic and engagement ambitions of McGill University.

To find out more about UA, please visit us at .

Position Summary:

Working in close partnership with UA colleagues and Deans, the Director of Development will provide strategic development support in order further to enhance the fundraising capacity of the cohort to optimize short- and long-term philanthropic support to the University, for the Faculty of Engineering and the Desautels Faculty of Management. The Director will develop, implement and manage the overall fundraising strategy for their pool of prospects at a high level. The Director will work collaboratively with the Deans of the Faculties served by the cohort, faculty members, senior management and development colleagues at McGill to identify, cultivate, solicit and evaluate potential donors and will develop gift fundraising strategies and timetables to secure gifts and foster a continuing interest in the University.

Primary Responsibilities:

• Develop, implement and manage the overall fundraising strategy for the pool of prospects. Oversee the fundraising strategic plan in support of all the faculties of their cohorts.

• Develop complex major gift fundraising strategies and timetables, to secure gifts of $500,000 or more from top prospects in the portfolio.

• Work closely with Deans, Faculty members and senior management to plan, coordinate, manage, implement and evaluate fundraising projects to address their respective needs and priorities.

• Develop multidisciplinary initiatives within their cohort and across the cohorts.

• Work in close collaboration with the other Cohort leads on cross-Faculty fundraising projects.

• Lead the development and realization of the Faculty case for support by working closely with University Advancement and Faculty resources, in order to achieve goals and needs. Work closely with University Advancement Communications to ensure that messages and communications (case statements, proposals, bulleting, donor reports) are consistent with the University’s case for support and fundraising priorities.

• Lead strategic gift conversations with prospects at a high level, with a focus of over $500K.

• Manage a prospect portfolio (approx. 75) of donors of the highest capacity and carry out significant steps (moves) in accordance with a strategy designed to result in increased philanthropic support for the Cohort.

• Through personal visits, identify and qualify individuals to determine capacity, inclination and interests in providing major and principal gift support. Evaluate and recommend appropriate next steps for newly qualified potential donors and current donors.

• Provide counsel and guidance to Alumni Engagement Officers in the elaboration of strategic prospect engagement plans.

• Manage, integrate and lead volunteer strategy for the Cohort’s corresponding Faculties including the Faculty Advancement Council. Manage relationships with Faculty Advancement Council members.

• Participate in Prospect Management System; ensure relationships with prospects and donors are managed and recorded in timely and appropriate contact reports, recording of proposals, etc.

• Undertake special projects.

Other Qualifying Skills/Abilities:

The position requires an in-depth knowledge of fundraising best practices, in a metrics driven, team environment, and a strong track record of closing $500K+ gifts. A minimum of seven to ten years of direct fundraising experience preferred; experience working in education an asset. The candidate must be a results-driven, highly motivated fundraiser who can build a high level of trust in relationships, and influence others to reach ambitious objectives. They should have a leadership style characterized by coaching and engagement, while at the same time having a high degree of managerial courage and proactively dealing with challenging situations. Proven Discretion, diplomacy, and good judgment are essential, as are strong networking skills, and a client-focused attitude. The candidate must possess demonstrated skills in planning, organizing, priority setting, and problem solving in a fundraising environment. The candidate should have the proven ability to work in a fast-paced environment and be able to manage multiple projects within tightly prescribed timetables. In addition, the candidate requires the ability to make difficult decisions, identify potential risks and adjust activities to reach required goals. Strong presentation ability and written communications skills are also required, including the ability to prepare complex advancement communications, such as case statements and proposals. Proven to work autonomously and manage own schedule, with the ability to regularly work

on evenings and/or weekends and to travel as required for meetings with prospects, donors, etc. Demonstrated ability to work in a PC environment, using MS Office, and client-server database software. Bilingual in French and English.

As one of Montreal's Top Employers, here is what we offer:

  • Competitive benefits package (Health, Dental, Life Insurance) (if eligible)
  • Defined contribution pension plan (with employer contribution up to 10%) (if eligible)
  • Group Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) and Tax Free Savings Account (TFSA)

title: HR & Finance Generalist
description:
About Us

TEEG is a dedicated human services nonprofit organization focused on empowering individuals and strengthening families in Northeast Connecticut. For nearly four decades, we have provided vital community resources, including food security, youth services, senior programs, and state and federal benefits navigation. Our team works collaboratively to build a better, more supportive future for our community.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an organized, detail-oriented HR & Finance Generalist to own the people-operations and payables side of our small but mighty organization. This is a true generalist role: one week you might be running payroll and answering a benefits question, the next you're processing vendor invoices and setting up a new purchase order. If you like variety, take pride in accuracy, and want a role where your work is directly visible to leadership, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

  • Run payroll each pay period and serve as the go-to person for payroll and benefits questions.
  • Manage employee records, onboarding, offboarding, and leave/PTO tracking.
  • Administer employee benefits and serve as liaison to our brokers and carriers.
  • Process vendor invoices, purchase orders, and expense reports.
  • Maintain vendor files and support month-end close alongside the Fiscal Administrator.
  • Help keep our HR policies and purchasing procedures current, compliant, and easy for staff to follow.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years of experience in HR administration, payroll, bookkeeping, or a mix of both.
  • Comfort with payroll/HRIS tools (e.g., BambooHR, Gusto, ADP, Paychex) and accounting software (e.g., Aplos, and/ or QuickBooks).
  • A sharp eye for detail and a genuine trustworthiness with confidential information.
  • Nonprofit experience is a plus, but not required — we care more about your judgment and follow-through.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary range: $45,000-$55,000, commensurate with experience. Benefits include health insurance, 401k, PTO policy, holidays.

We’re delighted to hear that you’d like to return as a River Tour Guide at Scudamore’s.


Your role

Here’s a quick reminder of what the role entails and what we look for in our River Tour Guides:


What's involved?

  • Delivering a memorable punt tour that is informative, inspiring and entertaining.

What makes you a Scudamore’s River Tour Guide?


  • You’re friendly, approachable and enthusiastic, with great interpersonal skills.
  • You enjoy engaging with people and are committed to providing outstanding customer service.
  • You’re a confident public speaker and have an excellent command of spoken English.
  • You’re self-motivated, keen to learn, and have the ability to absorb and share knowledge.
  • You’re physically active, energetic and enjoy working outdoors.


The returners’ process

Our training and coaching programme is unique to us and is the gold standard for visitor attractions in Cambridge. Its purpose is to equip our staff with the skills, knowledge and confidence which will enable them to give our customers the best possible experience.


With this in mind we induct all returners and assess their river tours for quality purposes before they start working for us again. To ensure we are providing our customers with the very best guided tour possible, you may be asked to complete some additional training and a skills test. This will be decided depending on how long you have been away from the river and your current tour score. This will also need to be completed before you can apply for shifts. title: Design and Engineering Manager
description:
Design & Engineering Manager



Permanent, Full Time

Christchurch, NZ



  • Senior Leadership Role – People, Commercial and Technical Management focus
  • Established NZ Company with Global Market Focus
  • Market Leading Products in Capital Equipment / Machinery sector
  • Renowned reputation for product innovation and development
  • CHRISTCHURCH based role

THE OPPORTUNITY

Wyma, , has established a global reputation for reliable, high-performance post-harvest equipment and processing systems, and is a world leader in the global fresh produce sector. This reputation has been built through practical innovation, customer-driven product development, and the ability to turn new concepts into repeatable, commercially successful products. In this key technical leadership role, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring Wyma continues to deliver high-quality, innovative products and solutions, while lifting engineering capability, execution discipline, technical systems and leadership depth for the future.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Design & Engineering Manager, you will be part of Wyma NZ’s senior leadership team. Based at Wyma’s Christchurch manufacturing, engineering and product development centre, you will lead a multidisciplinary engineering team of 28 staff across New Zealand and the Czech Republic. The team delivers standard products, configured solutions and customer-specific engineering projects, while supporting product development, product release and lifecycle improvement.

You will be responsible for:

  • Building a high-performing engineering team through leadership, coaching, succession planning, and capability development.
  • Providing technical leadership and engineering judgement across complex mechanical, automation, and integrated system decisions.
  • Ensuring engineering projects are delivered to quality, budget, and schedule commitments.
  • Driving improvements in engineering standards, design reuse, documentation, governance, and resource planning.
  • Providing engineering input to support product release, lifecycle improvement and customer-specific requirements, while balancing technical and commercial outcomes.
  • Collaborating closely with Manufacturing, Product & Innovation, Sales, Project Delivery, and Aftermarket teams to achieve broader business objectives.
  • Developing future engineering leaders and ensuring critical technical knowledge is shared and retained across the business.

WHAT WE ARE SEEKING IN THE RIGHT PERSON

Leadership capability is important, and success in this role will be built on strong engineering judgement, practical problem-solving capability and the ability to earn the confidence of experienced engineers, manufacturing teams, project delivery teams and senior stakeholders. You will bring strong technical credibility from an engineered-products, machinery or capital equipment environment, together with the commercial judgement to balance customer requirements, manufacturability, serviceability, project risk and margin.

You will be comfortable operating in a practical engineered-products environment where standard products, configured solutions and customer-specific development often overlap.

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate capability and experience in the following areas:

  • Leadership through leaders: able to develop engineering managers, senior engineers and technical specialists rather than being the sole technical problem-solver.
  • Strong technical capability: credible engineering leader with the judgement to guide complex mechanical, automation or integrated equipment/system decisions, particularly in a project delivery or engineered-product environment.
  • Commercial delivery and execution: proven ability to deliver engineering outcomes to quality, budget and schedule commitments while balancing customer expectations, project risk, manufacturability, serviceability and margin.
  • Strategic systems and continuous improvement: able to lift engineering performance by improving systems, standards, design reuse, documentation, resource planning and technical governance, while building scalable capability without losing responsiveness.
  • Cross-functional influence: works effectively with Manufacturing, Project Delivery, Product & Innovation, Sales, Aftermarket and global stakeholders, with a strong whole-of-business mindset.
  • Customer and market orientation: understands how engineering decisions affect customer outcomes, product competitiveness, serviceability, reliability and long-term value.
  • People judgement and accountability: creates a constructive, high-accountability culture where expectations are clear, performance issues are addressed, and good people are coached, retained and developed.

THE COMPANY

Wyma is a world leader in the design and manufacture of post-harvest vegetable and fruit handling equipment. The business operates internationally, with Christchurch as its manufacturing, engineering and product development centre, supported by operations in Australia, the UK and the Czech Republic.

Wyma has continued to grow and develop over the past 27 years and is recognised for innovation, high-technology equipment and practical engineering solutions that help customers improve post-harvest handling performance. Its products are highly regarded in global fresh produce markets, supported by a strong focus on product development and continuous improvement.

Wyma is part of Fortifi Food Processing Solutions, a global food processing solutions group that also includes MHM Automation, Bettcher and Frontmatec. Through Fortifi, Wyma has the backing of a broader international group with complementary capability across food processing, automation and equipment solutions, while continuing to focus on its specialist strength in post-harvest vegetable and fruit handling equipment.

This is an opportunity to lead a capable engineering function in a growing international business, with real influence over how engineering capability, systems and product delivery continue to develop.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Richard at FOSTERRA Consulting Group on 021 854 545

NOTE: FOSTERRA is exclusively managing this recruitment assignment on behalf of Wyma.

title: Senior Superintendent
description:
TMG’s Senior Superintendent provides the knowledge, skills, and experience required to manage the day-to-day field operations of task orders and/or larger lump sum institutional and/or commercial construction projects. Senior Superintendents are responsible for managing other Superintendents and the self-performing staff in the production aspects of the work and are accountable for: producing quality work that is constructed consistent with the standards set forth in the project’s contract documents; performing the work in a timely and cost-effective manner and maintaining a work environment that is safe and continuously kept clean and orderly. Senior Superintendents play a leadership role at TMG, are the forward face of TMG, and are responsible for establishing a professional work environment that includes fostering a positive atmosphere, promoting proactive and effective communication, facilitating problem solving, minimizing and resolving conflict in a constructive manner, and managing other staff members to create a productive and learning environment.



Scope of Senior Superintendent Position

Supervises other Superintendents, TMG’s self-performing staff, and multiple trades of subcontractors on all aspects of small projects and large projects from start-up to completion with an approximate volume of between $7-10+ million.



Essential Functions of Senior Superintendent Position

Expert working knowledge of civil, architectural, mechanical, or electrical discipline and a strong expert understanding of the other disciplines. Expert working knowledge of construction means and methods associated with the renovation and construction of commercial and institutional buildings and site work. The ability to effectively communicate with senior and mid-level management, subcontractors, customers, and subordinates. Ability to travel to different job sites within a designated geographical area.



Responsibilities

  • Leading and managing the day-to-day field activities to ensure that all project milestone dates and overall schedule completion dates are met;
  • Creating and coordinating short-interval look-ahead project schedules that make sure that upcoming events are communicated, tracked, and are being proactively attended to;
  • Creating and maintaining a culture that values safety, health and cleanliness;
  • Managing and coordinating the work to ensure that it is constructed in an orderly and deliberate manner that is consistent with the standard-of-care set forth in the contract documents that is viewed by industry as an effort that is consistent with best-practice standards;
  • Establishing and maintaining all dimensional controls for the project to include the use of third-party survey and layout personnel when appropriate;
  • Verifying that all work is installed in a workmanlike manner (i.e., plumb, level, straight, etc.);
  • Manage and look-ahead no less than two months to proactively identify issues that could lead to problems and facilitate solutions;
  • Obtaining all inspections and ensuring that the quality aspects of the physical work are fully documented;
  • Ensuring all aspects of the project are compliant with all contract terms and legal requirements that govern the project and the community in which the project(s) takes place;
  • Administering client-specific programs, such as CQC, Safety, Environmental Stewardship, etc. ;
  • Conducting and/or attending pre-construction, progress and other project and staff meetings;
  • Conducting and/or participating in regularly held meetings involving TMG internal staff and external stakeholders such as owners, subcontractors, etc.;
  • Meeting with client representatives on a regular basis to discuss the status of projects, to proactively identify and resolve problems and to assure that the client is kept knowledgeable about the status of the work;
  • Managing self-performed activities to ensure that work is being performed within the established project budget;
  • Managing changes in project scope to ensure that the most contemporary contract documents are being used at all times to prevent avoidable rework;
  • Administering contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders and other agreements to ensure that the scope, terms and conditions are consistently and proactively being met;
  • Managing the punch list and project closeout process to assure timely completion;
  • Maintaining daily paperwork such as timecards, field reports, schedule updates and email correspondence;
  • Providing timely and cordial interaction with supporting work groups, such as accounting, HR, ICS, etc.
  • Directing and managing the workloads of supporting staff to include training, mentoring and follow-up; and
  • Participating in and encouraging staff to seek out life-long learning opportunities and professional development.
  • Evaluating the performance of staff members, writing performance evaluations, developing performance objectives and development goals, and recommending appropriate salary increases.

Minimum Qualifications

  • AS degree in Construction Management or similar field with 10+ years of related experience or a Journeyman status in a building trade (i.e., Carpenter) with 20+ years of progressive responsibility supervising construction;
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in the construction industry with a commercial and/or institutional general contractor engaged in general building and civil construction;
  • A minimum of 7 years of experience in government contracting preferred;
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets, email, and other software used in the construction industry.
  • Must be able to lift and handle 50-pound objects;
  • Must be fully mobile and capable of walking job sites, climbing ladders and stairs multiple times daily to inspect work, direct subcontractors and TMG’s own field forces, and assure safety and quality control;
  • Must have a clean driving record to facilitate getting materials from suppliers when necessary;
  • Current safety credentials to include OSHA 30 1, 1st Aid and CPR1;
  • Current CQC certification issued by USACE / NAVFAC 1;
  • US Citizenship required

1 A grace period of up to six months may be allowed to obtain stated credentials.



TMG provides a mix of voluntary and company-paid health and welfare benefits, vacation, sick and holiday paid time off, a 401 (k) match, and we fully support training and professional growth.

title: Principal Engineer (Salesforce / nCino Architect)
description:
Worker Type:

Permanent

Here at BNZ, it's about more than just banking. We work together in an agile, energising environment to create innovative solutions through our promise "If you can imagine a better future, let's find a way."

We support wellbeing, flexible working and have a generous leave offering. There is the opportunity for growth, learning and career development. No two days are the same.

Ko mātou tēnei | This is Us

Join our Customer360 team and be at the heart of one of BNZ's most significant technology transformations. We're creating a connected colleague platform that brings together customer conversations, lending journeys and workflows into a single experience, helping our colleagues better support customers at every stage of their banking journey. Leveraging Salesforce, nCino and AI, we're transforming how colleagues work and how customers are served, creating smarter, faster and more connected experiences at scale.

We have an opportunity for a Platform Architect (known in BNZ as a Principal Engineer) to join our team and provide architecture and technical leadership across our Salesforce and nCino platform.

Mō te Tūranga | About the Role

This role offers the opportunity to operate as a leader within Customer360, helping guide technical solutions for one of BNZ's most significant technology investments. By aligning with business goals and the platform’s best practice capabilities, you’ll help shape the architecture that enables us to deliver solutions that are secure, scalable, resilient, and fit for purpose as we continue our transformation journey.

This is a permanent, full-time opportunity based in Wellington or Auckland, with a hybrid working model and reporting to the Platform Manager.

What are five day-to-day tasks the person in this role will complete?

  • Strategic Technical Leadership - Provide technical leadership across our teams and value streams. You’ll guide the architecture, lead the platform design and help to ensure that our engineering standards are embedded for the future.
  • Stakeholder Influence & Delivery Enablement - Collaborate with business, technology and vendor stakeholders to align technical decisions with programme objectives to support successful delivery.
  • Complex Problem Solving - Lead the resolution of complex technical, operational, and platform challenges by applying systems thinking and influencing solutions across organisational boundaries.
  • Engineering & Quality Excellence - Set the standard for solutions that incorporate engineering best practices, platform reliability, security, observability and quality.
  • Technical Coaching & Mentoring - Mentor Engineering Leads, Senior Engineers, and emerging technical leaders, helping uplift capability and foster a culture of technical excellence.

What is the team culture and environment like?

You'll join a highly collaborative technology group of engineers, business analysts and testers within a wider programme team across four companies and three countries. You’ll be a key member of our technical domain leadership group composed of Engineering Leads, Platform Owners, and Principal Engineers. The existing environment features people who are focused on colleague outcomes, stay cool in a crisis, and like to meet high standards of quality in everything they do. Our leadership group is committed to creating a collaborative and supportive environment while driving for continuous improvement.

What is the most exciting thing about this opportunity?

This role gives you with the opportunity to provide solutions for one of New Zealand's largest Salesforce and nCino implementations. You'll help guide technical decisions that will contribute to the delivery of modern banking experiences used by thousands of colleagues and customers. The role offers significant scope to leave a lasting impact through technical leadership, mentoring and engineering excellence.

What is the most challenging thing about this opportunity?

You'll be navigating complex enterprise environments that balance colleague outcomes, regulatory obligations, operational resilience, security requirements, and delivery priorities. Success requires pragmatic technical judgement, systems thinking, influence without authority, and the ability to guide teams while maintaining a focus on simplicity, quality, and long-term sustainability.

What attributes will this person display to be successful in this role?

This role is suited to someone who sees beyond individual solutions and understands how decisions impact colleagues, the platform, operations, security, and long-term maintainability. You’ll be a pragmatic leader, able to balance engineering excellence with delivery outcomes, knowing when to pursue the ideal solution versus the right solution.

What skills are required for this role?

  • Strategic Technical Leadership - Proven experience leading the technical direction across teams and platforms with the ability to influence architecture and engineering practices, feeding into technology strategy at scale.
  • Systems & Platform Design - Strong understanding of the Salesforce and nCino platform architecture and best practice designs including resilience, scalability, security and operational reliability.
  • Influence & Stakeholder Engagement - Exceptional communication skills with the ability to influence and collaborate with engineering leads, enterprise architects, delivery teams and business stakeholders alongside vendor expertise.
  • Mentorship & Capability Building - A track record of mentoring technical leaders and engineers, uplifting capability, and fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.
  • Engineering Excellence - Demonstrated expertise in software engineering practices, quality engineering, DevSecOps, observability, testing strategies, reliability engineering, and continuous delivery.

This is an exciting opportunity to join us! We're bold thinkers who are taking brave steps to create a company that people want to work for, and customers want to bank with. If you're ready to join a fun organisation where we are proud of our culture and how we are helping New Zealander's to 'Find their way', then show your interest by submitting your application - we can't wait to read it.

title: Quality Assurance Billing Representative
description:
Location(s)

Chesterfield, Missouri

Details

Kemper is seeking a Quality Assurance Representative to join our Policy Administration team in Chesterfield. This role is responsible for evaluating the quality and accuracy of work performed across Policy Administration, including billing, payments, policy servicing, and other operational functions.

The Quality Assurance Representative plays an important role in helping us deliver an exceptional customer experience by ensuring work is completed accurately, efficiently, and consistently. This role goes beyond identifying errors. It uses quality results, data, and performance trends to understand why issues occur and identify opportunities to prevent them from happening again.

The ideal candidate is naturally curious, detail oriented, and interested in understanding the reasons behind how work gets done. You will work closely with department leaders, supervisors, subject matter experts, training partners, and other stakeholders to turn quality insights into actionable improvements that strengthen processes, employee performance, and the customer experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform quality reviews of completed work across Policy Administration, including billing, payments, and policy servicing, using established quality standards and tools.
  • Evaluate work for accuracy, compliance, consistency, and adherence to established procedures and service expectations.
  • Analyze quality results to identify trends, recurring issues, root causes, and opportunities for improvement at both the individual and team level.
  • Translate quality findings into actionable insights and recommendations for department leaders, supervisors, and other stakeholders.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps and partner with leadership, subject matter experts, and training partners to develop solutions that improve performance.
  • Participate in the development, calibration, and continuous improvement of quality standards, review criteria, and monitoring processes.
  • Develop and maintain quality reporting, trend analysis, performance metrics, and documentation of findings and follow up actions.
  • Recommend and support process improvements that increase accuracy, efficiency, consistency, and the overall customer experience.
  • Support the development and maintenance of standardized workflows, procedures, training materials, and job aids based on quality findings and process changes.
  • Participate in department initiatives, process improvement efforts, and special projects as assigned.

What We’re Looking For

  • 2+ years of experience in quality assurance, operations, insurance, billing, customer service, policy administration, or a related financial services environment.
  • Experience performing quality reviews, analyzing operational data, or identifying process improvement opportunities preferred.
  • Associate or bachelor's degree preferred. Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to identify patterns, investigate issues, and determine root causes.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to interpret data and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Outlook.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and quickly learn new processes and systems.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and willingness to respectfully challenge existing processes when opportunities for improvement are identified.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role is about more than completing quality reviews. You will help Policy Administration:

  • Identify and prevent recurring errors rather than simply reporting them.
  • Use quality data and trends to help leaders make informed decisions.
  • Strengthen training and employee development by identifying meaningful knowledge and skill gaps.
  • Improve processes and procedures to make work easier, more efficient, and more consistent.
  • Promote accountability and ownership for quality throughout the organization.
  • Improve the customer experience by helping prevent errors, rework, delays, and unnecessary customer contacts.

Why Join Us?

At Kemper, you will have the opportunity to make a measurable impact on both our operations and the customer experience. Your observations, analysis, and recommendations can directly influence how work gets done and help shape the future of our Policy Administration organization.

We value collaboration, curiosity, continuous improvement, and employees who are willing to look beyond the status quo to find better ways of working. You will have opportunities to partner with leaders and teams across the organization, expand your expertise, and contribute to initiatives that improve how we serve our customers.

Kemper offers competitive compensation, a comprehensive benefits package, opportunities for professional growth and advancement, and a supportive work environment. Depending on business needs and role requirements, flexible scheduling and hybrid work opportunities may also be available.

If you enjoy solving problems, analyzing data, improving processes, and turning insights into meaningful action, this could be a great opportunity to make a difference.

  • Cross-functional leadership: Act as the bridge among Headquarters, Regional, Sales, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Medical/Clinical, Finance, Service, and external partners, translating business needs into coordinated action.

  • Compliance and quality: Ensure all marketing materials, claims, events, sponsorships, and customer activities comply with applicable laws, company policies, quality requirements, and approval processes.

  • Business reporting: Prepare accurate forecasts, market updates, launch dashboards, campaign reviews, and management presentations; communicate risks, opportunities, and recommended actions clearly.

title: Train Conductor
description: Train Conductor At CN, we are committed to our pursuit of excellence. We take pride in delivering work of the highest standard, continually innovating to shape the railroad of the future. As responsible railroaders, we make the right decisions every time, putting safety first, acting with unwavering integrity, and holding ourselves accountable for our actions. We believe in succeeding together—by fostering inclusivity and collaboration, we sustainably deliver exceptional results for our customers. If you enjoy working outdoors in a safety-focused environment, a rewarding career as a Train Conductor might be right for you! With a dynamic 24/7 schedule, no two days working look alike. You can expect exciting challenges, paid training, and supportive colleagues who share your passion for motion. The careers we offer are meaningful because the work we do matters. Join us and get your career moving! Job Summary The Train Conductor acts as a member of a 2 or 3-person train crew and performs duties associated with the movement of trains, rail cars, and locomotives in rail yards and on the road. The incumbent coordinates the assembly of trains and completes any ground-work outside the locomotive cab while in the yard or on-route (operating track switches, picking up rail cars and making emergency repairs). Working Conditions Work a flexible schedule with regular and predictable attendance, in line with the 24/7 railroading environment. Available to work night shifts, weekends, holiday work hours, some overtime and being away from home for extended periods of time when required. Push, pull, lift and carry up to 90 pounds. Primarily work outdoors in various types of weather and environmental conditions. Operate various devices on rail cars and locomotives, such as uncoupling levers and handbrakes. Climb on and off ladders of rail cars. Grasp and hold objects while riding the side of a train. Walk for frequent extended periods. Bend, stoop, squat, and kneel frequently. Meet medical fitness requirements for the position, including those established by the Railway Association of Canada, such as the ability to recognize and distinguish between the colours of signals. Major Responsibilities Ensure compliance with all train orders, signals, railroad rules and regulations related to safety and operations. Provide and receive various forms of oral and printed instructions concerning the movement and placement of rail cars. Assemble and dismantle trains in the rail yard, and pick up and set off rail cars on-route. Observe, interpret, and relay signals to ensure safe train and locomotive movement. Operate track switches to change locomotive and rail car routes. Inspect the condition of a train and equipment. Make effective decisions when in unfamiliar locations or emergency situations. Communicate effectively with the Rail Traffic Control center, other train crews and other departments on a regular basis via handheld radio. Requirements High School Diploma or equivalence. Write and pass safety and rules exams (as per Collective Agreement, subsequent required Locomotive Engineer qualification to retain seniority and employment). Acquire and maintain Conductors Rule Card. A valid passport allowing entry and re-entry to the Canada and the United States (location-specific). Proficiency in both oral and written communications (English / French per location). Assets Relevant work experience in similar working conditions or regulatory and safety environment. Completion of College or Vocational or Technical School or Freight Conductor experience. What We Offer Competitive Wages, Benefits, and Pension Plan Paid Training and Career Development Medical, vision, and dental insurance 24/7 Telemedicine Service Employee Share Investment Plan Educational Financial Assistance Program Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) Extensive Employee Discount Program Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP) This position is a unionized position, as such pay and benefits are governed by the applicable Collective Agreement. Paid Training: Newly hired CN Conductors participate in a comprehensive paid training program at the CN Campus ( Winnipeg, MB) . Expenses related to transportation, accommodation and meals while at Campus are covered by CN. Successful completion of the entire training program, including written exams, physical assessments, and field training, is required to work as a CN Conductor. Paid Training Structure: 9 – 10 weeks* at CN Campus (classroom training exams) 11+ weeks* at CN Home Terminal (on-the-job training qualifying trips) * The specific number of weeks spent in training will depend on the requirements of the terminal and union agreement. Successful Candidate Process: Medical assessment (including drug, hearing, and vision) Criminal background check Offer Letter

title: Call for Registered Clinical Counsellors and Registered Social Workers
description:
Call for Registered Clinical Counsellors and Registered Social Workers


The Violence Prevention Programs (VPP) is seeking qualified and experienced Registered Clinical Counsellors and Social Workers to join our contractor roster.


Some Projects in VPP focus on supporting individuals and couples in developing healthier relationships, stronger communication skills, and more constructive ways of navigating relationship challenges. A key component of the project is psychoeducation for couples, with a focus on understanding healthy relationships, communication, emotional awareness, conflict resolution, boundaries, and strategies for building positive and respectful relationships.

The project will also include group sessions for men focused on managing difficult emotions and developing healthier ways of responding to emotional and interpersonal challenges. These groups will provide opportunities for participants to build emotional awareness and regulation skills, explore patterns of behaviour and communication, and develop practical strategies for responding to difficult situations in healthier and more constructive ways.


Roster members may be called upon to review or develop session content, facilitate or co-facilitate group sessions, provide counselling support during sessions, and support the overall emotional safety and well-being of participants. Where appropriate, participants may also be referred to roster counsellors for specialized or individual support based on their needs. Assignments will be offered on an as-needed basis and will depend on project requirements, qualifications, experience, and availability. Being placed on the roster does not guarantee a minimum number of hours or sessions. However, it provides an opportunity for counsellors or social workers to contribute their expertise to Violence Prevention Programs on a flexible, occasional basis.



Interested in joining the roster?

Clinical Counsellors and Social Workers who are interested in being considered for the Violence Preventions Programs’ roster are invited to reach out with:

  • A brief summary of your relevant counselling and group facilitation experience
  • Your current availability, including preferred days and times
  • Your general availability to facilitate or co-facilitate group sessions
  • Any upcoming periods when you will be unavailable
  • Any relevant experience working with couples, men’s groups, relationship education, emotional regulation, or psychoeducational programming


We will review expressions of interest and connect with service providers as opportunities arise.


Location: Services may be provided out of various MOSAIC Burnaby and Vancouver locations



Contract Details:

  • Service provision agreements with MOSAIC
  • Professional liability insurance
  • Invoicing must be submitted on a monthly basis


QUALIFICATIONS, EDUCATION AND SKILLS:

  • Master's Degree, registered with the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors
  • Bachelor's or Master's Degrees, Registered with the BC College of Social Workers
  • Experience facilitating or co-facilitating group-based psychoeducational sessions and the ability to create a safe, respectful, inclusive, and non-judgmental environment for participants
  • Strong skills in group facilitation, communication, relationship-building, and emotional regulation,
  • Trauma-informed practice would be considered an asset
  • Experience working with couples, men’s groups, relationship education, emotional regulation, or community-based programming would also be an asset

title: Creative Strategist
description:
About Tribe X

Tribe X Digital is a premier, global performance agency that sits at the intersection of luxury aesthetics and digital science. We don’t just manage campaigns; we architect end-to-end digital experiences for the world’s most prestigious hospitality brands, luxury real estate developers, and disruptive tech startups.

With a footprint spanning Amsterdam, Dubai, and Cairo, we operate as a high-octane extension of our clients' teams. Our work is defined by a "zero-ego" commitment to excellence, utilizing AI-powered advertising, bespoke content creation, and data-driven strategy to transform brand presence into measurable global impact. At Tribe X, we are building the future of luxury marketing, one pixel-perfect, ROI-positive campaign at a time.


Role Overview

As a Creative Strategist at Tribe X Digital, you play a key role in turning brand strategy and client goals into social first creative thinking, platform native ideas, content territories, and briefs that unlock great work. You connect insight, culture, and performance to create concepts that are both creatively strong and measurably effective.


What You’ll Do

  • Translate brand strategy into creative territories, content pillars, messaging angles, and platform native formats.
  • Develop campaign and high impact content ideas across mediums and channels
  • Write sharp creative briefs that clarify the “what/why/how,” of brands including audiences, hooks, deliverables, and success metrics.
  • Partner with Social Content Leads to ensure strategic intent carries into always-on execution without losing craft.
  • Collaborate with Paid/PR/Accounts to align channel roles, sequencing, and messaging across touchpoints.
  • Analyze performance and social signals to produce creative learnings and testing recommendations.
  • Present ideas and rationale clearly internally and, when needed client facing.


What You Bring (Qualifications):


Must Have:

  • 4–6 years of experience in creative strategy, social strategy, or content strategy roles, preferably within agency environments.
  • Strong strategic thinking and the ability to turn insights into clear creative direction.
  • Excellent briefing skills (creative clarity, deliverable definition, measurable outcomes).
  • Deep understanding of platform native storytelling and what “good” looks like on each channel.
  • Ability to connect performance data to creative decisions (iterate with purpose).
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, structured thinking, and persuasive rationale.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience developing social first campaigns (not just always-on content).
  • Experience directing or collaborating closely with AD/copy/production partners.
  • Familiarity with creator/influencer content models and how to brief creators effectively.
  • Experience with performance creative principles (testing frameworks, iterative production).


Success in This Role Looks Like

  • Your work makes the team smarter and the output stronger.
  • Briefs lead to better creative, ideas feel culturally relevant and platform native.
  • Consistently use performance insights to sharpen creative direction leading to more impactful campaigns and moments over time.


Why You’ll Love It Here

At Tribe X, we champion impact without ego by fostering a high-performance environment where your voice matters and your ideas scale. You will work at the edge of what is next as we use the latest AI and martech tools to solve complex challenges for premium global clients. Joining our team means tapping into a global pulse where the flexibility of a hybrid remote culture meets the high-octane energy of a world-class agency. We are built to grow and we invest deeply in your evolution because if you have the drive to lead, we provide the platform to make it happen.


Apply Now


If you are ready to bring your expertise to a team that values sharp thinking and effortless execution, let’s talk. We are looking for the restless and the bold to help us build what is next. Send us your work and start the conversation.

University Advancement plays a pivotal role in fostering meaningful connections between the University and its alumni, donors, and partners. Through strategic initiatives and collaborative efforts, we help shape the future of the University, ensuring that it continues to thrive as a leading institution of higher education and research. Together, we empower our students, faculty and researchers to make a lasting impact on the world.

Position purpose:

The incumbent is responsible for actively supporting fundraising efforts and engagement outreach of the University. As an integral part of the Advancement team, the incumbent identifies and researches prospects and constituents, tracks movement through the donor cycle, analyzes key fundraising metrics as well as develops tools to make data visible and usable. This role will manage the process of sourcing, identifying, researching and tracking prospects and constituents in the database and provide training for the effective use of the system and reports.

In this role, you will:

  • Prospect management and research: Arranges individual and group meetings with Advancement staff and Senior Leadership, which includes Managers, Directors, Deans, the office of the Vice President (Advancement) and President, to review strategies for prospect and pipeline development. Conducts high-level prospect research and analysis activities and monitors pipelines to provide timely and accurate analytical information to advise staff on strategies to advance files. This will include advice and support for data requirements.

  • Pipeline Management and research: Tracks fundraiser activities and helps to move prospects through the pipeline phases. Uses research, data mining, and analytics, to identify new prospects to optimize the growth of pipelines.

  • Prospect and research management Tools: Develops and implements pipeline and prospect management tools to assist Advancement staff to keep a robust pipeline, which will inform staff of their targets and university-wide campaign goals. In combination, prospect research tools or databases will assist with tracking and generating prospects for the pipeline.

  • Training: Provides training support and troubleshoot questions for Advancement staff related to the coding of their pipelines, and the use of systems and reporting.

  • Reporting: Prepare various moderately complex reports, on a scheduled as well as ad-hoc basis, on the health of pipelines and prospect moves for advancement teams to provide recommendations to managers, directors and senior leadership. This includes, profiles, peer screening, and environmental scans. In that sense, the incumbent helps design analytical tools such as dashboards and performance indicator reports.

  • Records management: Implement and manage an effective filing and records management system to preserve the confidentiality of the records and ensure that complete and accurate documentation is available for future reference. Ensure data integrity of systems by running validation reports and flagging inconsistencies. Provides a regular mechanism for system improvements and modifications on tracking and reporting systems.

  • Continuous Improvement: Keeps apprised of emerging strategies on prospect research and pipeline management and identifies opportunities to integrate these strategies into the University’s advancement service and to standardize business processes.

  • Other related duties: Performs other duties in support of the University’s prospect management and research efforts as assigned.

What you will bring:

  • Degree in library sciences, information management, business or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Five (5) years of experience in advancement research, prospect management, fundraising, in higher education or non-profit environment.

  • Bilingualism – French and English (spoken and written).

  • Superior interpersonal skills, with proven ability to successfully collaborate with varied parties in a professional and diplomatic manner.

  • Demonstrated understanding of development and major gifts fundraising and how research and prospect management support development efforts as well as experience working with frontline fundraisers to evaluate moves management.

  • Strong analytical skills: able to influence, analyze and synthesize data and present findings that are clear and actionable to a variety of Advancement professionals.

  • Understanding of multiple screening strategies and methodologies, including data mining, segmentation, and analytics.

  • Ability to work independently and proactively, and function in a collaborative team environment, exhibiting self-reliance, and an ability to form effective working partnerships with colleagues.

  • Strong computer skills (word processing and database analysis) and ability to learn new systems quickly. Knowledge and advanced skills in Microsoft Office are strong assets.

  • Working knowledge of French and English, with fluency (written, comprehension and spoken) in at least one of these two languages

  • Familiarity with PIPEDA (Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act) is a strong asset. The role requires the ability to use sensitive and confidential information appropriately.

  • Experience providing training to individuals and groups in both French and English would be a strong asset.

POSITION SUMMARY: A Driver- CDL (B) is responsible for safely operating a collection truck, and providing prompt, courteous and complete waste removal services for customers. PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform complete pre- and post-operation inspection of the vehicle in accordance with Company policy to ensure tire pressure, fluid levels, safety equipment, gauges, and controls are in proper working order. Report any safety issues on standard reports.
  • Safely operate his or her heavy truck along his or her designated route and to the disposal site; read route sheet, follow map and service each customer as identified on the route sheet or as assigned by the dispatcher and/or supervisor.
  • Operate manual and/or automatic controls in accordance with Company safety policies and procedures to lift and load refuse, operate compactor and dispose of collected material at the designated facility.
  • Courteously interact with all customers, dispatchers and others on a daily basis to ensure all customer routes are serviced in a timely and professional manner.
  • Identify unsatisfactory waste containers and tag containers in accordance with applicable departmental procedures.
  • Continuously monitor waste for evidence of unacceptable waste.
  • Clean area around an accidental waste spill, ensuring adherence to all applicable safety standards and policies.
  • Continuously monitor the condition of the vehicle to ensure it is operationally ready at all times to minimize down time; clean waste from the packer blade and truck body (where appropriate) on each disposal trip.
  • Complete required route/productivity sheets, VCRs and other reports, as required.
  • Maintain adherence to required productivity standards for the department to ensure all customers are serviced in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Follow all required safety policies and procedures.
  • Actively participate in the Company’s ReSOP program.
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
  • Good customer services skills to meet and exceed customer expectations; acts in a professional, courteous and cooperative manner toward customers and co-workers; works with a sense of honesty and trustworthiness.
  • Good time management skills to ensure assigned responsibilities are completed in an efficient and safe manner.
  • Good follow through ability; adheres to work schedule and follows through on challenges as they arise.
  • Ability to adhere to Company policies and rules set forth; promotes the Company’s safety standards; does not take inappropriate risks.
  • Maintains a feeling of pride in work; strives to achieve all goals.

For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).


RECENT RECOGNITION

  • CDP Discloser
  • Dow Jones Best-In-Class Indices
  • Ethisphere’s World’s Most Ethical Companies
  • Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies
  • Great Place to Work
  • Sustainability Yearbook S&P Global

title: Proposal Specialist
description:
About Street Level Strategy
Street Level Strategy, LLC is a political and public affairs consulting firm specializing in grassroots mobilization, coalition building, campaign management, marketing, communications, and strategic consulting. Street Level Strategy combines time-tested grassroots engagement strategies with a data-driven, results-first approach to design and execute high-impact programs for clients across various industries and sectors.

Street Level Strategy is a growing firm with a footprint across North America. Our team of over 30 professionals is based in Pasadena, CA, with offices in Sacramento and Berkeley, CA. Clients include political candidates, ballot measures, issue advocacy campaigns, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and Fortune 500 corporations across the US and Canada.

We take pride in the diversity of our team – we are bilingual, have women and people of color in high-level leadership positions, and reflect the diversity of the communities we work in.

Street Level is hiring a Proposal Specialist in Pasadena, CA or Sacramento, CA

Position Summary

Street Level Strategy is a growing public affairs firm, with a high volume of proposal opportunities. In this role, you’ll prepare proposals that describe the features and benefits of Street Level’s constantly evolving services. You’ll edit, rewrite, and write technical and nontechnical text as necessary to prepare the most compelling possible proposals that highlight Street Level’s services. You’ll also be responsible for the creation of clear, visually persuasive graphics and for the timely delivery of a clean, error-free final product.

Reporting directly to the Managing Partner and coordinating with Client Team Leads, this role will play a critical part in designing and defining SLS’s business strategy.

This position is ideal for someone who has initiative, flexibility, and dependability to produce documents that reflect Street Level’s commitment to engaging and outreaching to communities.

What You Will Achieve

Pipeline Sourcing & Opportunity Assessment

  • Build and develop a pipeline across federal, state, local, and private sources, establishing the tools and routines that surface relevant solicitations early
  • Perform detailed analysis of RFI/RFQ/RFP documents — evaluation criteria and applicable state or agency procurement rules — to identify requirements, constraints, and discriminators
  • Provide leadership with honest bid/no-bid recommendations, including recommending which RFPS to pursue and have a chance to win
  • Draft and submit questions to the contracting officer or procurement contact to resolve ambiguity before the response is built


Capture & Pre- RFP Positioning

  • Track priority business pursuits from client team leads, as well as build a tracking mechanism to monitor all public business sites for federal, local, and state RFP’s.
  • Develop working knowledge of target local, state, and federal agencies' priorities and procurement history, and translate it into positioning SLS can act on
  • Identify and recommend structures that close capability gaps for specific RFP pursuits
  • Produce capture plans for the firm's highest-value business pursuits, defining win strategy, discriminators, and gaps to close


Proposal Management & Schedule Ownership

  • Own the proposal schedule end to end, with milestones, reviews, and author deadlines
  • Coordinate input from teaming partners and subcontractors on the process, ensuring deadlines and milestones are met.


Compliance & Solicitation Discipline

  • Build and maintain the compliance matrix or checklist for each submission, ensuring every requirement is addressed,
  • Enforce all format constraints — page counts, fonts, margins, volume structure, file naming and size — as hard limits
  • Fact-check content and flag technical errors, unsupported claims, and inconsistencies before submission
  • Hold final documents to firm editorial standards, drawing on shared editorial support for line-level proofing


Content Development & Narrative

Function Building & Continuous Improvement

Who You Are
