OVERVIEW

CetraRuddy is an award-winning global architecture, planning and interior design firm driven by design excellence and the belief that Architecture Is Home. For three decades, the firm has led with a guiding principle that architecture and design must engage in context and enrich the human spirit, seeking opportunities to craft innovative solutions and lead clients on their journeys toward building a new legacy. The firm’s portfolio of work is defined by crafted details, innovative use of materials and contextual sensitivity across various market sectors including residential, hospitality, educational, cultural, and commercial.



We are currently seeking a Senior Interior Designer with specialized experience in multifamily residential projects, particularly in the design and transformation of office spaces into residential buildings. This role offers the unique opportunity to contribute to impactful projects while upholding the firm’s dedication to quality, creativity, and contextual integrity.



As a Senior Interior Designer, you will lead complex projects from concept through final detailing, bringing senior-level design leadership paired with a strong aesthetic sensibility and the ability to make thoughtful, aligned design decisions. The ideal candidate has previous experience mentoring team members and collaborating across disciplines and with clients, all while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced studio environment.

You will oversee the coordination of interior documentation and FF&E specifications, while also guiding Intermediate Designers to ensure their work aligns with CetraRuddy’s continued evolution of multifamily design by prioritizing quality, functionality, and design integrity.



We offer a comprehensive benefits package, a hybrid optional working environment on Mondays and Fridays, and opportunities for professional development within a collaborative team.



RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the development of design layouts, frameworks, and overall interior direction across large-scale multi-family residential projects, ensuring alignment with project goals and design intent.
  • Provide guidance and oversight to Intermediate Designers, managing internal teams and delegating tasks to support high-quality execution and studio-wide growth.
  • Work alongside other senior staff and Principals to successfully execute project administration.
  • Oversee the creation and refinement of drawings, renderings, and presentations for internal reviews, client meetings, consultant coordination, and construction phases.
  • Manage Construction Administration efforts including submittal reviews, RFIs, site visits, and punch list walkthroughs to ensure design intent is carried through to completion.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for clients and consultants, maintaining strong relationships while identifying opportunities to cultivate new ones.
  • Lead the development of space planning strategies, schematic design presentations, and design narratives that reflect project goals, budgets, and client expectations.
  • Direct the presentation of design concepts, mood boards, and visual materials that clearly communicate vision and support stakeholder alignment and approvals.
  • Oversee the selection and specification of materials, finishes, fixtures, and furnishings, including the development of FF&E packages and custom furniture drawings that align with design direction and budget.
  • Ensure all designs meet firm and client standards, as well as applicable codes, safety regulations, and accessibility requirements, with deep knowledge of ADA compliance.
  • Lead consultant coordination and manage the interiors scope through all phases, ensuring clear communication and collaboration across disciplines.



SKILLS & REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Interior Design or related field.
  • Minimum of 10 years of experience in an interior design firm, with at
    least 6+ years supporting large-scale multifamily or adaptive reuse residential projects.
  • Strong proficiency in Revit, AutoCAD, Adobe Creative Suite, SketchUp, and FF&E documentation tools.
  • Can provide a strong design sensibility with an advanced understanding of design principles, aesthetics, and interior detailing across all project phases.
  • Demonstrates strong presentation skills with the ability to remain poised and confident, effectively translating client and team feedback into actionable deliverables across all project phases.
  • Manage complex projects from schematic design through construction administration, including documentation, finish coordination, and FF&E integration.
  • Lead coordination efforts with clients, consultants, and internal teams, and translate feedback into clear, actionable deliverables.
  • Mentor and delegate to Intermediate and Junior Designers, supporting their development while maintaining design quality and project efficiency.
  • Apply strong written and verbal communication skills, with a proactive mindset and collaborative approach to leadership.
  • Engage in firm-wide initiatives and contribute to a supportive, inclusive studio culture.

title: Freshwater Ecologist

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
We are looking for an experienced Technical Product Manager with strong hands-on experience writing engineering-grade specifications, to work deeply on a complex B2B SaaS platform. In this role, you will be responsible for translating product needs into precise technical specifications, working closely with engineering teams throughout development.

This role is not focused on outbound activity or broad strategic positioning — it is a deeply hands-on position centered on getting into the details and working internally across departments to take ideas from concept to execution.


Key Responsibilities

  • Product Requirements (PRD): Write detailed, engineering-level Product Requirement Documents, including functional logic, edge cases, technical dependencies, and clear specifications for implementation by R&D.
  • User Experience (UX): Hands-on involvement in the UX design process, ensuring specifications are intuitive, technically implementable, and meet high usability standards.
  • Collaboration with R&D: Work closely with engineers to clarify specifications, resolve technical questions during development, and ensure implementation matches the original intent of the spec.
  • Data Analysis: Use data analytics to inform product decisions and measure the impact of product changes.



Qualifications

  • Experience: Proven track record in product specification within a B2B environment, particularly SaaS Gaming\trading Experience with complex systems is essential.
  • Proven previous experience working closely with RND teams
  • Technical Skills: Hands-on experience building roadmaps and writing engineering-level Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) – required.
  • Hands-on experience with UX design – required.
  • AI Proficiency: Knowledge and hands-on experience using AI tools for product specification and product management (e.g., AI-assisted PRD writing, roadmap planning, and analysis) – a plus.
  • Familiarity with SaaS product development processes.
  • Experience in data analysis – a plus.
  • Problem-Solving: Exceptional problem-solving skills, with analytical and creative thinking to translate complex problems into clear technical specifications.
  • Technical Communication: Strong ability to communicate and translate complex requirements between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

title: Hydronic Piping Foreman
description:
Hydronic Piping Foreman
Location: Richmond, Virginia
Department: Field Operations
Reports To: Project Manager / Superintendent
Employment Type: Full-Time


Position Summary
Titan Mechanical & Plumbing, Inc. is seeking an experienced Hydronic Piping Foreman to lead and coordinate field installation of hydronic piping systems on commercial mechanical construction projects. The Foreman will oversee daily field activities, direct journeymen, apprentices, and other assigned personnel, and ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project plans and specifications. Please note: The work location for this role is Richmond, VA.


The ideal candidate has strong commercial mechanical piping experience, understands hydronic systems, can read and interpret mechanical drawings, and is comfortable leading a field crew while working closely with Project Managers, Superintendents, General Contractors, and other trades. Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead and supervise hydronic piping crews on commercial construction projects.
  • Plan and coordinate daily manpower, materials, equipment, and work activities.
  • Install and oversee installation of hydronic piping systems, including:
    • Chilled water piping
    • Hot water piping
    • Heating water systems
    • Condenser water piping
    • Pump and equipment connections
    • Valves, fittings, strainers, and related components
  • Read and interpret mechanical drawings, specifications, and project plans.
  • Understand piping layouts, elevations, dimensions, and equipment connections.
  • Coordinate piping installation with HVAC equipment, plumbing, electrical, structural, and other trades.
  • Verify materials and equipment are available and properly staged before beginning work.
  • Ensure installations are completed according to approved drawings and project specifications.
  • Identify potential conflicts, layout issues, and field conditions and communicate them to the Project Manager or Superintendent.
  • Perform and oversee pipe layout, fabrication, installation, and support.
  • Ensure proper pipe slope, alignment, supports, hangers, insulation clearances, and equipment connections.
  • Assist with pressure testing, flushing, system startup, and commissioning activities.
  • Inspect completed work to ensure quality and workmanship standards are met.
  • Maintain accurate daily reports and communicate job progress and manpower needs.
  • Train, direct, and mentor apprentices and less-experienced employees.
  • Enforce company safety policies and OSHA requirements on the jobsite.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area.
  • Coordinate inspections with the appropriate project personnel.
  • Communicate effectively with General Contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and Titan management.
  • Troubleshoot field issues and provide practical solutions.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.


Qualifications

  • 5+ years of commercial mechanical piping experience preferred.
  • Previous experience as a Foreman or Lead Mechanic strongly preferred.
  • Strong experience with commercial hydronic piping systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings and specifications.
  • Strong understanding of pipe fittings, valves, supports, hangers, and piping systems.
  • Ability to take measurements and perform basic calculations.
  • Ability to lead a crew and effectively delegate work.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills.
  • Ability to identify and resolve field conflicts.
  • Ability to work independently while following project direction.
  • OSHA 30 certification preferred.
  • Valid driver's license required.
  • Must be able to work safely in an active construction environment.


Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry materials and equipment as required.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb, and work for extended periods.
  • Ability to work from ladders, lifts, scaffolding, and elevated work areas.
  • Ability to work in varying weather and jobsite conditions.
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Ability to safely handle tools, piping, fittings, and mechanical equipment.


What We Offer

  • Competitive pay based on experience
  • Health, dental, and vision benefits
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid time off
  • Paid holidays
  • Opportunities for advancement
  • Company-paid training
  • Stable work with an established commercial mechanical contractor

title: VP, Head of Agency Middle Office
description:
Client Service Delivery | Administrative Agency| VP, Head of Agency Middle Office | New York

About ING:

In the Americas, ING’s Wholesale Banking division offers a broad range of innovative financial products and services to domestic and international corporate and institutional clients.


When you come to work at ING, you’re joining a team where individuality isn’t just accepted, it’s encouraged. We’ve built a culture that’s fun, friendly and supportive – it’s the kind of place where you can be yourself and make the most of whatever you have to offer.

We give people the freedom to take risks, think differently, take ownership of their work, and make great things happen. We’re here to help you get ahead. And with our global network, there’s plenty of scope to take your career in new directions, perhaps even ones you’ve never considered. ING Americas follows a hybrid work model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility. Hybrid work arrangements vary based on business area.


Sound like the kind of place you’d feel at home? We’d love to hear from you.

About the position:

The Head of Agency Middle Office is responsible for leading a team of Agency professionals and overseeing the agency function for a diverse portfolio lending transactions where ING serves in the capacity of Admin Agent or similar Agency function. This role serves as the primary escalation point for complex agency matters and is responsible for ensuring the consistent delivery of high-quality agency services to borrowers, lenders, and internal stakeholders. The position partners closely with Origination, Lending, Legal, Risk, Operations, and external counterparties to manage transaction execution, governance, risk oversight, and client service. In addition, the role is responsible for the continued development of the Agency Middle Office function, including process enhancement, control framework development, team leadership, and implementation of scalable operating practices.

About the department:

The Agency Middle Office team manages all aspects of the Administrative Agent function for transactions where ING Capital LLC serves as Administrative Agent and/or Collateral Agent. The team acts as a central point of coordination between borrowers, lender groups, legal counsel, consultants, and other various stakeholders throughout the lifecycle of a transaction. The department is focused on delivering best in class agency services while maintaining strong operational controls, risk management, and client engagement.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Agency Middle Office team, including direct management and ongoing development of team members, while overseeing ING Capital LLC’s Administrative Agency function.
  • Serve as the primary escalation point and subject matter expert for complex agency matters, including amendments, waivers, consents, documentation interpretation, and lender approvals.
  • Develop and support the Agency personnel through staffing, training, performance management, workload prioritization, and succession planning.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with borrowers, lenders, legal counsel, consultants, and internal stakeholders, serving as a trusted partner throughout the transaction lifecycle.
  • Maintain a centralized agency pipeline across sectors to support capacity planning and resource management.
  • Drive process improvement, standardization, and innovative enhancements to improve efficiency and service delivery across the agency portfolio.
  • Maintain strong risk controls and governance by ensuring compliance with legal documentation, internal policies, regulatory requirements, and LSTA agency market standards.

title: Senior Associate, Survey Programming (SurveyCTO)
description:
ABOUT INKOMOKO

Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive.

In 2026, Inkomoko was listed by the Financial Times as the 5th fastest-growing company in Africa, supporting entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa to grow thriving businesses and build inclusive, resilient economies.

Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 100,000 entrepreneurs, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest investor to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa.

Inkomoko has 900+ staff in 50 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko’s 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives.


INKOMOKO VALUES

All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values:

  • Purpose:be solutions-oriented, produce high-quality work, and be a global leader.
  • Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you previously thought possible.
  • Improvement: be humble, engage in continuous growth through open & accurate feedback
  • Bravery:willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, and inclusive.
  • We Eat Goat: we celebrate success and support each other in hard times. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, Kula na sawa, On est ensemble.

Inkomoko is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer. Refugees, women, and persons who reflect the diverse communities we serve are strongly encouraged to apply.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY AND RESPONSIBILITIES

As a Senior Associate, Survey Programming, you will be the organization's go-to expert for translating survey instruments into high-quality, field-ready digital tools. Working closely with the Business Analytics Manager, the wider MERL team, and Programs teams across the region, you will understand the questions that define our program indicators and code these into robust, well-tested surveys — ensuring survey logic faithfully captures each indicator, forms are error-free and user-friendly, and resulting data is clean and analysis-ready.

Success in this role requires strong technical survey-programming skills, meticulous attention to detail and data quality, and the ability to collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical teams in different countries. This role is regional, working closely with teams across Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Chad.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Survey Design & Programming (35%)

  • Translate paper-based/draft instruments into fully-programmed, logic-driven digital forms; primarily in SurveyCTO with robust skip patterns, relevance/constraint logic, validations, calculations, case management, and multi-language versions.
  • Design forms for offline data collection in low-connectivity field environments (repeat groups, roster/loop structures, geopoint/media capture), and translate program indicators into precise, coded survey questions while working with MERL and Programs teams.
  • Skilled in questionnaire design using tools such as Google Forms, particularly for rapid surveys and qualitative data collection.

2. Data Quality, Testing & Piloting (20%)

  • Conduct rigorous dummy-data testing, dry runs, and piloting of every form before deployment; build data-quality checks (range, consistency, duplicate, GPS/time) within the survey and at data review.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve form- and server-level errors quickly during active data collection to minimize disruption to fieldwork.

3. Indicator Alignment & MERL/Programs Collaboration (15%)

  • Work with the Business Analytics Manager, MERL, and Programs teams to clarify indicator definitions and ensure they are correctly operationalized in survey tools; maintain codebooks, data dictionaries, and naming conventions.
  • Support survey sampling logic and case assignment design where relevant (e.g., CommCare case management for longitudinal/beneficiary tracking).

4. Server & Platform Administration (15%)

  • Manage SurveyCTO server console(s) form deployment/versioning, user/role management, dataset publishing, server-side data checks, and monitor data collection dashboards in real time, flagging anomalies to field teams.
  • Maintain secure including controlled access to forms, organized form/dataset repositories and support integration of survey data into downstream reporting and analytics pipelines.

5. Training, Documentation & Continuous Improvement (10%)

  • Train Programs/MERL staff on tool usage and troubleshooting; maintain documentation of survey logic, version histories, and SOPs.
  • Stay current with SurveyCTO best practices and recommend improvements to tools and workflows.

6. Analytics Support (5%)

  • Support the Analytics & Research team with data cleaning, analysis, and reporting using Excel, Stata, Python, R, or similar tools to support program learning and decision-making.

Requirements

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • Education: Bachelor's degree required; a degree in Statistics, Computer Science, IT, Data Science, M&E, or Social Sciences will be highly considered.
  • Experience: 4+ years in survey programming/digital data collection, ideally within an M&E, research, or international development context.
  • Survey Platforms: Experience coding surveys in SurveyCTO strongly preferred; candidates with ODK, KoBoToolbox, or CommCare experience are also encouraged to apply.
  • Technical Skills: Strong command of form logic (relevance, constraints, calculations), XLSForm structure, repeat groups/case management, and multi-language form design.
  • Data Handling: Proficiency in Excel/data-cleaning tools; ability to export, review, and quality-check datasets from digital surveys.
  • Data Analysis: Basic to advanced skills in data analysis using tools such as Excel, Stata, Python, R - among others
  • MERL Literacy: Working understanding of indicators, logframes/results frameworks, Theory of Change (TOC), and how survey design affects downstream data quality.
  • Attention to Detail: A meticulous, quality-first approach to form testing, logic-checking, and troubleshooting under field deadlines.
  • Collaboration: Proven ability to work closely with MERL and Programs teams including remote/cross-country teams.
  • Languages: Fluency in English required; French is an added advantage given our operations in Chad.

Key competencies:

We are looking for someone who:

  • Instills Trust - Follows through on commitments, builds credibility by being direct and truthful, and shows genuine care for staff members.
  • Acts with Courage - Steps up to address difficult issues and speaks openly with bravery; takes the initiative to pursue new opportunities; takes full ownership of own work
  • Makes Informed Decisions - Seeks relevant data and input when needed, takes appropriate action within their area of responsibility, and knows when to escalate.

Benefits

WHAT YOU’LL GET

This role is inside a high-growth, mission-driven social enterprise. By joining, you’ll access:

  • Meaningful work that directly contributes to sustainable livelihoods and job creation across East and Central Africa.
  • Competitive salary, and potential Performance-based bonus
  • Incredible company culture, with opportunities for learning and growth
  • Diverse colleagues across the region, and policies that demonstrate commitment to equity and inclusion
  • A dynamic and entrepreneurial team environment committed to innovation and social impact
  • Health insurance for self and family
  • Staff savings and provident fund negotiated bank rates for long-term employees
  • Generous annual leave, parental leave, and sabbatical options.

TO APPLY

If you’re excited about this role, please submit your CV and tell us why you are the right fit for this opportunity.

Application Deadline: 1st September 2026

Inkomoko is committed to justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion. As we seek to reflect the communities we serve, refugees and women are strongly encouraged to apply. As a company, we have policies that ensure fair treatment in the application process.

NB: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Employment is conditional upon successful background checks and other verification as needed.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and background screening checks. Inkomoko also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual misconduct, fraud, or abuse. By applying, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

title: Early Years Lead Educators (Barcelona, Spain)
description:
👋 About Boundless Life

Boundless Life is redefining the way families live, work, and learn by empowering them to embrace a nomadic lifestyle that fosters deeper connections and personal growth. We provide family-friendly accommodations, an innovative education system that travels with you, and vibrant communities of like-minded individuals. Our mission is to create immersive "live abroad" experiences that balance professional commitments with enriching personal development.

Since our founding in 2021, we've rapidly expanded to eight locations across Europe, Asia, and Latin America. Our growth reflects our commitment to transforming the experience economy and making a meaningful impact on how families integrate work, education, and exploration into their lives.

At Boundless Life, we believe in the power of community and the importance of a holistic approach to education. Our programmes are designed to inspire curiosity, build resilience, and nurture a global perspective, preparing children for an ever-changing future.

Join us in pioneering a new way of living that harmoniously blends work, learning, and adventure, enabling families to thrive in a connected and dynamic world.


Please note:

- This role is part of our hiring for the upcoming launch in Barcelona. As we are still finalising operational timelines for the location, exact start dates are yet to be confirmed. We're reviewing applications on a rolling basis and are committed to keeping shortlisted candidates informed as plans take shape.

- Our business language is English; please submit your application in English.


🙌 About the Role

Boundless Education is transforming current systems of education. Our educational concept empowers all children to explore their natural creativity, discover their true passions, and shape their own future. We apply the renowned Finnish Curriculum, integrated with best pedagogical practices from around the world, to create a personalised, multi-age, skills-driven and strength-based system that is supportively led by educators as mentors.

We are looking for a passionate Explorers Lead Educator to join our team for the upcoming launch of Boundless Life in Barcelona.

Working with children in our Explorers age group (1–5 years old), the Explorers Lead is responsible for driving the classroom experience and guiding each child through their individual learning journey. You will create a safe, nurturing and stimulating environment where young children can explore their natural curiosity, build independence and develop socially, emotionally, physically and cognitively.

Learning at Boundless is not confined to the classroom. You'll create meaningful, experiential learning opportunities that make use of the local environment and community while integrating Montessori principles and the Boundless Education Questing framework into everyday learning.


👩‍🏫 What You'll Do

  • Ensure the duty of care for all children and create a safe, nurturing learning environment
  • Lead the day-to-day classroom experience for the Explorers age group
  • Cultivate a strong sense of community, belonging and independence
  • Foster children's holistic well-being, encompassing their physical, social and emotional development
  • Implement the Boundless Education Questing framework to create authentic learning experiences
  • Guide children along personalised learning pathways, responding to their individual interests, strengths and developmental needs
  • Apply Montessori principles and practices within the Early Years environment
  • Plan interdisciplinary and experiential learning opportunities incorporating the local environment and community
  • Establish developmentally appropriate goals with children and monitor their progress through observation, documentation and feedback
  • Provide routine updates to parents and carers using our technological tools
  • Lead parent conferences and contribute to end-of-cohort Growth Trackers
  • Maximise educational technology tools where developmentally appropriate
  • Build strong and trusted relationships with parents and carers
  • Collaborate closely with fellow educators and the wider Education team to maintain high standards of learning and care
  • Engage in continuous professional learning and contribute to the ongoing development of Boundless Education


✅ About You

General Requirements

  • Excellent English language skills; Spanish is a strong advantage for this location
  • Living in Barcelona or nearby, or willing to relocate, and able to commute daily
  • Minimum two years of teaching experience in Early Years
  • Experience working with children within the 1–5 age range
  • Experience with culturally and linguistically diverse learners
  • Able to thrive in fast-paced, evolving and multicultural environments
  • A clear, warm and effective communicator with both children and adults
  • Strong understanding of child development and age-appropriate learning practices
  • Ability to create a safe, inclusive and child-centred learning environment
  • Special educational needs or inclusive education experience is a strong advantage

Educational Qualifications

  • A recognised qualification in Early Childhood Education, Early Years Education, Child Development, or a closely related field
  • Montessori training, with the ability to confidently apply Montessori principles within an Early Years learning environment
  • Strong knowledge of early childhood development, safeguarding and children's social and emotional needs

Preferred

  • Formal Montessori certification, such as AMI, AMS or an equivalent recognised Montessori qualification
  • A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Early Childhood Education, Education, Child Development, Special Educational Needs, or a related discipline
  • Experience with inquiry-based, experiential, play-based or other child-centred educational approaches
  • Familiarity with, or formal study of, the Finnish curriculum
  • Certification or postgraduate study in special educational needs, inclusive education or learning support
  • Experience supporting multilingual learners
  • Current safeguarding or child protection certification
  • Current first aid or paediatric first aid certification
  • Evidence of ongoing professional learning relevant to Early Years education

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory enhanced criminal records check or equivalent.


🎁 What We Offer

  • Meaningful impact — help create an educational experience where children grow holistically
  • Curriculum innovation — pioneer experiential and place-based learning that turns destinations into classrooms
  • Professional growth — develop within a dynamic international education environment where your role can grow as you grow
  • Family benefits — enjoy discounted tuition for your children at Boundless Education
  • Competitive salary and vacation
  • Meals during the day


Take a look at our policies and benefits here.


✨ What's Next?

  1. Recruitment screening (30 min)
  2. Interview with the Programme Learning & Design team (60 min)
  3. Interview with the Education Centre Director (60 min)
  4. Final check-in with the COO, if required (60 min)


The process might change slightly as we go along — we will keep you posted at all times.

Want to know more about working at Boundless Life? Check out our story!

title: Private Patient Coordinator
description:
Who are we?

Newmedica is one of the leading providers of NHS ophthalmology services in England, delivering outpatient appointments, diagnostic testing and eye surgery to change lives through better sight and eye health.

We’re proud to have been certified as a Great Place to Work for the third year running and listed among the UK’s top 30 Best Workplaces™ for 2026 —recognition that reflects how colleagues feel about working here.

Our Purpose is to change lives through better sight and eye health, and our Vision is to end avoidable sight loss in every community we serve; we live our values every day—Commercial, Courageous, Compassion, Collaborative and Curious.


Role overview
We are looking for a Private Patient Coordinator to join our Leeds site. This will be 40 hours over 5 days per week, including weekends on a rota basis. The ideal candidate must have flexibility to travel to Harrogate and Wakefield when required.


As Private Patient Coordinator, your role will be to ensure that all of our private patients have a fantastic experience throughout their journey with us, from first contact to the end of their treatment pathway. This will include meeting and greeting them on the day of their appointments and treatments. We aim to offer our private patients a truly personalised service and this role is key to ensuring that they feel supported by someone they know and trust.
You will be the central point of contact for all telephone queries in regard to private patients and also for ensuring all initial enquiries and referrals are dealt with within the required KPIs. You will also undertake general administrative tasks such as ordering lenses and inputting data onto the private patient tracker.


Our clinics are busy so we're looking for someone who can manage a busy and varied workload. We are looking for someone who is incredibly customer focused, with the ability to provide a first class service to patients. The thought of eye surgery can be a daunting prospect for patients to deal with, so you will need to have an empathetic approach and be able to put others at ease.


What skills and experience do I need?

  • Experience in a customer service role and a passion for delivering excellent service
  • Experience in a healthcare environment would be advantageous but not essential
  • Experience in recruitment, financial services or private healthcare sales advantageous but not essential
  • Excellent administration skills
  • The ability to reassure and support patients in a healthcare setting where people may be nervous or anxious about treatment
  • Excellent computer skills. Comfortable with Microsoft Office products and the ability to learn new systems
  • Outstanding communication skills
  • A good team player - happy to jump in and support others when required


What we're offering

  • A salary of £27,976.00 per annum
  • 200 hours annual leave plus bank holidays (pro-rata).
  • Death in Service scheme.
  • A company pension scheme.
  • Access to a range of benefits including free eye tests, discounted or free glasses, a free 24/7 well-being/counselling/advice service.
  • An environment where your learning and development is supported through a range of various learning tools and courses.
  • Working with a friendly multi-disciplinary team passionate about improving the lives of our patients
  • A bright, spacious and modern working environment, built to the highest standards.


If you would like an informal chat about the opportunity or to request a job description, please contact Sophie Newsome, HR Administrator at sophie.newsome@newmedica.co.uk


Our employment offers are subject to receipt of satisfactory pre-employment checks. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK and a Disclosure and Barring Service check will be necessary in the event of a successful application which we will pay for.


At Newmedica, we actively promote diversity and equal opportunities, and we are committed to this, in both the running of our services and how we recruit out staff. We actively encourage applications from everyone with the essential requirements of the job, regardless of any protected characteristics.


Newmedica is fully committed to safeguarding the welfare of all people, irrespective of gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, race, language or social origin.

title: Associate Planner
description:
City of Kenora

External Job Posting


Kenora provides a high quality of life for residents and unforgettable experiences for visitors by celebrating and embracing the community’s rich heritage, diversity, and natural environment.


Job Title: Associate Planner

Location: Kenora, Ontario

Division: Planning

Type: Full Time | Temporary 18 Month Placement

Salary: (PM 06) $95,194 – 111,714 per year

Closing Date: September 25, 2026


Please note that we encourage early applications as we may proceed with interviews and make offers to exceptional candidates before the closing date.


Reporting to the City Planner, the Associate Planner provides planning knowledge and expertise related to statutory planning and community development. Activities include: interpretation of relevant planning legislation, along with the evaluation of complex land use planning issues to ensure that growth and development is planned and managed for current and future generations.


Duties/Responsibilities:

    • Provides information and assistance to staff and the general public on planning-related matters including development procedures, zoning, land use, and municipal policies plans as they relate to planning.
    • Accepting, reviewing, and processing land development applications including but not limited to applications for minor variances, applications for consent, application for Draft Plan of Condominium, Draft Plans of Subdivision, site plan control applications and agreements, etc. in accordance with the Planning Act, City By-laws, policies and procedures.
    • Communicates with internal departments and external stakeholders.
    • Reviews requests for zoning and building compliance. Prepares and signs compliance letters.
    • Receives, processes and tracks requests for Letter of Comfort Applications and License of Occupation applications.
    • Receives, processes and tracks Environmental Site Assessment Application requests.
    • Reviews and signs off on planning and zoning matters related to Business Licenses.
    • Contributes to the preparation of land development applications by providing input and advice to the City Planner.
    • Designs and implements communication tools as prescribed by the Planning Act and initiated by the City to support public engagement and consultation events and activities.
    • Conducts research on relevant planning matters; prepares qualitative and quantitative analysis to inform policy recommendations.
    • Performs statutory duties of Secretary Treasurer of the City of Kenora Committee of Adjustment and Land Division Committee (Planning Advisory Committee).
    • Works independently and as part of departmental and interdepartmental teams on the preparation of major studies, plans and policy proposals for recommendation to senior staff, administration and Council.
    • Attends evening and weekend meetings (as required).
    • Other related duties from time to time as required.


    Qualifications:

    • Post-secondary degree in Urban, Rural or Regional Planning, preferably at the Master’s level. An equivalent combination of a directly related degree (e.g. geography, landscape architecture) combined with planning work experience may be considered.
    • One (1) to three (3) years of demonstrated experience in municipal planning, real-estate or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
    • Eligibility for candidate membership in the Canadian Institute of Planners, or a willingness to work towards membership status (Full membership is preferred).
    • Able to work independently, concisely, and accurately with the ability to meet deadlines.
    • Ability to balance multiple projects and priorities to bring projects to completion using sound judgment, initiative, and creativity in a fast-paced, politically sensitive environment with minimal supervision.
    • Effective analytical and critical systems thinking skills.
    • Strong problem-solving skills including the ability to handle sensitive issues.
    • Excellent interpersonal skills that facilitate effective working relationships with colleagues, other departments, and clients.
    • Ability to communicate effectively with strong written, listening, and presentation skills that promote understanding and clarity in a respectful manner.
    • Proven related knowledge and experience in municipal planning and/or planning principles
    • Strong computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office including: Excel, Word and PowerPoint,
    • Experience in mapping software including GIS would be an asset.
    • A valid “G” Class Driver’s License with an acceptable Driver’s Abstract is required. This position may be required to operate a municipal vehicle for business purposes.


    Successful candidates will be required to submit a criminal record check and professional references.


    The City of Kenora is an equal opportunity Employer and committed to building a workforce that reflects the rich diversity of the community we serve. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals including members of groups with historical and/or current barriers to equitable employment, including but not limited to, Indigenous Peoples, members of racialized communities or visible minorities, persons with visible and/or invisible disabilities, diverse sexual and gender identities, orientations and/or expressions, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

    The City of Kenora is committed to providing accommodation in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you require an accommodation, please advise the Human Resources department in advance to ensure your participation in the recruitment and selection process.

    Personal information is collected under the authority of the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act and is used to determine eligibility for potential employment.

    We thank all candidates for their interest, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

    Accommodations are available for all parts of the recruitment process.
    Applicants need to make their needs known in advance.

title: Internal:  Counsellor, Children's Services- Nipigon CC0826
description:
Benefits:

  • Competitive and comprehensive employer-paid health and dental benefits, along with paid sick time
  • The Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
  • 12 paid days off to honour and observe statutory holidays, including a holiday shutdown during the winter break
  • 4-weeks’ vacation* with 3 Family Care Days and 3 Floater Days (pro-rated for the first year of employment)


Other Benefits:

  • Expense claim reimbursement for mileage and meals when travelling across the district
  • Flexible work schedule per accrual of flex time
  • Opportunities for growth and professional development
  • Agency Wellness Committee initiatives
  • Financial assistance with relocation is available


Summary


The Counsellor, Children’s Services is a full-time, permanent (37.5 hours per week), on-site, in-person in Nipigon, ON. Working within a Recovery Framework, the Counsellor, Children's Services supports children and youth (birth to 17 years of age) living with mental health challenges and/or developmental disabilities and their families/guardians and communities across the District of Thunder Bay. The Counsellor, Children's Services, works as an integral part of a clinical team responsible for providing mental health core services funded by the Ministry, including but not limited to access/intake, assessment, brief service, counselling, crisis response, case management, and family support. Services are delivered one-on-one and through group facilitation and may occur in person, in-community, or virtually. The Counsellor, Children Services reports directly to the assigned Clinical Services Manager.


Qualifications and Requirements THE “MUST HAVES”

  • Education that grants eligibility or qualifying status, at the time of application, and a commitment to obtain regulated membership from one of the six colleges governed by the Psychotherapy Act, 2007 and the Regulated Health Professions Act, 1991 (RHPA): Social Service Worker (SSW) diploma, Bachelor of Social Worker (BSW), or Masters of Social Worker (MSW) program or equivalent for registration with the Ontario College of Social Workers and Social Service Workers (OCSWSSW); Master’s degree central to the practice of psychotherapy or equivalent Bachelor’s level program eligible for registration with College of Registered Psychotherapists in Ontario (CPRO); Baccalaureate Nursing (RN) Programs or equivalent (Registered Practical Nurse [RPN]) eligible for registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO); Bachelor of Science degree or Master of Science in Occupational Therapy or equivalent eligible for registration with the College of Occupational Therapists of Ontario (COTO); Master’s degree in psychology or equivalent eligible for registration with the College of Psychologists of Ontario (CPO); or Medical degree from an accredited Canadian or US medical school or from an acceptable international medical school eligible for registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO).
  • The ability to actively engage with children, youth, and families while fostering sustainable and meaningful interpersonal professional relationships.
  • Proven knowledge in utilizing evidence-based and evidence-informed assessments, counselling techniques, and discharge planning tailored specifically for children, youth, and families.
  • Demonstrated skill in developing goals and plans of care for children, youth, and families based on their individual needs and circumstances, based on the principles of person-centered planning, self-determination, and choice, and providing services reflective of this plan.
  • Knowledge and hands-on experience in implementing clinical interventions for children, youth, and families. Specialized focus on understanding social determinants of health, developmental stages, mental health, substance use health, and family systems in providing one-on-one counselling support and facilitating group sessions.
  • Sound knowledge of the child protection system in Ontario and relevant legislation.
  • Knowledge of and experience with clinically sound documentation standards.
  • Sound clinical acumen.
  • An understanding of the Personal Health Information Protection Act (PHIPA) and the ability to effectively apply privacy practices within the rural living context.
  • Ability to effectively organize and multi-task several competing priorities at any given time with a demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a member of an interdisciplinary team, with minimal supervision.
  • Awareness and commitment to valuing the role of diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace and within the community being served by the position.
  • An understanding of the impacts of intergenerational trauma in the Indigenous community and a sound understanding of culturally relevant approaches in service delivery.
  • Clear understanding of how systemic racism and oppression have adversely affected the social determinants of health for BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and other People of Colour) communities with a demonstrated ability to apply an anti-oppressive/anti-racist perspective in service delivery throughout the lifespan.
  • Ability to recognize and identify situations where incidents of an imbalance of power and privilege may occur and can result in possible negative impacts for service users.
  • Clear understanding of the scope of practice as it relates to the position and in keeping with the applicable Regulatory College and performance of duties within this scope.
  • Advanced skills in oral and written communication.
  • Working knowledge and excellent application of technology, with experience working with Microsoft Office Suite and Outlook and confidence in utilizing other clinical databases and/or platforms (e.g., EMHware, DATIS, CATALYST, Time tracking software, etc.).
  • A valid Ontario Driver's Licence is required. The use of a privately owned vehicle and appropriate insurance coverage are also required.
  • Ability to travel across the District of Thunder Bay and/or out-of-district communities, as required.
  • This position may require flexible work hours, contingent upon client needs.

Qualifications and Requirements THE ‘NICE TO HAVES’

While not required, preference will be given to candidates with the following:

  • Membership in a Regulated Profession, in good standing, from one of the six colleges governed by the Psychotherapy Act, 2007, and the Regulated Health Professions Act, 1991 (RHPA).
  • A preference of three (3) years of experience in a mental health and/or developmental services agency providing clinical interventions for children, youth, and families.
  • Knowledge of the range of community health and social services across the District of Thunder Bay and Northern Ontario and how to access them.
  • Familiarity with evidence-based therapy approaches (e.g., Cognitive Behaviour Therapy [CBT], Solution-focused therapy [SFT], Dialectical Behavioural Therapy [DBT], Mindfulness, etc).
  • Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) is considered an asset.
  • The ability to speak French is considered an asset.


Before starting with us

As our work puts us in direct contact with vulnerable persons in our community, with health and safety as a priority, the successful candidate must complete or obtain the following before the commencement of their employment:

  • A Vulnerable Sector police check.
  • A positive police check does not automatically disqualify an applicant for a position with North of Superior Counselling; however, the Police Check will be reviewed and evaluated to decide on suitability for employment to the specific duties and responsibilities of the position being filled.

North of Superior Counselling Programs is an equal-opportunity employer. We benefit from the diversity of lived experiences in the workplace and encourage applications from qualified candidates who reflect the diversity of the communities we serve. North of Superior Counselling Programs participates in the Government of Canada’s 50-30 Challenge. This program challenges organizations to improve access for women and/or non-binary people and other equity-deserving groups, including those identifying as racialized, Black, and/or people of colour, people with disabilities (including invisible and episodic disabilities), 2SLGBTQ+ and/or gender and sexually diverse individuals, and Aboriginal, and/or Indigenous Peoples to increase the representation and inclusion of diverse groups within their workplace.

Under the Ontario Human Rights Code, Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, and North of Superior Counselling Programs' policies, accommodation requests will be considered throughout the hiring process.

We thank all applicants; however, only those selected for interviews will be contacted.


About Us


Are you seeking exceptional experience working to improve mental health and social well-being in rural communities utilizing a generalist approach? Look no further than North of Superior Counselling Programs (NOSP)!

At NOSP, we are a non-profit multi-service agency dedicated to working together to optimize health and well-being throughout the lifespan. We strive to provide equitable, accessible, and client-driven services that make a real difference in the District of Thunder Bay.

Our services include on-site individual and group-based counselling and/or case management for mental health and addictions, school-based counselling, parental support, and access to specialized services like assessment and referrals for live-in treatment programs.

But that's not all! We also provide supportive roles in formal on-site and virtual psychiatry and psychology diagnosis and assessments. Plus, we offer housing case management with rental supplement support programs. Through our incredibly dedicated volunteers, we provide enrichment and social engagement (EASE) to Adults (18 plus) with a physical disability or older adults (55 plus).

At NOSP, we believe in a generalist approach to care. We aim to collaborate with other service providers to deliver responsive wrap-around, whole-health care through person-centric goal planning. Through clear systems of care and innovative approaches, we strive to provide positive mental health outcomes for young people, adults, and families across the diverse communities of the District of Thunder Bay.

Are you curious about who we are and what we do? Visit our website at . Discover how NOSP is making a difference, and join our team in improving mental health and social well-being in Northern Ontario's rural communities!

title: Senior Clinical Assitant
description:
When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.

At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.

Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

Key Accountabilities:

Project Initiation & Planning

  • Contribute to site activation by:
    • Assisting with the site staff access to vendor systems
    • Access reconciliation quarterly
    • Following-up with sites to ensure staff training completion required by the study, including but not limited to vendor systems
    • Coordinating the Investigator’s Site File printing and shipment to sites as per the instructions received from the project team
    • Assisting with the material / equipment shipment to sites

Project maintenance

  • Contribute to the project management by providing requested data to the clinical project leadership team (e.g. Principal investigator availability, etc…)
  • Contribute to site maintenance and guarantee inspection readiness by:
    • Managing with quality the Trial Master File (TMF), which includes, but is not limited to: upload documents on time, assist with the update of the Expected Document List (EDL) on and ongoing basis and take the applicable actions to prevent and resolve Quality Issues (QIs).
    • Follow up with site staff members and internal study team members regarding pending documents, needed information or pending actions (e.g. trainings to be completed, data to be added to the Electronic Data Capture (EDC), verification of safety information, etc…)
    • Transfer of documents to sponsor TMF systems (if applicable)
  • Supporting investigator’s payment management
  • Address identified site issues and ask guidance to closure, besides to assist the CRAs with the site management issues closure
  • To assist project teams with trial progress tracking by contributing to ongoing CTMS updates, applicable studies systems and trackers with site information.
  • Apply working knowledge and judgment to identify potential issues and provide feedback to study teams, as needed
  • Follow study timelines to ensure successful outcome of the project
  • Participate in all required applicable trainings

Project Close-out

  • Follow up on return of equipment by also coordinating with vendors or internal stake holders
  • Assist the project team (e.g. Clinical Operations Leader and Clinical Research Associate) with database lock activities
  • With the clinical team guidance, collaborate to ensure that all applicable site management administrative closeout procedures are completed on time and with quality.

The successful candidate will combine strong product leadership with deep domain expertise in UEM, MDM, and enterprise security. title: Associate Therapist
description:
About Encircle

Encircle is building a world where LGBTQIA+ youth and their families thrive. Through our dual-service model, we provide life-affirming therapy services alongside community-based programming in environments that are welcoming, supportive, and rooted in our guiding principle: No Sides Only Love.

We specialize in affirming, evidence-based mental health care delivered within communities that may hold complex cultural and faith dynamics. Our clinicians are deeply committed to compassionate care, professional excellence, and collaborative teamwork.


Position Overview

The Associate Therapist provides high-quality, LGBTQIA+-affirming mental health services to youth, adults, and families. This role includes individual, family, and group therapy, and collaboration within a multidisciplinary team.

We are seeking a clinician who is clinically strong, culturally responsive, and energized by working at the intersection of identity, faith, and community.


Note for Students: New or upcoming graduates are encouraged to apply. If selected for the position, we can provide a pre-graduation job offer, allowing you to transition into your clinical career as soon as your degree is officially conferred. Job offer contingent on earning degree.


What You’ll Do

Clinical Care

  • Provide evidence-based, trauma-informed therapy to LGBTQIA+ youth, adults, and families
  • Conduct comprehensive intakes, risk assessments, treatment planning, termination notes, and duties related to ethical care of clients.
  • Maintain a consistent caseload. Offer 28-30 sessions per week. Complete an average 25 therapy sessions per week. Monday thru Friday. Work hours can be as early as 9 AM and as late as 7 PM (in-person) and 8 PM (online)
  • Offer evening availability to support students and working families (10 evening sessions per week. Evening begins at 4 PM)
  • Develop and update treatment plans in alignment with best practices and payer requirements
  • Complete timely, accurate documentation in compliance with HIPAA and insurance standards

Crisis & Safety Support

  • Conduct suicide risk assessments and create safety plans when appropriate
  • Provide crisis intervention within scope of practice
  • Coordinate with internal teams when higher levels of care are needed

Collaboration & Team Engagement

  • Participate in weekly clinical consultation and supervision (2 hours total)
  • Attend organization-wide trainings and in-person gatherings (twice annually)
  • Collaborate with operations staff to ensure seamless client onboarding and billing processes
  • Engage in internal communication platforms to support team coordination

Community Engagement/Marketing

  • Contribute monthly to community-facing programming (e.g., support groups, activity nights, drop-in hours) as part of Encircle’s integrated service model (Plan up to 2 hours a month)
  • Create and maintain a Psychology Today profile. Plan on up to 2 hours per month of marketing to meet session expectations.

Professional Development

  • Maintain active associate-level licensure (CSW, ACMHC, AMFT, etc.) in Utah
  • Complete required supervision and continuing education
  • Engage in ongoing training related to LGBTQIA+ affirming care and evolving best practices


Qualifications

Required

  • Active associate-level licensure in Utah (CSW, ACMHC, AMFT, or equivalent)
  • Experience working with youth, families, or LGBTQIA+ clients
  • Strong diagnostic assessment and treatment planning skills
  • Ability to maintain timely and compliant clinical documentation
  • Evening availability (minimum of 10 evening sessions per week)

Preferred

  • Experience working within conservative cultural or faith-based communities
  • Familiarity with WPATH Standards of Care (SOC8)
  • Experience with EHR systems and digital collaboration tools
  • Group therapy experience
  • Ability to work at our Provo location preferred


What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You approach identity and faith intersections with empathy and nuance
  • You value collaboration and transparent communication
  • You are self-aware about burnout prevention and proactive in managing workload
  • You thrive in mission-driven, fast-paced environments
  • You are aligned with our philosophy: No Sides Only Love

Schedule & Expectations

  • Full-time position
  • Approximately 28–30 scheduled sessions weekly
  • In-person and telehealth availability
  • 10 Evening hours required to meet community needs

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
    • Encircle offers a pay-per-session model, allowing therapists to build a flexible caseload:
      • $50 to $60 per clinical hour (DOE)
      • Potential pay range for 25 sessions a week on a 48 week work year is $60,000 to $72,000 not including benefits.
  • Benefits
    • Medical (HDHP or Traditional options)
    • Dental
    • Vision
    • Life Insurance: $25,000 policy - Premium paid by Encircle
  • Supervision for pre-licensed clinicians to support licensure requirements
  • $500 annual stipend for professional development & continuing education
  • 3 Paid days for CEU
  • PTO
  • Paid Holidays
  • Paid Sick time
  • Up to 4% 401(k) employer match
  • Insurance credentialing support to expand client reach
  • Flexible scheduling – No weekends or on-call requirements. Some evenings required
  • Clinical consultation groups for peer support and case collaboration
  • Access to liability insurance coverage
  • Laptop provided
  • Opportunities for growth to primary therapists once licensure completed
  • Mission-driven workplace culture


Equal Opportunity Employer

Encircle is committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences. We strongly encourage LGBTQIA+ clinicians and allies to apply.

title: Senior Care Unit-Mental Health Tech PRN
description:
Job Description


Job Summary:

Mental Health Technicians provide patient care in a manner that promotes safety, comfort, and a therapeutic environment. Mental Health Technicians assist patients with Activities of Daily Living, attend to patient behavioral issues, and observe patients to determine changes in condition and precautions. Shift Available: 7a-7p




Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Facilitates groups and activities. Plans and implements both specialty groups and health teaching groups. Documents on patients progress in regard to group activities during otherwise un-programmed time, especially weekend time. Assists Activity Therapists, Social Workers and Nurses as directed.
  • Appropriate boundaries are maintained with patients and an understanding of the difference between therapeutic relationships and friendships is demonstrated. Assists other staff in understanding and maintaining these boundaries and reports to supervisor if boundaries are violated by others.
  • Maintains documentation in accordance with departmental/facility standards and requirements of regulatory bodies. Writes legibly, uses approved abbreviation and correct spelling as documented in the clinical record. Demonstrates skill in the area of documentation and is able and willing to help others achieve same level of skill.
  • Understands the importance of maintaining the dignity of the psychiatric patient. Communicates with non-judgmental statements regarding patient behavior, as observed by supervisor and as documented in chart. Follows philosophy of unconditional positive regard toward patients.
  • Under supervision, observes, records, and reports activities of patients requiring special precautions. Completes appropriate observation logs.
  • Interventions and limits are direct, timely, non-threatening, and effective in de-escalating patient or altering behavior.
  • Is able to lead a crisis team within the milieu, giving direction to others in proper policy for resolution.
  • Is able to de-escalate potentially dangerous situations including proper use of time outs, locked seclusion or restraints.
  • Uses good judgment in reporting verbally and in writing all clinically pertinent observations of patients or situations requiring nursing expertise or technical follow up to the charge nurse or other supervisor.
  • As directed by a licensed nurse, performs technical nursing care assignments such as collecting, labeling and storing specimens, weighing patients and taking and recording vital signs.
  • Assists in maintaining a safe and clean environment by reporting equipment that is out of order, reporting other problems to management, cleaning equipment as assigned and receiving linen and supply stock for the unit.
  • Assists in and, as necessary, accompanies patient in admission, transfer, and discharge procedures.
  • Initiates and conducts search of patient and patients’ belongings within the guidelines established by policy and procedure. Carefully monitors for contraband on the Unit and strives to maintain a safe environment.
  • Facilitates patient’s visiting with their families in an orderly and therapeutic manner.
  • Attends and contributes feedback in staff meetings. May initiate and lead staff meetings when a need is recognized. Takes personal responsibility for increasing staff morale and positive attitude on unit.
  • Assists Charge Nurse when requested in assigning staff to groups and assigning duties of other staff.
  • Acts as a preceptor to new MHT’s during their orientation.
  • Performs additional job-related duties as required and necessary within scope of job responsibilities including taking the initiative to complete tasks that are unassigned.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • Current CPR & CPI Certified (Crisis Prevention Institute)

Note: New hire has 60 days in which to get certified in both CPR and CPI, during that time new hire is not assigned patients.

We partner with communities, schools, governments, and global development agencies to deliver impactful programs in WASH, climate resilience, food security, biodiversity, waste management, gender and social inclusion, peacebuilding, and human rights.

You can find out more about Live & Learn in these link

We are now seeking an experienced, strategic, and values‑driven Board Chair to guide the governance of Live & Learn Solomon Islands.



About the Role

The Board Chair serves as the leader of the Board of Governance and plays a pivotal role in strengthening oversight, ensuring robust accountability, and supporting the organisation to deliver high-quality, community‑driven development outcomes.

The Chair will oversee the Board’s governance responsibilities, support strategic decision-making, foster strong engagement with stakeholders, and ensure compliance with relevant policies, legislation, and donor standards.

This is an opportunity to contribute to the long‑term resilience, wellbeing, and empowerment of communities across the Solomon Islands.



Key Responsibilities



As Chair, you will:



Governance & Leadership

  • Lead the Board to effectively discharge its responsibilities in strategy, risk, performance monitoring, and compliance.
  • Ensure effective conduct of Board meetings, including agenda planning, decision-making clarity, and constructive engagement among trustees.

Strategic Direction

  • Guide the development, review, and monitoring of strategic plans.
  • Support high-quality strategic thinking and ensure alignment to Live & Learn’s mission and community needs.

Stakeholder Engagement & Representation

  • Represent Live & Learn in media, donor engagements, and government relations where appropriate.
  • Support the Country Manager in high-level advocacy or strategic discussions.

Board Development

  • Guide and support the ongoing development, performance, and effectiveness of the Board and its members.
  • Ensure board members has access to induction, training, and development opportunities.

Risk, Finance & Compliance

  • Ensure proper oversight of financial controls, risk management systems, and internal audits.
  • Maintain adherence to Live & Learn Network Policies, Companies Act of 2009, Charitable Trust Act, Donor requirements and other relevant legal and compliance frameworks.

Who We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Demonstrated leadership experience in governance, preferably in NGOs or community development.
  • Understanding of Solomon Islands context and development priorities.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strategic thinking and sound judgement.
  • Commitment to Live & Learn values: responsiveness, accountability, transparency, respect, leadership, commitment, and representation.
  • Experience in financial oversight, risk management, or public policy engagement will be highly regarded.



Term & Commitment

Appointment

Voluntary (meeting allowances provided); 2-years term, renewable under the organisation’s governance framework. Voluntary

Commitment

Minimum of three Board meetings per year, with additional strategic engagements as needed.



How to Appy:

Applications close at 4:00 pm on 18th September 2026

Interested applicants are invited to submit the following:

  1. A cover letter outlining your motivation for applying and your relevant experience in relation to the key responsibilities and qualifications.
  2. A current CV, including two professional referees.

Please send your application or any enquiries regarding the role to: elmah.panisi@livelearn.org or call +23698. When submitting your application, please use the subject line: “Application – Board Chair (LLSI)”

Child Safeguarding and Equal Opportunity



Live & Learn is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to the wellbeing and safety of all children. All board members, employees, volunteers are required to agree to and comply with our Child Protection Policy, Fraud Control Policy, Good Practice Manual, and Code of Conduct.

title: Software Engineer - AVP ( Loan Origination)
description:
Who We Are

As Singapore's longest established bank, we have been dedicated to enabling individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations since 1932. How By taking the time to truly understand people. From there, we provide support, services, solutions, and career paths that meet their individual needs and desires.

Today, we're on a journey of transformation. Leveraging technology and creativity to become a future-ready learning organisation. But for all that change, our strategic ambition is consistently clear and bold, which is to be Asia's leading financial services partner for a sustainable future.

Your Opportunity Starts Here.

Why Join

Join a role where you will deliver a secure, scalable, and compliant Loan Origination Platform that drives digital lending transformation in a highly regulated banking environment. You will shape credit workflows, customer onboarding, and lending automation while leveraging AI technologies (including MCP). You will collaborate closely with business, credit risk, and compliance stakeholders to deliver solutions that align with MAS TRM requirements and secure engineering practices.

How You Succeed

You succeed by delivering robust, compliant, and scalable systems that align with MAS regulations and internal risk controls. You uphold strong engineering standards and a quality-first mindset, enabling high levels of automation and low defect rates while effectively balancing speed and governance. You foster a positive team culture, maintain high team engagement, and ensure strong audit readiness. You establish yourself as a trusted partner to business, credit risk, and compliance stakeholders while leveraging AI and automation to improve efficiency, quality, and delivery outcomes.

What You Do

Work within a regional squad of 12 engineers, driving the end-to-end delivery of Loan Origination solutions, including compliance screening, credit assessment, workflow orchestration, and document management. Provide hands-on technical leadership using Java and API-driven architectures while driving automation and testing practices across the squad. Ensure system reliability through observability and monitoring tools (e.g., Kibana) and implement strong quality engineering practices. Drive CI/CD practices (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab) to enable secure and controlled deployments with integrated testing and security checks. Manage data integrity through SQL development and database validation. Leverage AI technologies to enhance development efficiency, automation, and intelligent lending capabilities. Collaborate closely with business, operations, and regulatory stakeholders while ensuring proper documentation, effective communication, and audit traceability.

Who You Are

5-8 years of experience in software engineering (banking or financial services experience preferred). Proven experience delivering Loan Origination Systems (LOS) or digital lending platforms.

Core Skills (Must-Have)

Strong expertise in Java development. Solid experience in the loan origination and lending domain. Proven team leadership experience with end-to-end delivery ownership. Hands-on experience with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitLab, or equivalent platforms. Familiarity with MAS TRM guidelines and working within regulated environments.

Preferred Skills (Good-to-Have)

Experience with test automation tools such as Playwright, Selenium, or ACCELQ. Experience with AI technologies, including MCP or similar solutions. Exposure to observability and monitoring platforms (e.g., Kibana, logging and monitoring tools).

Strengths

Strong understanding of credit workflows and lending processes. Experience integrating with core banking systems, credit bureaus, and KYC/AML platforms. Good knowledge of data governance, risk controls, and regulatory compliance practices. Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills. Strong sense of ownership, accountability, and governance.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
Job Title: Senior Project Manager

Location: Gand Rapids

Classification: Full Time



Why Build Your Career at Owen-Ames‑Kimball



At Owen-Ames-Kimball, you are not just taking a job. You are joining a team that has spent more than 130 years proving that great buildings are built by great people. We trust our employees to do meaningful work, encourage them to grow, and support them with leaders who value integrity as much as results. We are people who value people, and with an average tenure of 12 years, that is something we live every day.

If you are looking for a place where your voice matters, your contributions are recognized, and your work leaves a mark on communities across Michigan, Colorado, and Florida, there is a place for you at Owen-Ames-Kimball.

About this opportunity

Owen-Ames-Kimball Co. is hiring a Senior Project Manager in our Castle Rock office to lead the successful delivery of large, complex commercial construction projects from preconstruction through closeout. This role provides strategic project leadership, overseeing budgets, contracts, schedules, and team coordination while ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, and to the highest quality standards. The Senior Project Manager also mentors project team members and helps drive consistency and excellence across the organization.

What you’ll do

  • Lead all phases of project delivery, including preconstruction, design coordination, procurement, construction, and closeout
  • Oversee budgets, cost projections, pay applications, change management, and financial reporting
  • Direct subcontractor procurement, negotiations, and contract execution
  • Partner with superintendents and preconstruction teams to develop schedules, sequencing plans, and project strategies
  • Coordinate with owners, architects, engineers, and consultants to resolve design and construction challenges
  • Ensure quality, safety, and contract compliance across all project activities
  • Manage risk by proactively identifying issues and implementing mitigation strategies
  • Mentor and support Project Managers and project team members to strengthen overall performance

What we’re looking for

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or related field (preferred)
  • 10+ years of commercial construction experience with proven success leading complex projects
  • Strong expertise in project financial management, contracts, scheduling, and construction operations
  • In-depth knowledge of construction means and methods, codes, and documentation processes
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to mentor others

The O-A-K Advantage

We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including but not limited to salary, 401(k) profit sharing, paid time off, health insurance. You’ll work with a close‑knit, supportive team in a low‑turnover culture where people genuinely enjoy what they do. Our size and values mean your contributions are recognized, your work makes a real impact in the communities we serve, and no two days are the same thanks to a variety of engaging, cross‑departmental tasks. Founded in Grand Rapids in 1891, O‑A‑K is a stable, respected company delivering construction projects annually across Michigan, Colorado, and Florida.

Owen-Ames-KimballCo. complies with all Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) laws and regulations. O-A-K does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, religion, color, sex, national origin, marital status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender Identity and expression, disability, veteran status, pregnancy status or other status protected by law.

Candidates that accept an offer of employment must undergo and pass pre-employment testing including a drug and background screen.

Notice to External Search Firms: Owen-Ames-KimballCo. does not accept unsolicited resumes and will not be obligated to pay a placement fee for unsolicited resumes. O-A-K Talent Acquisition engages with search firms directly for hiring needs.
