title: VP, Construction Financial Control & Reporting
description:
• Do you have the sharp analytical skills needed to check and approve complex change orders without letting extra costs slip through?
  • Do you enjoy turning messy historical and market data into simple, accurate models that predict baseline costs by geography and technology?

If you said yes — read on.

About us


eStruxture Data Centers is an award-winning company and the largest Canadian-owned data center provider with locations in Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver, and Calgary. Our solutions are designed to give customers more: more locations, more capacity, more connections that enable them to run modern, demanding enterprise applications, and offer their business the control to rapidly scale in response to unpredictable changes in business processes. eStruxture provides access to an ecosystem to almost 850 customers that trust and depend on our infrastructure and customer support, including carriers, cloud providers, media content, financial services, and enterprise customers. eStruxture offers colocation, bandwidth, security and support services to customers across Canada in its 16 carrier and cloud-neutral facilities.

Everything starts with our dedicated and talented team. As an award-winning industry leader, our data centers help our customers improve network connectivity, redundancy, and uptime, scale up or down, increase cost savings, and provide a high level of physical security. This would be unachievable without the people of eStruxture.

About the role

A key collaborator within the Finance department, the VP, Construction Financial Control & Reporting
serves as a strategic partner to both the Leadership and Construction & Engineering teams. This role oversees the end-to-end financial lifecycle for a billion dollars per year of investments in our construction projects, from capital expenditures tracking and cash flow forecasting to driving value with the construction team. We are seeking a high-caliber construction control professional who is equally adept at navigating construction meetings as they are at presenting complex financial trends and variances to executive stakeholders. This position has two direct reports.

What You’ll Own

Capex financing tracking and reporting


  • CapEx tracking: Oversee the real-time tracking and reporting of all construction CapEx against project budgets and overall timelines. Identify the source of cost differences and their impact on the total project. Provide early warning for total costs or $/MW cost overruns and potential delays, and review with the construction team possible initiatives to contain the cost increases and get the project back on track.
  • Oversee activities of the finance construction team: manage the activities of the team issuing the POs, organizing the cash deposits, approving supplier invoices for payment, receiving the equipment in the ERP and tracking the progress of the projects.
  • Change management: Monitor and authorize change orders and contract amendments.
  • Controls: Set and apply financial guardrails on the construction projects.

Modeling and forecasting


  • Modeling: using historical and market data, develop models to accurately forecast the timing of CapEx, deposits, and the baseline $/MW while identifying variables (technology type, geography, timelines, etc.) causing fluctuations versus the baseline. Compare the eStruxture metrics with available industry data.
  • CapEx forecasting: oversee the preparation, in collaboration with the construction team, of the quarterly CapEx forecasts and annual budgets for all expansion projects including equipment, labor, materials, professional fees and other expenses.
  • Cash flow forecasting: Review and approve the payments and deposits forecasts for CapEx and work in collaboration with the finance team to ensure the company has the necessary liquidities available when payments are due.

In partnership with the Procurement team


  • Capital efficiency: In partnershipwith the VP, Engineering & Construction, drive capital efficiency by optimizing CapEx spending and timing through strategic equipment selection for various data center environments, robust pricing negotiation, and strategic cash flow management.
  • Vendor Management: Work closely with the procurement team managing the key suppliers, and approve terms such as pricing, payment terms, delivery timelines and PO alignment with agreed-upon terms. Use historical data to compare quotes and challenge vendor pricing



Other


  • Insurance: Prepare information for the insurance companies to obtain construction insurance coverage before the projects start.
  • Actively participate in construction meetings and visit construction sites.


What you bring



Experience


  • 15 years of experience in project control or financial planning within the data center, infrastructure or heavy construction industry. Experience in the data center industry is an asset.
  • Previous experience in project control on construction projects valued at $100M+.
  • Direct experience developing and tracking project metrics, such as cost/Megawatt or similar indicators.
  • Knowledge of construction operations, such as materials, construction methods and procedures.
  • Experience in project management including planning, cost control and forecasting, change management and documentation controls.
  • Experience with complex cost models correlating construction milestones with cash flows.


Education/Certification/Designation


  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics or Business Administration.
  • Advanced knowledge of Excel and experience with ERP systems and project management tools.CPA title is an asset.

Skills & Technical Knowledge


  • Strategic thinking and ability to influence various teams.
  • High organization skills with ability to prioritize multiple deadlines.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities: ability to dig into the "why" behind the numbers rather than taking estimates at face value and challenge the various stakeholders to get to the root cause.
  • Great communication skills: ability to adapt communication style to various stakeholders and to explain complex project aspects in simple terms.
  • Good business acumen and commercial awareness.

Working Conditions

The role has standard working conditions in an office environment with a regular workweek schedule from Monday to Friday. Due to the nature of the role, the incumbent must be able to meet tight deadlines, handle pressure and manage stress.



Ready to make an impact?


If you’re looking for a role where your expertise and leadership will directly influence the growth of a fast-moving company — we’d love to hear from you.

title: Electronics Assembler
description:
About Orpyx

Orpyx is a leading health technology company dedicated to improving outcomes for people living with diabetes through personalized remote care and continuous foot monitoring. Our flagship product, the Orpyx Sensory Insole System, is transforming diabetes care by helping prevent diabetic foot ulcers—one of the most serious and costly complications of diabetes and a leading cause of lower-limb amputation. Our dedicated remote monitoring team, comprised of credentialed nurses, leverages advanced data science and clinical workflows to deliver personalized support, proactive risk detection, and timely clinical escalation. With a whole-person approach to chronic disease management, Orpyx empowers individuals to take control of their health, reduce complications, and maintain mobility and independence. We are an ISO 13485 certified company committed to providing high-quality medical solutions that consistently meet customer needs and regulatory requirements.

Who We Are

At Orpyx, we are a team of mission-driven innovators committed to improving outcomes for people living with diabetes. Our diverse backgrounds across healthcare, medical device, technology, software, data science, and operations enable us to solve complex clinical challenges with rigor and creativity. What unites us is a shared dedication to excellence, accountability, and meaningful impact. As we grow, we are focused on building a high-performing team that values collaboration, continuous improvement, and integrity—while maintaining the supportive and innovative culture that defines who we are.

What We Offer

At Orpyx, you’ll find more than just a job. You’ll join a supportive, purpose-driven culture where your work helps improve health outcomes for people living with diabetes through cutting-edge medical technology. Our total compensation pack includes:

  • Salaried position with starting compensation equivalent to $20–$23 per hour, paid semi-monthly
  • Employer paid health care benefits after 3 months
  • RRSP matching program
  • Employee stock option plan
  • 3 weeks’ paid vacation annually
  • 5 paid flex and 7 paid health days annually
  • In-person events, and team events every second Friday

What You’ll Do

Reporting to the Production Manager and working as part of a cross-functional team, the Electronics Assembler (Manufacturing Technician 2) is responsible for assembly sophisticated, sensitive, precision medical electronics for incorporation into sensory insoles and related products.

This includes:

  • Assemble production components as per work instructions, standard operating procedures, and good manufacturing practices
  • Operate and attend to manual and automated equipment within production
  • Connect component lead wires to printed circuit boards (PCBs) using soldering or other bonding equipment
  • Troubleshoot technical manufacturing issues
  • Align parts using jigs and fixtures for semi-automatic assembly using specialized equipment (example hot-bar bonding)
  • Install finished assemblies in enclosures or plastics
  • Understand and review the product through specified production process, recognizing inconsistencies and following appropriate processes to rectify them
  • Perform on-line go/no-go testing and inspection using measurement instruments, magnifying devices, or other test equipment to ensure assemblies meet production specifications and standards
  • May perform assembly operations under microscope or magnifying device
  • Follow requests for assembly of prototypes based on drawings, sample assemblies or verbal instructions from the Production Manager or engineering
  • Utilize manufacturing software – MES to control workflow and record work progress
  • Support the implementation of continuous improvement initiatives to meet manufacturing demand, product, and quality assurance requirements, while minimizing production costs
  • Liaise with Production Manager, engineers, and others to meet requirements of schedule, quality, and safety
  • Develop, update, and maintain manufacturing records, work instructions and documentation, as required
  • Identify and report product and equipment inconsistencies to the Production Manager
  • Identify and communicate production status, issues, deviations or bottlenecks and general information and escalate issues to Production Manager, as required
  • Support operational initiatives (for example the 5s initiative) by completing administrative tasks including but not limited to inventory, stocking stations, organizing workstations etc.
  • Follow Personal Health Information regulations where applicable
  • Work in compliance with ESD (electrostatic discharge) guidelines
  • Perform other manufacturing related tasks, as assigned
  • Maintain a clean, and safe working environment
  • Perform duties in a manner that is consistent with and committed to upholding the requirements of the quality management system

Additionally, due to the ever-changing and sometimes chaotic environment of an early-stage high-tech company, the Manufacturing Technician 2 may assume additional responsibilities, as required.

What You’ll Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent. Additional technical certifications in electronics assembly is a plus.
  • 2+ years of experience in a manufacturing including experience assembling small parts, electronic components, and fine detail work
  • Attention to detail and precision in manual assembly tasks.
  • Proficiency in using hand tools, power tools, soldering equipment, soldering under a microscope, PCB rework and other assembly tools
  • Proficiency with 0402 component soldering
  • IPC certification is required. Candidates with an expired IPC certification are also encouraged to apply.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with one or more of the following is an asset, but not required:

  • Experience with medical devices, wearable technologies, and/or sensor-related technologies
  • Experience and knowledge in electro-mechanical assemblies and Lean Manufacturing principles and applications
  • Experience working in an ISO 13485 environment

The Details

Employment Status: Permanent full time.

Schedule: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 8:30am-5:00pm with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break. Occasional overtime may be required.

Work Location: This position is required to work onsite at our Head Office located at Suite 205, 1240 – 20th Avenue S.E.

Application Instructions and Deadline: Applications will begin being reviewed on September 3, 2026, and will continue to be reviewed on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Please note that if this job posting remains active, the position is still open and accepting applications.

For more information, visit:

title: Head of Investment Advisory
location: Ho Chi Minh, Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam
description:
Head of Investment Advisory

Location: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

Workplace Type: On-site


About the Role

Are you passionate about transforming macro research, investment strategies, and market data into tangible value for clients? Do you envision building a standardized "One House View" that empowers hundreds of Relationship Managers (RMs) and Advisors to offer unified investment advice? If you're driven to elevate Wealth Management in Vietnam to global standards, where every recommendation is personalized to client goals and risk appetites, this unique opportunity at ACB might be for you. ACB is embarking on a significant transformation to establish a next-generation Wealth Management model, moving beyond mere financial product offerings to become a long-term partner in wealth planning, management, and growth. This role is not a traditional portfolio management position; you will be a core member in designing the investment advisory platforms for ACB's Wealth Management division. The frameworks, model portfolios, risk assessment tools, and investment perspectives you develop will be instrumental for our expert advisors across the entire network, serving our valued Wealth clients.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain a unified "One House View" by synthesizing insights from Research, Fund Management, and market data, translating them into consistent investment perspectives for various market scenarios and guiding asset allocation principles.
  • Design and implement a robust Model Portfolio system, creating standardized portfolios tailored to different risk tolerance levels, establishing principles for asset allocation, rebalancing, and risk management, ensuring alignment with diverse Wealth client segments.
  • Develop comprehensive Risk Profiling frameworks and Goal-based Investing tools, including designing assessment instruments for risk appetite, linking risk profiles to asset allocation and model portfolios, and creating tools to help clients define long-term financial objectives.
  • Build and manage a data library and advisory tools, standardizing key macro, market, and risk indicators, collaborating with Data & Technology teams to develop dashboards and data repositories, and transforming in-depth research into easily digestible content for RMs and clients.
  • Monitor portfolio performance and conduct stress testing, regularly evaluating portfolio effectiveness, developing market scenarios for stress testing, and providing recommendations for adjustments aligned with investment objectives and risk appetites.


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Over 15 years of experience in investment, research, or portfolio management within asset management firms, securities companies, or banks.
  • Deep understanding of macroeconomics, financial markets, and portfolio theory.
  • Proven ability to translate academic research and market analysis into practical advisory solutions.
  • Experience in building Asset Allocation strategies or Model Portfolios is a significant advantage.
  • Possess a long-term, objective, and client-centric mindset.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of conveying technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in financial modeling and data analysis tools.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Economics, or a related quantitative field.


Additional Information

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the strategic direction and foundational architecture of Wealth Management at ACB. You will be instrumental in building a standardized investment advisory system for the entire Wealth Management division, defining the investment philosophy and asset management principles for Wealth clients, and enhancing the capability of RMs to transition from product sales to solution-based advisory. You will contribute to creating one of the most modern and differentiated Wealth Management platforms in the market. This is an ideal position for individuals seeking to make a strategic impact at the model and platform level, rather than solely managing individual investment portfolios. If you are an investment expert, investment strategist, or portfolio manager looking to co-create the future of Wealth Management in Vietnam with ACB, we encourage you to apply or refer suitable candidates to lettm03@acb.com.vn. We look forward to connecting with talented professionals who share our vision.

title: Quality Systems Engineer
description:
What You Will Do

  • Maintain and improve the Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure compliance with automotive industry and customer quality requirements.

  • Lead internal audits of manufacturing processes and quality systems to verify compliance with IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 standards.

  • Manage quality documentation, including standard operating procedures (SOPs), policies, and quality manuals.

  • Drive corrective and preventive action initiatives to address internal and customer-related quality issues.

  • Analyze quality data and metrics to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and process optimization.

  • Serve as a key liaison between operations, engineering, and customer-facing teams to align on quality objectives and issue resolution.

How You Will Do It

  • Administer and maintain the Quality Management System in accordance with IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 requirements.

  • Plan, coordinate, and lead internal quality audits, ensuring effective follow-up on findings and corrective actions.

  • Manage document control processes, including the review, approval, and update of quality-related documentation.

  • Facilitate Root Cause Analysis (RCA) activities and implement CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Actions) processes.

  • Utilize quality tools such as FMEA, PPAP, and Statistical Process Control (SPC) to improve process performance and product quality.

  • Apply problem-solving methodologies including 8D, 5 Why, and Ishikawa to resolve quality concerns.

  • Monitor key quality metrics and collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Support customer quality requirements and ensure effective communication across manufacturing, engineering, and operations teams.

What We Look For

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

  • 2-4 years of quality assurance or quality engineering experience in a manufacturing or automotive environment.

  • Strong knowledge of IATF 16949, ISO 9001, and APQP methodologies.

title: Child and Youth Care Worker (Casual)
description:
Child and Youth Care Worker - Temporary Casual



Location: Grande Prairie


Shifts:

  • Day (7:00 am - 3:00 pm)
  • Evening (3:00 pm - 11:00 pm)
  • Overnight Awake (11:00 pm - 7:00 am)


Before you read on…

  • This is not just a shift on your schedule.
  • This is a role where a child’s trust, joy, and sense of safety depend on you showing up, fully present.
  • If you’re simply looking to add another job to your roster, this is not the right fit.
  • But if you are ready to laugh, play tag, shoot hoops, set healthy boundaries, and be a steady, caring presence through the hard days and the good ones, keep reading.


Why Your Transparency Matters

Our goal is to provide excellence in service for the children we provide care for and build a team with the comfort, knowledge, and skills to truly make a difference.


This work will test your patience, stretch your creativity, and demand your accountability. But it will also give you the chance to make a lasting impact in the life of a child who needs it most.

When expectations are clear from the start, we can prevent unexpected disruptions, which can be heartbreaking for the children and the team.


What Success Looks Like

  • A child smiles because they feel you genuinely care.
  • They invite you into their world, whether that’s basketball, video games, or simply a quiet walk.
  • You set respectful boundaries: “Internet time is done for today,” and they know you mean it, firm but fair.
  • You help them navigate complex emotions with patience, empathy, and consistency.


A Day in the Life

  • Build trust through playful engagement and mentorship.
  • Guide youth through crisis in challenging situations by using role modelling, encouragement, and crisis intervention strategies.
  • Support them with your presence, engagement, and accountability.
  • Create moments of joy, whether that’s organizing a game, cooking together, or teaching life skills.
  • Document daily activities and observations with attention and care.
  • Collaborate with Program Supervisors to support individualized therapeutic plans.


Behaviour Management Comparison


Please note: The Child and Youth Care Worker (CYCW) role is significantly different from a daycare or childcare position. While both involve supporting children, the purpose, approach, and level of responsibility in a CYCW role are unique and specialized.


What Behaviour Management Looks Like in a CYCW Role

In this role, you will be working with children and youth who often have complex behavioural, emotional, and trauma-related needs. Behaviour management is not about basic supervision, it is about understanding the underlying causes of behaviour and responding in a therapeutic, relationship-focused way.
Key aspects include:

  • Providing individualized, trauma-informed care tailored to each child's history and needs.
  • Supporting children and youth who may display behaviours such as aggression, resistance, withdrawal, or emotional dysregulation.
  • Actively building
    trusted, meaningful relationships that help promote healing and stability.
  • Teaching coping skills, modelling healthy boundaries, and providing consistent emotional support.
    This work is
    intensive, relational, and specialized, requiring empathy, patience, and the ability to understand behaviour as communication.


How This Differs From a Daycare Setting

A daycare environment typically focuses on group routines, play-based learning, and general supervision.
Behaviour management usually involves guiding children through common developmental challenges such as sharing, turn-taking, and following simple rules.
Additionally:

  • Children in daycare generally come from stable home environments with minimal trauma-related behaviours.
  • Care is short-term and group-based, rather than deeply individualized.
  • The role emphasizes routine and safety, not therapeutic intervention or long-term relationship building.


What You Bring

  • A deep passion for supporting youth with complex behavioural and emotional needs.
  • Patience, compassion, and the ability to stay calm in tough situations.
  • A balance of playfulness and structure, you can laugh, run, and play, but also hold firm boundaries.
  • Knowledge (or willingness to learn) around trauma-informed care, wholistic well-being, and child development.
  • Experience in youth care, working with complex behavioural needs, social work, or related fields is an asset.


Your patience already shines, having taken the time to read and reflect on this opportunity. Give yourself the space to truly consider whether you are ready to open your heart, and to commit to a life-changing role for both you and the youth, if you are, we would love to hear from you.


Compliance Regulated Requirements

  • Own a reliable 4-door vehicle to transport the individual(s)
  • An active Alberta Class 5 Driver's License
  • A clear Alberta 10-year Driver's Abstract (10 years driving experience is not required)
  • A current Standard/Intermediate First Aid with CPR Level C (Canadian Provider in person, or blended online/in-person)
  • $2 Million Alberta Auto Insurance Liability coverage
  • Clear Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check obtained in last 5 months
  • Clear Intervention Record Check obtained from Children Services in last 5 months


Regulated Physical Requirement

To perform this role, the employee must be able to:

  • Walk and stand for extended periods, including long distances.
  • Bend, kneel, crouch, and maintain balance to prevent falls.
  • Work in varied environments, including outdoor and seasonal conditions.
  • Lift, push, or pull up to 10 lbs. occasionally; reach overhead and outward.
  • Perform fine motor tasks (typing, grasping, holding) and repetitive movements.
  • Communicate verbally and maintain physical stamina for both short and long durations.


The PERKS!

  • Career growth opportunities in a growing, award-winning organization
  • Innovative technology to assist in your daily routine of providing care
  • Mobile App. access technology
  • Cornell University Intervention)
  • Ongoing training & professional development
  • We are partnered with ZayZoon, an employee benefit that gives you instant access to your wages ahead of payday.

We thank all applicants for applying; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Chief of Philanthropy
description:
ABOUT HSSV
For more than 95 years, Humane Society Silicon Valley (HSSV) has been a leader in animal welfare, serving pets and people throughout the Bay Area and beyond. As an independent, privately funded nonprofit organization, HSSV provides adoption and foster programs, veterinary care, behavior and training support, community programs, regional rescue partnerships, and resources that help pets and the people who love them thrive together.

HSSV is nationally recognized for its leadership and impact in animal welfare, with a long history of developing and sharing approaches that improve outcomes for animals and strengthen the human-animal bond. Through its Animal Community Center, Community Pet Clinic, and a dedicated network of donors, volunteers, partners, and supporters, HSSV works to save lives, keep families together, expand access to care, and build a stronger safety net for pets and people.

Mission, Vision & Values
HSSV is driven by a mission to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people, with a vision of a world where animals thrive, people experience the power of the human-animal bond, and families have the resources and support to care for their pets.

HSSV is grounded in the values of Kindness, Courage, and Impact which are brought to life through a collaborative culture centered on empathy, gratitude, belonging, continuous improvement, and celebrating shared success. HSSV encourages their teams to think boldly, drive meaningful change, take thoughtful risks, and work across teams to create lasting impact for animals, people, and the communities they serve.

POSITION OVERVIEW
Reporting directly to the President & Executive Director, the Chief of Philanthropy serves as a key member of HSSV’s executive leadership team, providing strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s high-impact fundraising and donor engagement efforts. This leader will guide the development and execution of long-term philanthropic strategies that generate sustainable revenue, deepen donor relationships, and align philanthropic support with HSSV’s strategic priorities. The Chief of Philanthropy will play a critical role in advancing HSSV’s mission while fostering a strong organization-wide culture of philanthropy.

The Chief of Philanthropy will personally cultivate and steward a targeted portfolio of high-value donors and prospects while providing strategic leadership for the Philanthropy team. The role will oversee individual and major giving, annual giving, planned giving, endowment, institutional giving and grants, donor stewardship, partnerships, and major and principal gift prospects. As a senior leader and visible ambassador for HSSV, this individual will also build strong relationships throughout the community to advance the organization’s philanthropic goals.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, results-driven, and highly collaborative fundraising leader who can translate organizational priorities into clear, measurable philanthropic goals. They will foster a culture rooted in transparency, accountability, partnership, and continuous learning while embedding philanthropy as a shared responsibility across the organization. This leader will bring proven success managing multi-channel fundraising programs, developing data-informed multi-year strategies, cultivating high-capacity donors, and inspiring teams to achieve ambitious goals in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership

  • Lead the strategic direction and execution of HSSV’s multi-year philanthropy strategy, aligning fundraising initiatives, organizational leadership, operational execution, strategic partnerships, and innovative funding opportunities with HSSV’s mission and strategic priorities to drive sustainable revenue growth and maximize philanthropic impact.
  • Build strong cross-functional partnerships across HSSV, leverage organizational expertise and shared insights to strengthen donor experiences, advance fundraising efforts, and achieve collective goals.
  • Cultivate, develop, and empower a high-performing team to achieve fundraising goals and ensure long-term success within an inclusive, collaborative, and mission-driven culture.
  • Direct the development and execution of capital campaigns and other special fundraising initiatives as needed, building the strategy, infrastructure, and leadership necessary to secure philanthropic support for HSSV’s highest-priority needs. This includes partnering with the President & Executive Director, Board, and key stakeholders to develop compelling cases for support, engage lead donors, and drive campaigns to successful completion.
  • Develop and implement a results-driven framework that establishes clear goals, measures impact, and fosters accountability, excellence, and continuous learning.
  • Maintain a personal portfolio of major and principal gift prospects and donors, with direct responsibility for achieving an annual individual fundraising goal through the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-capacity philanthropists and strategic partners.


Culture of Philanthropy

  • Develop and oversee a culture of philanthropy that strengthens and grows individual giving, major gifts, annual giving, endowment, planned giving, institutional giving, and grants while building a sustainable pipeline of philanthropic support.
  • Champion a culture of philanthropy across HSSV by fostering cross-functional collaboration, engaging staff and leadership in fundraising efforts, and embedding philanthropy as a shared organizational responsibility.
  • Build and steward a robust donor engagement strategy that cultivates lifelong supporters, philanthropic leaders, and community ambassadors who advance HSSV's mission and long-term sustainability.


Program Impact

  • Drive strategic financial leadership by overseeing budget planning and financial management to maximize fundraising effectiveness and operational efficiency.
  • Provide strategic oversight of Philanthropy operations to ensure an exceptional donor experience through seamless stewardship, effective talent development, and consistent operational excellence.
  • Lead the strategic use of data, technology, and analytics to strengthen decision-making, enhance fundraising effectiveness, and drive measurable results.
  • Model and promote the highest standards of ethical fundraising by ensuring compliance with the Association of Fundraising Professionals (AFP) Code of Ethical Standards and Professional Practice.


Community and External Relations

  • Serve as a champion and ambassador for HSSV, representing the organization at community events, public forums, and key stakeholder engagements.
  • Build and strengthen strategic partnerships with community leaders, animal welfare organizations, and other nonprofit organizations to expand upon a culture of philanthropy.


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Proven success and results-driven experience in strategic leadership with multi-channel fundraising programs; nonprofit organization a must.
  • Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams, with a demonstrated ability to inspire collaboration, drive results, and foster a culture of accountability and excellence.
  • Proven leadership experience (or capabilities) with cross-functional teams working in a highly collaborative environment.
  • Ability to develop a multi-year fundraising strategy that includes a strategy that is well supported by analytics and business cases that lead to success.
  • Deep passion for the mission of HSSV: to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people.
  • Must excel in key competencies: strategic thinking, integrity and ethical decision-making, strong interpersonal skills, accountability, transparency, and adaptability.
  • Proven ability to lead change initiatives and cultivate resilient, high-performing teams that adapt to evolving organizational needs.
  • Exceptional ability to pivot planning between strategy and operations.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrates sound professional judgment, maintains a high level of confidentiality, and applies strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to achieve results.
  • Outstanding interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust, engage internal and external audiences, and influence outcomes with stakeholders.
  • Animal welfare experience a plus.


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
This position offers a competitive salary range of $230,000 – $250,000, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage; 403(b) retirement plan; flexible spending accounts; paid time off, and additional wellness benefits.


CANDIDATE TIP

Add "apps.bamboohr.com" to your email contact list so you make sure to receive emails from HSSV regarding your application.

title: Junior Consultant
description:
Job Description


Are you someone passionate about reshaping the mining industry through social and environmental practices into Life of Mine plans?


If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you. We’re growing in the North American region and are on the lookout for an ambitious Junior Consultant (Engineer or Scientist) to join our dynamic team. Come be a part of a visionary journey that is all about making a positive impact. This role is open to our Saskatoon office.


At Okane, we believe that integrated mine closure planning is just the starting point to ‘Help Create a Better Tomorrow’. We work with mining companies to return land responsibly and safely, enabling what comes next to serve both people and the planet. Our work challenges the status quo - we advocate for meaningful partnerships with communities, including Indigenous rightsholders, and design solutions that create lasting financial, environmental, and social value. From early-stage planning through to relinquishment, we’re helping reshape the future of mining, and we’re looking for people who want to be part of that transformation.


Responsibilities:

In this role, you will work closely with our interdisciplinary technical teams on projects that span diverse sites with unique challenges to support the development of practical solutions.


Your work will include:

  • Collaborate design work and project scopes with multidisciplinary teams (ie: geoscience, geotechnical, hydrological and geochemical) to ensure optimized feasible mine closure plan and to gain consensus among stakeholders and collaborate towards shared goals.
  • Prepare proficient technical documentation and reporting in area of technical discipline. Prepare or review detailed work scopes for proposals relating to technical discipline.
  • Complete simulations of mine closure and risk assessment conditions for a given model domain development through robust conceptual analysis.
  • Complete background reviews in support of conceptual model development.
  • Foster and maintain client relationships.
  • Plan and complete field investigations such as material sampling programs and construction QA/QC projects.
  • Empathize with stakeholders and communities affected by mining operations and work to address their concerns with sensitivity and understanding.
  • Take ownership of tasks, seek out opportunities for improvement and contribute positively to team efforts.
  • Actively participate in development of workshops, including development of materials.
  • Ensure the highest commitment to ethical behavior, integrity, and transparency in all interactions, particularly when dealing with stakeholders and sensitive environmental issues.
  • Willingness to continuously learn and expand knowledge in technical discipline, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder engagement practices.
  • Ability to analyze environmental data, including soil and water quality data, to inform reclamation plans and closure strategies.
  • Junior-level project management skills to assist in planning, organizing, and executing reclamation and closure projects.


Qualifications:


  • Educational background in environmental, civil, geotechnical or mining engineering, earth sciences, environmental science or geology is an asset.
  • Experience working in professional services or within the mining industry is an asset.
  • Knowledge of environmental principles, regulations, and best practices related to mine reclamation and closure.
  • Genuine interest in environmental sustainability and a commitment to mitigating the environmental impacts of mining activities.
  • Experience in engaging with local communities, stakeholders, and regulators to gather input, address concerns, and build relationships is an asset.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills to convey technical information clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills to identify issues, evaluate options, and develop practical solutions in reclamation and closure planning.
  • Understanding the environmental regulations and permitting requirements relevant to mine reclamation and closure activities could be considered an asset.
  • Experience in facilitating workshops or meetings to develop closure visions with input from various stakeholders considered an asset.
  • Ability to remain resilient and composed under pressure, while maintaining professionalism and focus on achieving project objectives.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities, project requirements, and stakeholder expectations in a dynamic work environment.
  • Meticulous attention to detail to ensure accuracy and precision in data analysis, reporting, and project documentation.


Why Join Okane?

At Okane, we're committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, where every individual is valued for their unique contributions. Our dedicated teams span across the globe, connecting people from diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Our workplace culture is defined by the everyday behaviors of our team and driven by our Core Values: Passionate, Thoughtful & Caring, Smart & Clever, Positive and Humble. We believe in flexibility, work-life balance, and an open-door approach to communication.

We believe in personal and professional development, offering opportunities for continuous learning and growth. At Okane, we foster the opportunity for everyone to grow and develop their skills that align with their career path. As we continue to expand our global presence, we're looking for individuals who share our values and are dedicated to making a positive impact in the world.


How to Apply:

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact in the mining industry and contribute to sustainable land stewardship, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter detailing your experience and why you’re a great fit for this role by September 15th, 2026. Please note that only those candidates who are selected will be contacted.

If you require an adjustment during the recruitment/interview process, please let the HR team know, and we will work with you to meet your needs. For more information about Inclusion, Diversity & Equity at Okane, please click here: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion • Okane Consultants.

title: Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer (DMLRO)
description:
Finora Bank is a specialized bank dedicated to accelerating growth for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises, and entrepreneurs. Licensed by the European Central Bank (ECB), Finora Bank offers innovative financial solutions, including loans, leasing, factoring, and guarantees, to help businesses achieve their full potential.


Based in Vilnius and Tallinn, Finora Bank has a team of 70+ professionals with extensive international experience in banking.


Join the journey of building a fast-growing bank!


DEPUTY MONEY LAUNDERING REPORTING OFFICER (DMLRO)


Position Purpose


The Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer (DMLRO) will be responsible for the quality control of KYC/KYB proccesses, payments and customer alerts, oversight of First Line of Defence processes, and assessment of AML/CFT monitoring systems. The role will also support the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) in preparing STRs and periodic reports, contribute to the improvement of AML/CFT processes, and cover for the MLRO in their absence.


What will you be doing?


First Line of Defence Quality Control


  • Perform quality control of Know Your Customer (KYC) and Know Your Business (KYB) processes, assessing whether customer identification, risk assessment and documentation comply with applicable legal and internal requirements.
  • Monitor the First Line of Defence’s compliance with ongoing due diligence (ODD) and periodic customer data review deadlines.
  • Provide guidance to the First Line of Defence on KYC/KYB, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and other AML/CFT matters.


Transaction Monitoring and Customer Alert Controls


  • Perform quality control of transaction monitoring activities, assessing the quality of reviews conducted by the First Line of Defence and their compliance with established requirements.
  • Perform quality control of customer alert investigations, assessing their quality, timeliness, documentation and appropriate escalation.

title: Application Analyst - Mobility & Airport Technology Systems
description:
What success looks like in this role:

As an Application Analyst - Mobility & Airport Technology Systems, you'll support the technology behind the Unisys Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS), helping airlines keep baggage operations running smoothly. Working across SOTI-managed Android devices, Windows infrastructure, application support, software testing, and operational support, you'll troubleshoot complex issues, support critical systems, and help ensure airport services remain available, secure, and performing to demanding service levels, while building specialist expertise in a unique airport technology environment.

In this role, you will:

  • Own and support the SOTI Mobile Device Management environment and Zebra Android scanner fleet.

  • Support Windows Hyper-V server environments including replication, backups, security patching, domain administration, and troubleshooting.
  • Plan, create, execute, and track testing activities for software releases and patches.
  • Investigate system issues, analyse customer problems, and provide effective resolutions.
  • Develop expertise in the Unisys Baggage Reconciliation System and associated scanning technologies.
  • Support messaging gateway and message queue technologies that underpin the solution.
  • Act as an initial point of contact for operational issues and service requests.
  • Collaborate with airline clients, ground handlers, project teams, and third-party providers.
  • Participate in an out-of-hours on-call support roster to help maintain service continuity.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

  • Experience supporting enterprise mobility environments, ideally within managed services, software support, or operational technology environments.
  • Hands-on experience with SOTI Mobile Device Manager (MDM).
  • Strong knowledge of Android operating systems and mobile device lifecycle management.
  • Experience supporting Windows Server and Hyper-V environments.
  • Solid understanding of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, Active Directory, DHCP, and DNS.
  • Strong troubleshooting, incident resolution, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience supporting business-critical systems within defined SLAs.
  • Excellent customer service, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Experience working with software deployments, upgrades, patching, and testing activities.
  • General IT qualifications and a current driver's licence.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an Airport Airside Security Pass and successfully complete police and reference checks.

Highly Regarded

  • Microsoft Intune administration.
  • Google Admin experience.
  • iOS device management and support.
  • Experience supporting large-scale software solutions.
  • Business analysis, end-user training, database administration, UNIX, or programming experience.

This is a unique opportunity to combine mobility, infrastructure, application support, and airport technology in one role. You'll gain hands-on experience across SOTI MDM, Android devices, Windows infrastructure, software testing, and critical operational systems while building specialist expertise in airline baggage operations. You'll have direct ownership of technology that supports day-to-day airport operations, solving real-world challenges and delivering meaningful outcomes for airline customers.
If you're passionate about technology, enjoy complex problem solving, and want to grow your expertise in a highly specialised environment, we'd love to hear from you. Join Unisys and help keep critical airport baggage operations running smoothly.

title: Senior Advisor, Supervision - DR/SARC/Money Movement
description:
Job Description Summary

Complex transactions. Sensitive client circumstances. Decisions that matter.

The Senior Advisor, Supervision helps protect Raymond James clients and the firm by reviewing money movement activity, identifying potential fraud or financial exploitation, and resolving supervisory matters that do not always have a straightforward answer. This role is for someone who remains calm under pressure, follows the facts, exercises sound judgment, and communicates decisions clearly.

You will independently review and approve day-to-day money movement activity while partnering with financial advisors, branch and regional leadership, Fraud, and other teams to investigate concerns and determine appropriate action. You may also be cross-trained to support Dispute Resolution (DR) and Senior & At-Risk Clients (SARC) and may transition temporarily or permanently among these functions based on business needs. The work can be complex—but it makes a meaningful difference.

Job Description

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Review and approve money movement transactions using applicable regulations, firm policies, supporting documentation, and sound supervisory judgment.

  • Follow the facts to identify inconsistencies, unusual circumstances, potential fraud or financial exploitation, and matters requiring investigation or escalation.

  • Contact clients to verify disbursements that meet established thresholds or when circumstances warrant additional confirmation.

  • Review ACH, Standing Letter of Authorization (SLOA), and Periodic Payment setups for Branch Manager client accounts; communicate findings and address identified concerns.

  • Monitor the Money Movement Supervision inbox, assess next steps independently, and escalate issues when appropriate.

  • Partner with financial advisors, branch managers, regional leadership, Fraud, SARC, and other internal teams to resolve complex account matters.

  • Explain supervisory concerns, decisions, and required actions clearly—even when the conversation is sensitive or the answer is not the one requested.

  • Maintain current knowledge of regulations, firm policies, and emerging money movement risks and apply that knowledge consistently.

  • When assigned, investigate customer disputes and evaluate matters involving senior and at-risk clients.

  • Identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities to strengthen supervisory practices, processes, controls, policies, and procedures.

  • Take ownership of matters from initial review through documented resolution and perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Skill In:

  • Critical thinking and sound judgment, including the ability to interpret requirements and apply them to complex or unusual circumstances.

  • A disciplined eye for detail and risk, balanced with practical consideration for workflow and the client and advisor experience.

  • The ability to manage competing priorities, make timely decisions, and work independently with minimal direct supervision.

  • Clear, confident written and verbal communication with clients, financial advisors, branch managers, regional leadership, and internal partners.

  • Professional composure during sensitive, challenging, or high-stakes conversations.

  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across business units and differing perspectives.

  • A commitment to high-quality service without compromising supervisory standards or risk controls.

Ability To:

  • Follow the evidence: Investigate complex transactions and client circumstances, connect relevant facts, and reach well-supported conclusions.

  • Communicate with clarity: Explain concerns, decisions, required actions, and supporting rationale in a direct, respectful, and well-documented manner.

  • Use sound judgment: Balance regulatory requirements, client circumstances, firm exposure, and probable consequences; recognize when further investigation or escalation is needed.

  • Build expertise: Maintain strong technical knowledge and continue developing capability across Money Movement, Dispute Resolution, and Senior & At-Risk Client matters.

  • Partner effectively: Build trust across Supervision, Operations, Fraud, branches, and regional leadership, and work through differing perspectives to reach appropriate outcomes.

  • See the broader risk: Look beyond an individual transaction when circumstances may indicate fraud, financial exploitation, inappropriate activity, or another heightened concern.

  • Own the outcome: Carry matters from initial review through resolution, manage priorities independently, follow through, and document decisions and actions completely.

  • Adapt and learn: Respond effectively to changing priorities, regulations, emerging risks, and business needs, including assignments across DR, SARC, and Money Movement.

Educational/Previous Experience Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree (B.A) in a related discipline and a minimum of three (3) years of experience in Supervision and/or the financial services industry.

~or~

• An equivalent combination of experience, education, and/or training approved by Human Resources.

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Appropriate series license(s) for assigned functional area preferred or the ability to obtain within an established timeframe.

    • SIE required provided that an exemption or grandfathering cannot be applied.

    • Required to have a Series 7, 9 and 10

    • Series 24 can be used instead of the 9 and 10

  • Additional licenses/certifications demonstrating the candidate’s knowledge/expertise in industry regulation and concepts preferred.

Are You Ready to Make an Impact?

If you are curious, composed, and willing to make well-reasoned decisions when the path is not obvious, we would like to hear from you. The work will not always be easy—but it will matter.

title: Sustainability & Social Value Coordinator
description:

We’re looking for a passionate and proactive Sustainability & Social Value Coordinator to help turn our sustainability ambitions into measurable action.


This is a varied role covering ESG and carbon reporting, social value, customer support, employee engagement and sustainability projects. You’ll work across the business, helping to coordinate our sustainability strategy and ensuring initiatives move from ideas into meaningful outcomes.


It’s a great opportunity for someone looking to develop their career in sustainability, ESG and social value within a business where environmental and social impact genuinely matter.


The Business

Recycling Lives Services is not a typical recycling company. Since 2008, our business has been built around social value – employing people from disadvantaged backgrounds, partnering with the justice system to reduce reoffending and delivering environmental excellence at scale.


As a certified B Corp, scoring 103.5 against a business median of 50.9, we generated £42.9m in social value in 2024, achieved a 61% reduction in CO₂ emissions and diverted 97% of waste from landfill.


We operate UK-wide across construction, manufacturing, retail, utilities and public sector markets, providing total waste management, WEEE recycling and specialist hazardous waste services.

  • Support sustainability sections of customer tenders, proposals and questionnaires.

  • Help deliver sustainability campaigns, training and employee engagement activities.
  • Build relationships with charities, partners and external sustainability organisations.
  • Coordinate sustainability projects and track progress against our strategy and action plans.
  • Research emerging legislation, best practice, accreditations and opportunities to improve our environmental and social impact.


What We're Looking For

You’ll be someone who is organised, analytical and genuinely passionate about sustainability, with the drive to take ownership and make things happen.

Ideally, you'll bring:

  • Strong organisation and project coordination skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and confidence working with data and reporting.

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.

  • A proactive, self-motivated and collaborative approach.
  • An interest in sustainability, ESG and social value.

Previous experience in sustainability, ESG, CSR or environmental management would be advantageous, as would knowledge of carbon reporting, B Corp, ISO standards, tender submissions or ESG reporting frameworks – but we don't expect you to know everything from day one.


What Success Looks Like

You'll help us deliver accurate sustainability reporting, stronger customer ESG support, increased employee engagement and effective delivery of our sustainability strategy. You'll build productive external partnerships and proactively identify opportunities to improve our environmental and social performance.


What We Offer

  • Employee Assistance Programme

Available after 12 months' service.

title: Safety Advisor
description:
Civil Safety Advisor


At Canoco Energy Services, we’re committed to delivering successful projects through safe, efficient, and high-quality construction and civil works. From infrastructure and site development to complex construction projects, we provide customized solutions that deliver real results for our clients.

With safety, quality, and our “we care” culture at the core of everything we do, we are committed to creating safe workplaces where employees, contractors, and clients can succeed.

Join a team where your expertise is valued, collaboration is second nature, and integrity and excellence are our everyday standards.


Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Civil Safety Advisor to support our civil construction projects. The successful candidate will be responsible for promoting and maintaining a strong safety culture across active construction sites while ensuring compliance with applicable Canadian and provincial occupational health and safety legislation.

Experience in civil construction, infrastructure, earthworks, excavation, road construction, utilities, or commercial construction is preferred.


Job Responsibilities

  • Oversee and implement health and safety policies and procedures on civil construction sites.
  • Conduct regular site inspections, hazard assessments, and safety audits to identify and control potential hazards.
  • Monitor construction activities including excavation, trenching, grading, earthworks, underground utilities, concrete work, lifting operations, traffic control, and equipment operations.
  • Provide safety orientations, training, toolbox talks, and daily safety meetings to employees and contractors.
  • Investigate incidents, accidents, near-misses, and unsafe conditions, preparing detailed reports and recommendations for corrective action.
  • Ensure compliance with Canadian occupational health and safety legislation, including applicable provincial OHS regulations and Alberta OHS requirements.
  • Work closely with project managers, site supervisors, forepersons, and contractors to identify hazards and implement effective controls.
  • Conduct and review Job Hazard Assessments (JHAs), FLHAs, Safe Work Plans, and other project-specific safety documentation.
  • Monitor the use of personal protective equipment and ensure workers follow established safe work procedures.
  • Assist with emergency response planning, drills, and emergency preparedness.
  • Maintain accurate safety documentation, inspection records, training records, incident reports, and corrective-action tracking.
  • Follow up on deficiencies and ensure corrective actions are implemented and documented.
  • Promote a proactive safety-first culture across all project activities.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for safety-related matters on assigned civil construction sites.


Qualifications

  • National Construction Safety Officer (NCSO) or equivalent certification required.
  • CRSP designation required.
  • Previous civil construction or industrial construction safety experience required.
  • Experience with excavation, trenching, earthworks, utilities, road construction, infrastructure, or heavy civil projects is an asset.
  • Strong knowledge of Canadian health and safety legislation and provincial OHS requirements, including Alberta OHS.
  • Strong understanding of construction hazards, hazard assessments, and risk-control practices.
  • Knowledge of applicable CSA standards and industry best practices.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively with project management, supervisors, workers, and subcontractors.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to maintain accurate safety documentation.
  • Ability to conduct risk assessments, identify deficiencies, and enforce corrective actions.
  • Proficiency with safety reporting, documentation, and computer-based systems.


Required Tickets / Certifications

  • NCSO or equivalent
  • CRSP
  • H2S Alive
  • CSTS or CSO
  • WHMIS 2015
  • Standard First Aid / CPR
  • Additional construction safety certifications considered an asset


Required tickets and certifications must be submitted with certificates/proof of certification.


Additional Requirements

Successful candidates must pass an Alcohol & Drug (A&D) test as a condition of employment.

The successful candidate must be willing to work in an active construction environment and comply with all company, client, and project-specific safety requirements.

Who You Are (Job Summary)

The Director, Pre-Construction & Scheduling is responsible for establishing and governing the processes, standards, systems, and controls that enable predictable execution across the QTS Development portfolio. Serving as a strategic partner to regional development execution teams, this leader oversees portfolio-wide planning, pre-construction governance, schedule management, cost and schedule compliance, production reporting, risk management, contractor evaluation support, and project controls functions.

Reporting to the VP, Development Pre-Construction & Scheduling, this role develops and drives the standards, metrics, and governance necessary to improve delivery predictability, increase organizational consistency, and provide leadership with visibility into cost, schedule, and execution risks across a rapidly growing development portfolio.

What You Will Do (Job Responsibilities)

Portfolio Planning & Controls Leadership

  • Lead development and implementation of enterprise planning and controls processes across the Development organization.
  • Establish governance frameworks supporting project planning, cost management, schedule management, and execution readiness.
  • Partner with Development executives to improve portfolio predictability, performance measurement, and project outcomes.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across pre-construction, project controls, and schedule management functions.
  • Develop organizational standards, templates, methodologies, and best practices.

Pre-Construction & Development Planning

  • Support project evaluation and early-stage planning activities.
  • Lead development and maintenance of cost, schedule, and execution planning standards.
  • Provide oversight of estimating methodologies, budgeting assumptions, and cost benchmarking programs.
  • Evaluate contractor proposals, schedules, commercial terms, and project delivery strategies.
  • Identify value engineering opportunities and risk mitigation strategies during project development.
  • Support procurement, contract administration, and work authorization processes.

Schedule Governance & Production Tracking

  • Establish portfolio-wide scheduling standards and governance processes.
  • Define schedule compliance requirements and performance expectations.
  • Lead production tracking, forecasting, and schedule analytics initiatives.
  • Develop executive reporting tools and dashboards supporting project and portfolio management.
  • Identify emerging schedule risks and coordinate intervention strategies when required.
  • Maintain enterprise schedule risk management and escalation processes.

Portfolio Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop and maintain performance metrics that provide insight into portfolio health, project execution, schedule performance, and cost management.
  • Ensure consistent and accurate reporting throughout the Development organization.
  • Partner with Data & Analytics teams to improve reporting capabilities and data quality.
  • Deliver executive-level insights and recommendations based on portfolio performance trends.
  • Establish KPIs and reporting frameworks supporting strategic decision-making.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Lead development and implementation of portfolio risk management processes.
  • Monitor compliance with approved development standards, planning requirements, schedules, budgets, and governance expectations.
  • Drive identification, escalation, and resolution of significant project risks.
  • Collaborate with Development, Procurement, Finance, Quality, and Design & Engineering leaders to mitigate delivery risks.
  • Establish project intervention processes for underperforming or high-risk initiatives.

People Leadership

  • Build, develop, and lead teams responsible for development planning, controls, analytics, scheduling, pre-construction, and project governance functions.
  • Establish performance expectations and technical standards.
  • Mentor and develop future functional leaders within the organization.
  • Drive organizational capability building related to project controls and portfolio management.

(Required Qualifications)

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Project Management, Business, or related field.
  • Nine or more years of experience in project controls, construction management, pre-construction, scheduling, development, or similar disciplines.
  • Three or more years of direct people leadership experience.
  • Experience managing complex capital projects or programs.
  • Demonstrated expertise in planning, cost management, scheduling, project controls, governance, and risk management.
  • Proven experience developing enterprise standards, reporting, and performance management processes.
  • Strong collaboration skills and ability to influence leaders across a matrixed organization.
  • Strong analytical, business, and executive communication capabilities.

Nice to Have

  • Twelve or more years of construction, development, project controls, or related experience.
  • Data center, mission-critical, or large-scale infrastructure development experience.
  • MBA, master's degree, PMP, CCM, PSP, or other relevant professional certification.
  • Expertise with scheduling, project controls, analytics, and portfolio management tools including Primavera P6, Power BI, Tableau, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, or similar platforms.
  • Experience establishing new organizational functions and operating models.
  • Advanced experience leading enterprise transformation or process improvement initiatives.

Other Key Skills (KSAs)

  • Strong knowledge of project planning, pre-construction, scheduling, project controls, and portfolio governance.
  • Ability to analyze complex business and project data to identify risks, trends, and opportunities.
  • Knowledge of cost management, schedule management, contractor procurement, and risk mitigation practices.
  • Ability to develop KPIs, dashboards, reporting frameworks, and executive-level insights.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to build teams, develop talent, and drive accountability.
  • Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across a highly matrixed organization.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Proven ability to lead process improvement, standardization, and organizational change initiatives.
  • Proficiency with project controls, scheduling, analytics, and reporting platforms.
  • Demonstrated strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.

title: Student Group Grant Adjudicator
description:
Are you passionate about student groups on campus? Would you like to be a part of enabling student groups to thrive by providing them with opportunities for financial support? Being an Adjudicator for the Student Group Grant Committee (SGGC) will allow you the opportunity to support student groups in their events and financial endeavours.

About The Opportunity
The Student Group Grant Committee (SGGC) disburses the Student Group Granting Program funds and reviews the procedural documents belonging to the Program, under the direction of the University of Alberta Students' Union (UASU). The SGGC is an adjudication committee composed of students with student group executive experience, and aids the UASU and Student Group Services, on behalf of the Students' Council Finance Committee, to provide funding to UASU-recognized student groups for their operations and events.

The SGGC also serves as an advisory committee for the UASU when making changes to the Granting Program. The SGGC is currently taking applications for undergraduate students-at-large to serve on the committee for the 2026/2027 academic year.

Eligibility
To be eligible, an applicant must:
● Be an Undergraduate student at the University of Alberta
● Be a member of the University of Alberta Students’ Union by being up-to-date on UASU fees
● Be a current or past executive member of at least one student group.

If you are part of the Adjudication Committee AND you are part of a student club, your club is still eligible to apply for grants.

Time Commitment
2-3 hours of Adjudication Training done asynchronously. ~10 hours per grant application round (or per semester). This includes Adjudication Meetings, potential Appeals Meetings, and Special Meetings. Adjudications will occur in the 2 months following each grant application deadline (June & July, October & November, and February & March)

Learning Opportunities and Benefits
● Experience in being part of a decision-making committee.
● Experience in a consensus meeting model.
● Financial literacy skills
● Gaining more knowledge of the University of Alberta, and the Students’ Union and the Student Group Granting Program
● Eligibility for an official letter of reference from UASU program staff
● Practical skills and professional experience
● An honorarium of up to $200, or $66.67 per round participated

Deadline
Applications close at 11:59 PM on September 20, 2026. If you have any questions in the meantime, please send an email to clubs@uasu.ca with the subject line "Student Group Granting Committee Application".

title: Small Business Loan Specialist
description:
Position Purpose: The Small Business Loan Specialist supports the bank’s small business lending function by serving as a knowledgeable, customer-focused resource throughout the loan process. This role is responsible for communicating effectively with customers, loan officers, and internal departments to ensure loan requests are handled accurately, efficiently, and professionally. The position also contributes to the continued growth, development, and operational effectiveness of the bank’s small business lending department.


What you’ll do:

· Serve as a primary point of contact for small business lending customers by providing timely, accurate, and professional communication regarding loan requests, documentation requirements, application status, and next steps.

· Partner with loan officers to support the intake, processing, tracking, and follow-up of small business loan applications and related documentation.

· Coordinate with internal departments, including credit, operations, compliance, servicing, and portfolio management, to facilitate an efficient and compliant loan process.

· Review loan files for completeness, accuracy, and consistency with bank policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

· Assist in gathering, organizing, and maintaining required customer information, financial documents, collateral information, approvals, and loan records.

· Monitor outstanding items, follow up with customers and internal partners, and help resolve documentation or process-related issues in a timely manner.

· Support loan officers in delivering responsive service and identifying opportunities to deepen customer relationships and support small business lending growth.

· Maintain a strong understanding of the bank’s small business lending products, processes, procedures, risk standards, and customer service expectations.

· Contribute to process improvement efforts by identifying opportunities to enhance workflow efficiency, customer experience, communication, and departmental effectiveness.

· Analyze financial data to include review of financial statements and personal/business tax returns.

· Underwrite loan facilities while balancing the customers’ needs with the Bank’s risk profile, growth and earnings goals.

· Coach and mentor Business Lenders and Commercial Loan Assistants; assist with training and guidance as needed.

· Prepare reports, updates, and status summaries as needed to support pipeline management, loan tracking, and department leadership.

· Ensure compliance with laws and regulations and adhere to lending compliance guidelines

· All other duties, as assigned

title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer
description:
About The Company

At Corinex, we are driving the future of energy with cutting-edge Broadband over Power Line (BPL) technology. As a global leader in smart grid solutions, we enable utilities to enhance grid visibility, flexibility, and decarbonization, supporting the seamless integration of renewable energy, electric vehicles, and heat pumps into the power grid.


Headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, Corinex is the market leader in Europe, particularly in Spain, where our BPL solutions are deployed by major DSOs (Distribution System Operators) to improve grid operations. With successful implementations across global markets, our technologies accelerate the transition to a more sustainable, decentralized, and efficient energy infrastructure. Recognized as a key contributor to industry standards and a 2024 Deloitte Technology Fast 50 winner, Corinex is shaping the future of smart energy.


About the Job

Corinex is seeking an experienced Senior Embedded Software Engineer to join our engineering team in developing next-generation smart grid communication devices. In this role, you will work on low-level embedded software and platform development across the full product lifecycle, from board bring-up and BSP development to system integration, debugging, validation, and production support.

The ideal candidate has strong hands-on experience with Embedded Linux, C programming, Linux kernel and device drivers, BSP development, bootloaders, and hardware bring-up. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, networking, and test teams to develop reliable and high-performance embedded platforms for our smart grid communication products.

This is a hands-on engineering role suited for someone comfortable working close to the hardware, debugging complex system-level issues, and taking ownership of embedded platforms from initial board bring-up through production deployment.


Duties & Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, integrate, and maintain embedded software for Linux-based communication devices.
  • Develop and maintain Board Support Packages (BSPs), platform software, and low-level firmware components.
  • Perform new board bring-up, hardware-software integration, and system-level debugging.
  • Develop, configure, and maintain Linux kernel components and device drivers.
  • Configure and maintain U-Boot, bootloaders, Device Tree (DTS/DTB), and Linux kernel configurations.
  • Debug hardware and embedded software using tools and interfaces such as JTAG, UART/serial console, GDB, and OpenOCD.
  • Investigate and resolve system-level issues involving hardware, firmware, kernel, drivers, and networking.
  • Work with embedded interfaces and peripherals including SPI, I²C, GPIO, UART, and Ethernet.
  • Support embedded networking functionality, including troubleshooting Ethernet, VLAN/bridge configuration, IP addressing and routing, TCP/UDP, multicast, and network management protocols.
  • Develop and maintain Embedded Linux builds using technologies such as Yocto Project, OpenEmbedded, and BitBake.
  • Collaborate closely with hardware engineers during schematic review, board validation, and product bring-up.
  • Perform structured root-cause analysis and troubleshoot complex hardware-software integration issues.
  • Participate in system architecture and technical design discussions.
  • Develop scripts and automation tools to support build, validation, flashing, testing, and manufacturing processes.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and automated hardware or firmware testing.
  • Conduct code reviews and contribute to engineering best practices, coding standards, and technical documentation.
  • Support manufacturing, factory flashing, recovery tooling, and production testing when required.
  • Mentor junior engineers and provide technical guidance on embedded software development and debugging.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of professional experience in embedded software, firmware, or Embedded Linux development.
  • Strong programming experience in C, with solid understanding of low-level programming concepts.
  • Strong hands-on experience developing software for Embedded Linux systems.
  • Experience with Linux kernel development, BSP development, and/or Linux device drivers.
  • Proven experience with board bring-up and hardware-software integration.
  • Hands-on experience with U-Boot or other bootloaders and Device Tree configuration.
  • Strong experience debugging embedded systems through UART/serial console and JTAG.
  • Experience working directly with hardware, schematics, processors, peripherals, and board-level interfaces.
  • Strong understanding of embedded communication interfaces such as SPI, I²C, UART, GPIO, and Ethernet.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and ability to perform structured root-cause analysis across hardware and software layers.
  • Proficiency with Git-based version control and modern software development practices.


Nice to Have

  • Experience with Yocto Project, OpenEmbedded, and/or BitBake.
  • Experience with Ethernet or networking driver development.
  • Strong understanding of networking concepts including TCP/IP, UDP, VLANs, bridges, routing, multicast, and network management protocols.
  • Experience using OpenOCD, GDB, or similar low-level debugging tools.
  • Experience with factory flashing, firmware recovery, and production tooling.
  • Experience scripting in Python or Shell.
  • Experience with CI/CD and automated hardware or firmware testing.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing or production test environments.
  • Experience with C++, bare-metal firmware, or RTOS-based systems.
  • Experience with embedded communication, telecommunications, networking equipment, industrial networking, or smart grid technologies is an asset.
