We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Note: This description provides an overview of the position and is not exhaustive. Responsibilities may evolve at the discretion of Bow Valley Credit Union.

title: Mental Health Worker - Mobile Crisis Intervention Team
description:
The Mobile Crisis Intervention Team (MCIT) works collaboratively with the O.P.P. Haliburton. This collaboration aims to reduce the number of repeat callers who call Police Services in times of crisis due to mental health and substance use issues. The Mental Health Worker (MHW) - MCIT provides assessment and follow up to individuals who come into contact with Police in a mental health crisis, liaising with community partners and Hospitals to ensure that clients are connected to appropriate services, diverting clients from engaging with the Police due to a mental health crisis.


This position is located in the Haliburton Area. Travel to and throughout Haliburton and the surrounding area is required.


Location: Haliburton and surrounding area
Status: Full-Time Temporary (18 months)

Posting# MHW-MCIT-FTT-08-26

Wage: $31.88 to $33.35 per hour
Application Deadline: 12:00 noon on September 9, 2026


Key Responsibilities

Client Supports

  • Working at/out of a police detachment, respond to police calls and direction to attend in crisis situations
  • Attend with Police Officers at police calls involving individuals who may be experiencing mental health issues or are in crisis
  • Provide crisis intervention services to de-escalate immediate situation
  • Utilize appropriate therapeutic approaches when dealing with potential aggression
  • Immediate assessment of the individual’s mental health needs and, assessment of risk pertaining to the client’s mental health status
  • Collaborate with Police, hospital, shelter, and other crisis intervention services to support the person and family to address immediate mental health needs
  • Work from a trauma-informed and concurrent-disorder-informed approach
  • Formulate and develop support/follow-up plan for individual and care providers
  • Provide brief case management support and services for clients in their place of residence, and in the community
  • Respond to requests from police for follow up and community linkages
  • Assess, implement, and develop evidence-based, best-practice short term interventions based on principles of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and Motivational Interviewing, to promote improved psychological function and recovery
  • Advocate and make appropriate referrals, with consent, for needed services and supports as identified in the client’s service plan
  • Provide mental health, developmental disorder, physical health and concurrent disorder information to individuals, care givers and other service providers
  • Ongoing assessment, monitoring and supporting clients working towards treatment goals.
  • Perform mental health status assessments, where applicable and collaborate with psychiatrists and other medical practitioners
  • Stay current on relevant legislation, best practices, treatment approaches, basic psychopharmacology and agency policies and procedures

Documentation

  • Ensure all client documentation is accurately recorded in a timely manner, e.g., consents, progress notes, service agreements, crisis plans, safety reports, risk assessments etc. as required by agency and program policies and procedures
  • Complete all required program-related data collection (e.g., statistics, outcome measures, e) in an accurate and timely manner
  • Communicate and /or submit case notes or data as required by police, for their records, with appropriate consents
  • Complete administrative tasks e.g., time sheets, expense claims, vacation requests, training
  • Completion of O.C.A.N. assessments as appropriate

Other Activities

  • Liaise with the Hospitals, Police, community partners
  • Attend and participate at Situation Table
  • Develop and promote collaborative partnerships with other service providers, agencies, and community partners
  • Maintain positive and effective working partnerships with Police, hospital staff and community partners
  • Participate in community outreach activities through the development of collaborative partnerships and through presentations, education and visits to community agencies and services as appropriate


Performance Management and Professional Development

  • Participate cooperatively in the agency performance management process/system
  • Stay current on relevant legislation and best practices, current research, policies, and procedures
  • Participate in ongoing professional development and mandatory training
  • Actively engage and participate in supervisory process

Health and Safety – Worker Responsibilities

  • Work in compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, applicable regulations and all organizational health and safety requirements and procedures to ensure the health and safety of clients, staff/colleagues, volunteers, and students
  • Actively participate in workplace, departmental and job-specific health and safety orientation, education, and training
  • Use or wear any equipment, protective devices or clothing required by the employer
  • Operate any equipment and work in a way that does not endanger self or any other worker
  • Comply with established policies, procedure and work practices regarding health and safety
  • Identify and report workplace and job hazards, defects, and contraventions of the Act to the supervisor or employer
  • Report health and safety problems to the supervisor or employer
  • Notify the supervisor if clarification of a policy, procedure or safe work practice is needed
  • Use initiative to reduce risk and apply discretion to solve problems, within scope of authority
  • Work co-operatively with co-workers, supervisor, J.H.S.C. members and others
  • Identify any workplace or job hazards at CMHA HKPR work sites, including defects and contraventions of the Act, reporting to their direct supervisor

Client Safety

  • Adhere to C.M.H.A. H.K.P.R. client safety programs including program policies as well as infection control and prevention procedures. In partnership with clients, family members, and fellow staff, maintain open lines of communication to assist the organization in identifying and achieving quality outcomes for client safety. Report client safety incidents and suggested improvements to manager or delegate.

Quality Assurance Measures

  • Work in compliance with Quality Assurance Measures as outlined in Reg. 299/10 of the “Services and Supports to Promote Social Inclusion of Persons with a Developmental Disability Act, 2008"
  • Work in compliance with all C.M.H.A. H.K.P.R. Quality Assurance Measures policies and procedures

Other Duties as Assigned

  • Attend, participate in team/staff meetings, and all-staff meetings as required
  • Participate in agency quality improvement activities, e.g., accreditation projects, committees, special events, etc.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities at the team/program level
  • Participate in external committees as required
  • Duties may change from time to time


Requirements of the Position

Education and Training

  • Successful completion of Bachelor’s degree in the social/health science disciplines is preferred. A relevant post-secondary diploma combined with significant, demonstrated experience may be considered.
  • We recognize that mandatory training before hire is an asset, however, successful completion of the training applicable to this role shall be requirements for continued employment in this position:
    • Health and Safety Training (including but not limited to the following)
    • Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (W.H.M.I.S. 2015)
    • Infection, Prevention & Control
    • Workplace Violence
    • Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act
    • Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (A.S.I.S.T.)
    • Verbal Intervention (V.I.)
    • First Aid/C.P.R.
    • Ontario Common Assessment of Need (O.C.A.N)

Assets with regard to this position

  • Completion of a Master’s degree is preferred, e.g., Masters of Social Work
  • Formal education in Motivation Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Dialectical Behavioural Therapy, Trauma Informed and Concurrent Disorders.


Related and Relevant Experience

Mandatory experience

  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience working in the mental health field.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the Ontario Mental Health Act, The Health Care Consent Act, social service benefits, related legislation in Ontario and community resources in the Central East Local Health Integration Network.
  • Demonstrated health assessment skills, sound clinical judgment and decision-making skills
  • Demonstrated knowledge and skills in the provision of psycho-social assessment of individuals and families
  • Demonstrated ability to be able to support the client holistically using the biopsychosocial model
  • Demonstrated ability of successful case management experience in an interdisciplinary team environment
  • Proven ability to demonstrate sound clinical judgment with respect to complex client situations
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain a professional attitude, rational detachment and a problem-solving, therapeutic approach while working with sometimes challenging clients and in stressful situations
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively utilize evidence-based interventions and treatments to address mental health
  • Demonstrated ability to adapt treatment modalities to use with diverse clients
  • Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in crisis intervention
  • Solid knowledge of psychiatric medications
  • Comprehensive knowledge of relevant legislation
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively coordinate community resources
  • Demonstrated knowledge of community mental health issues and resources
  • Demonstrated ability to be flexible, manage changing priorities and make quick and sound decisions
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and the ability to be creative in order to find solutions to problems
  • Superior skills required in communication, advocacy on behalf of clients, collaboration with inter-professional team, consultation with professional colleagues in community
  • Demonstrated commitment to own professional development and ongoing education
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organizational skills: demonstrated ability to self-manage time and multiple ta
  • Demonstrated ability to complete accurate and timely documentation
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively manage change on an organizational and program level
  • Demonstrated ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team

Preferred experience

  • Concurrent disorder or addictions experience
  • Mental Health Case Management experience
  • Experience in utilizing best practice modalities (e., Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Dialectical Behavioural Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Trauma- Informed Therapy)
  • Lived expertise with a mental health concern or addiction, either personally or with a family member is an asset


Other

    • Satisfactory police records search and vulnerable sector screening
    • Valid driver’s license
    • Access to an Automobile in good repair and insurance coverage as required by agency policy
    • Satisfactory work-related references


    Working Conditions

    • Work primarily in an office/clinic setting, Police Station and in the community, including client residences.
    • Work directly with individuals with a with serious mental illness and/or dual diagnosis and/or addictions who are experiencing emotional and/or mental health issues and are working towards recovery, may be experiencing crisis instability and various levels of functioning, may be experiencing poverty
    • Primary business hours with flexible hours pending client programming needs
    • Transport clients in personal vehicle, as required
    • There are multiple competing demands which require time management skills, the ability to be flexible and to prioritize
    • There is a high volume of work as well as the unpredictable work, life-threatening situations for others such as instances of suicide

title: Panel Manufacturer
description:
About us:

At Safe Life Defense, we are dedicated to saving lives by providing cutting-edge personal protective equipment that is innovative, reliable, and built with precision. Based in Henderson, Nevada, we are a fast-growing leader in the body armor and protective gear industry, serving law enforcement, first responders, security professionals, and civilians nationwide. Our mission is simple yet powerful: to ensure everyone has access to life-saving protection without compromise.

Our team is passionate about quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. We take pride in our diverse and inclusive work culture, where every team member is empowered to contribute to our success. At Safe Life Defense, innovation drives us, teamwork strengthens us, and making a difference inspires us.

If you’re ready to join a company that values integrity, dedication, and excellence, and if you want to be a part of something that truly matters, Safe Life Defense is the place for you! Let’s make a difference together.

Job Summary:

Safe Life Defense is seeking a detail-oriented Panel Manufacturer to assist in the production of high-quality ballistic panels for our protective gear. This role involves cutting, assembling, and inspecting materials to ensure they meet safety and durability standards. The ideal candidate will have experience in manufacturing, strong attention to detail, and a commitment to precision and quality.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Cut, assemble, and shape ballistic panel materials according to production specifications.
  • Operate machinery and tools safely to ensure efficient production.
  • Inspect panels for defects, ensuring all products meet company and industry standards.
  • Follow detailed work instructions and safety protocols throughout the manufacturing process.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work environment, adhering to workplace safety regulations.
  • Assist with quality control testing and report any defects or issues to supervisors.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet production goals and deadlines.
  • Keep accurate records of materials used and completed panels for inventory purposes.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Previous experience in manufacturing, textiles, or a related field is preferred but not required.
  • Ability to read and follow technical instructions.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality products.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Basic mechanical skills and the ability to operate cutting tools and machinery safely.
  • Ability to stand for long periods and lift materials as needed.
  • Commitment to workplace safety and quality assurance standards.

title: Bilingual Referral Coordinator
description:
Peak Behavioral Health is seeking a Bilingual Referral Coordinator to join our team at our Norman office!

The ideal candidate is proactive, dependable, and thrives in a fast-paced environment. They have excellent organizational skills, enjoy coordinating complex schedules, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and are committed to improving patient access to behavioral health services. They consistently demonstrate empathy, accountability, attention to detail, and a solution-focused mindset while supporting patients and providers throughout the referral process.


The Bilingual Referral Coordinator is responsible for managing the referral, scheduling, and coordination process for psychological testing services. This position serves as the primary point of contact for referral sources, patients, families, providers, and insurance companies to ensure timely access to care while maintaining exceptional customer service.


Essential Functions:

Referral Management

  • Receive and process incoming referrals from physicians, therapists, schools, hospitals, and community partners.
  • Review referrals for completeness and request missing documentation as needed.
  • Enter referrals accurately into the Referral Tracker and appropriate waitlist.
  • Track referral status from receipt through completed evaluation.
  • Maintain referral queues and ensure timely follow-up.
  • Communicate with referral sources regarding referral status and appointment availability.

Patient Scheduling

  • Verify insurance eligibility
  • Schedule psychological testing appointments according to provider availability and testing requirements.
  • Coordinate multi-session evaluations when necessary.
  • Optimize provider schedules to maximize utilization.
  • Maintain waitlists and proactively fill cancellations.
  • Confirm appointments and communicate preparation instructions.
  • Reschedule appointments promptly when needed.

Patient Communication

  • Serve as the primary contact for patients and families throughout the scheduling process.
  • Explain the testing process, timelines, and expectations.
  • Answer scheduling questions professionally and compassionately.
  • Respond to phone calls, voicemail, emails, and text communications promptly.
  • Provide exceptional customer service while maintaining confidentiality.

Provider Coordination

  • Collaborate with psychologists and therapists regarding scheduling needs.
  • Communicate schedule changes efficiently.
  • Documentation
  • Maintain accurate scheduling notes within the EMR.
  • Document patient communications.
  • Upload referral documents and authorizations.
  • Maintain HIPAA-compliant records.

Operational Responsibilities

  • Monitor testing referral volume and scheduling capacity.
  • Assist in reducing wait times through effective scheduling practices.
  • Generate reports on referral activity, waitlists, and scheduling metrics.
  • Participate in workflow improvement initiatives.
  • Cross-train with other scheduling staff.

Quality Expectations

  • Maintain high accuracy in scheduling and documentation.
  • Follow HIPAA and confidentiality requirements.
  • Adhere to organizational policies and procedures.
  • Demonstrate professionalism in all patient interactions.
  • Meet productivity and quality benchmarks established by leadership.


Required Qualifications

  • Bilingual:
  • Spanish and English
  • Fluent in both written and verbal communication
  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Minimum of two years of experience in medical scheduling, behavioral health, healthcare administration, or patient access.
  • Experience working with insurance verification and prior authorizations.
  • Proficiency with electronic health records (EHR/EMR).
  • Strong computer and Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Gmail) skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple competing demands.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, or a related field.
  • Experience scheduling behavioral health or psychological testing.
  • Knowledge of CPT codes, behavioral health billing, and insurance processes.


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Excellent customer service skills
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Professional phone etiquette
  • Conflict resolution skills
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with a team
  • Adaptability in a fast-paced healthcare environment
  • Strong written documentation skills
  • Willingness to accept feedback and make necessary changes
  • Commitment to personal growth through continuing education


Reporting

The Referral Coordinator reports to the Intake Manager.


Work Environment

This position works primarily in an outpatient behavioral health clinic located in Norman, Oklahoma. The role requires frequent interaction with patients, families, providers, referral sources, insurance companies, and internal staff while maintaining a professional, compassionate, and patient-centered approach.


Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by the Referral Coordinator to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the Referral Coordinator is regularly required to speak and hear sufficiently to communicate effectively by phone or in person at normal volumes. The Referral Coordinator’s vision must be adequate to read correspondence, computer screens, forms, etc. The position requires good manual dexterity. The Referral Coordinator is required to sit and use a computer and keyboard for prolonged periods of time. The position requires the ability to reach with hands and arms; and occasionally requires the ability to stand, walk, kneel, bend, lift and move up to 25 pounds.


Classification and Compensation

The Referral Coordinator is an hourly, non-exempt position. Payroll is processed bi-weekly, constituting 26 annual pay periods.

Benefits:

  • Base hourly wage $16 - $20 per hour
  • Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance (Peak will pay for 50% of these insurance premiums for the employee). Dependents can be added as needed, but the employee is responsible for 100% of those costs.
  • Short-Term Disability (100% paid by Peak)
  • Up to 4% matching Retirement benefits, once eligibility requirements have been met
  • Paid Time Off (accrue up to 2 weeks annually; additional accruals following 3 years of full-time employment)
  • 8 Paid Holidays, as outlined in Peak’s Policy Manual
  • Paid Expenses (supplies as needed for Administrative department)
  • Company computer


Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time position with the expectation that the Referral Coordinator works 40 hours weekly. Work is primarily expected to occur during typical weekdays (Monday-Friday); but work and/or training may be requested on weeknights or weekends to ensure the expectations and requirements of the position are being met. Overtime work is not required and, in all situations, must be approved in advance by the COO and/or the CEO.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Full Stack Data Scientist III/IV
description:
Full Stack Data Scientist III/IV

Location: Rabat, Morocco (preferred) or Dakar, Senegal (preferred); open to other IDinsight office locations (Nairobi, Kenya; New Delhi, India; Manila, Philippines; Lusaka, Zambia)

IDinsight is hiring full-time senior data scientists (4 to 8 years of relevant experience) to grow our machine learning, AI, and broader data science capabilities. In this role, the data scientist will leverage their expertise to drive social impact across multiple project teams and clients. You may lead work on models that help locate out-of-school children, LLM-powered co-pilots for teachers, agentic systems that help citizens access benefits, geospatial tools for planning public infrastructure, or optimization models for allocating resources in public health. We are a social-impact-oriented organization, so we can guarantee incredibly meaningful work tackling some of the world's most complex international development challenges.


Build cool stuff. Have a positive impact.

We are working to build IDinsight into a global leader in the use of data science, ML, and GenAI to solve some of the world's most urgent problems. As an expert in the field, you will provide guidance on methods, tools, design, and deployment of the solutions we build.

You'll be joining a growing data science team and working on highly impactful and innovative projects with our partners. We are an entrepreneurial team where you have a strong voice in how the team functions and grows.

You'll get to work on the full spectrum of a solution- from design to deployment. This includes not just data processing and algorithm design, but also full-stack engineering work. You may also evaluate tools that other organizations in the sector are building, and provide critical input for improving or scaling them.

Data science products need to be contextually relevant and build on subject-matter expertise to be effective. You will work closely with our partners and a multidisciplinary team- including economists, social sector experts, and domain experts (public health specialists, education experts, government officials)- to build and test solutions.

Learning is a key part of being a data scientist. 10% of your time would be dedicated to learning new skills and side projects of your choice. You'll have strong mentorship to guide your career, and you'll make interesting and valuable connections.


About IDinsight

IDinsight helps leaders combat poverty worldwide by designing, deploying and promoting evidence-generating tools. We tailor the best methodologies to partner needs and constraints to fuse evidence with action. We serve governments, NGOs, foundations and social businesses across Africa and Asia in all major program areas, including health, education, agriculture, livelihoods, finance, energy and governance.

Our approach rests on four pillars:

  • Rigorous: We develop and use a wide range of cutting-edge data and evidence tools, including experimental evaluations, monitoring systems, data analytics and visualization, process evaluations, machine learning and more.
  • Cost-effective: Every dollar spent is justified by expected impact. If funds could be better used in another way, we say so.
  • Timely: Actionable information is delivered in time for client decision-making deadlines.
  • Demand-driven: We deploy solutions tailored to partner contexts and needs with no competing agendas.

Our diverse, growing team of roughly 200 outstanding colleagues operates in nearly two dozen countries worldwide. Learn more about our mission and values at.


About the Role

We are seeking candidates with a strong background in Python, deep applied expertise in one or more data science specialties (e.g., machine learning, LLMs/GenAI, optimization, geospatial analytics, MLOps, or full-stack engineering for data products), experience building and deploying solutions in production, and a passion for building solutions to difficult social problems. Most importantly, successful candidates should have the ability to learn and adapt quickly, and work independently to solve complex human and technological challenges.

As a senior data scientist, you'll lead multiple projects as tech lead and be responsible for the performance of the solutions. Day-to-day work may include:

  • Working with clients to understand their needs: Understanding their current processes and pain points, identifying which of these can be framed as tractable data science problems, and knowing when they can't, and even when it is, the solution must suit the task and resources available.
  • Leading solution design and delivery end-to-end: Rolling up your sleeves as an individual contributor- writing production code, designing and evaluating methods and models, and building and deploying solutions (including APIs, UIs, CI/CD, etc.); while also working alongside other data scientists to shape the overall approach, synthesize findings, and communicate results.
  • Establishing standards and best practices: Bringing experience in writing quality code, conducting code reviews, and providing feedback on technical and non-technical documentation. Setting the bar for engineering rigor and project management on the team.
  • Coaching and mentoring: Upskilling junior data scientists on methods and approaches, and providing structured feedback on both technical and delivery skills.
  • Providing thought leadership in your specialty: Leading the org through deep expertise in a subset of the following (machine learning, deep learning, GenAI/LLMs, NLP, optimization, geospatial analytics, backend development, frontend development, DevOps, or MLOps) — and drawing on broad familiarity across methods to make sound judgment calls on which approach fits which problem.
  • Shaping the sector: Identifying trends and gaps in the AI-for-Good space; proposing products or services that could address these gaps; and contributing thought leadership on how data science and AI can be deployed responsibly and for the right problem types.

Moreover, professional development for our technical roles is essential for IDinsight’s long-term impact. With support from IDinsight leadership, the employee will maintain self-directed professional development plans and will be given "stretch" opportunities designed to strengthen their professional skills. Real-time feedback and structured reviews are regularly provided to maximize each data scientist’s expertise. IDinsight’s entrepreneurial culture allows roles and career progression to be tailored to individual strengths, interests, and goals. Employees have the opportunity to increase responsibilities, and high performers will have the opportunity to move up in the organization along technical, managerial, or client-facing paths.


Required Technical Qualifications

  • Master's degree and 8 years of experience, or a PhD and 4 years of experience, as a data scientist working in Python.
  • Demonstrated expertise in a subset of the following data science specialties: predictive modelling, machine learning, deep learning, GenAI/LLMs, NLP, optimization, or geospatial analytics.
  • Intermediate-to-advanced Python skills / experience working on complex codebases.
  • Working knowledge of at least one of: AI engineering, MLOps, backend development, DevOps, and frontend development
  • Broad knowledge of advanced machine learning and data science methods.
  • Strong foundations in statistics and probability.
  • Proficiency in collaborative software development practices such as version control and code reviews

Other required qualifications:

  • Proven ability to work independently and with teams in a dynamic, multicultural environment.
  • Experience leading technical teams to deliver complex data science or AI solutions, with a strong interest in mentoring, knowledge-sharing, presenting work and providing feedback to others.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills in English. Professional proficiency in French (written and spoken) is a plus.
  • Self-starter who will thrive while tackling new, unusual and unpredictable challenges.
  • Deeply passionate about global development and improving lives in disadvantaged populations.
  • Strong values aligned with
    IDinsight's values.


Locations

This position is preferably based in Rabat, Morocco or Dakar, Senegal. However, candidates based in other IDinsight office locations (including Nairobi, Kenya; New Delhi, India; Manila, Philippines; Lusaka, Zambia) may also be considered if there is a strong match.

Preference will be given to those with pre-existing work authorization in preferred location; however, IDinsight will seek work permits where possible for exceptional candidates.


Compensation

Compensation is commensurate with relevant experience and background and is competitive within the social sector. Please note that, as a non-profit, we are unable to provide compensation similar to leading technology firms.


Start Dates

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the start date is flexible, with a preference to start almost immediately. We expect a minimum one-year commitment, with regular professional development conversations and potential for a long-term career at IDinsight.


How to apply

Please click the "Apply for this job online" button at the top right. The application asks various questions for us to get to know you and requires a CV and cover letter.

Please ensure that your CV includes relevant professional and personal experience and details on academic qualifications. CVs can range from one to two pages. Please note that headshot photographs, parental information, birth dates, marital status, and other personal information not relevant to the application do not need to be included in your CV. Additionally, we strongly encourage you to use your cover letter to highlight why you want to work for IDinsight specifically and what has prepared you to succeed in the role you’re applying for. A customized cover letter is an important part of IDinsight’s recruiting process as it allows us to understand your motivations for the position, relevant skills, and clarity of writing.

More information, including details on IDinsight’s hiring process and
frequently asked questions, can be found online at IDinsight Careers. Any queries should be directed to redteamcareers@idinsight.org

N.B. To prevent important email correspondence from going directly into your SPAM folder, thereby missing important application updates, please ensure that you whitelist redteamcareers@idinsight.org


IDinsight’s commitment to reducing power asymmetries

IDinsight is committed to
reducing power asymmetries in the social sector. Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion reflects our understanding of the need for the sector to abandon unhealthy practices of the past. We wish to be part of a new generation of international NGOs who are honest about this history and transparent about our role in the present. Our commitment is also aligned with the impact of our work.

We seek a workforce that is inclusive of a variety of perspectives that will help us refine and improve our methods and relationships and strengthen the services we provide our clients and their communities or constituencies. The following commitments represent our vision for the IDinsight team:

  1. IDinsight will have greater representation from the populations we work with and the clients we serve.
  2. IDinsight will have greater representation from the countries in which we work.
  3. Across all countries in which we recruit, we will seek greater representation from historically excluded communities.
  4. IDinsight will foster an inclusive work culture that empowers a diverse team to do their best work.

IDinsight is an equal-opportunity employer and strives to create a diverse and supportive workplace.

title: Buyer
description:
Buyer

Reports To: Supply Chain Manager

FLSA Status: Exempt (Salary)

Work Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. (Flexible) (Schedule varies based on business needs).

Revision Date: March 1, 2026

Position Summary

The Buyer performs professional procurement and supply-chain functions requiring discretion, independent judgment, and decision-making on matters of significance. This role sources and selects suppliers, negotiates pricing and delivery terms, evaluates supplier performance, manages inventory levels, and collaborates cross-functionally to support operational requirements. The Buyer ensures cost-effective purchasing strategies that support production, quality, and overall business goals.

Essential Functions

  • Source raw materials, manufactured components, services, and consumables to support production and business operations.
  • Exercise discretion in supplier selection based on competitiveness, quality, alignment with company values, and long-term supply-chain considerations.
  • Maintain appropriate safety stock levels to support production continuity and mitigate supply chain risk.
  • Identify, evaluate, and qualify new suppliers in collaboration with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain.
  • Monitor supplier performance related to quality, delivery, and responsiveness; address performance issues as needed.
  • Conduct supplier site visits and audits to assess capabilities and compliance with company requirements.
  • Collaborate with Engineering and Quality teams to ensure supplier compliance with drawings, specifications, and quality standards.
  • Coordinate with vendors and logistics providers to optimize freight, shipping methods, and delivery schedules.
  • Lead negotiations on pricing, delivery terms, and vendor agreements to achieve cost and performance goals.
  • Create, manage, and follow up on purchase orders to ensure timely delivery in support of production schedules.
  • Analyze inventory levels and procurement processes to identify opportunities for efficiency, cost reduction, and risk mitigation.
  • Maintain accurate purchasing records, documentation, and reports within ERP systems.
  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance and communicate planned or unplanned absences in accordance with company policy.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area to ensure safety protocols and standards are met.
  • Perform special projects and other duties as assigned.

Safety Responsibilities

  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures.
  • Comprehend, retain, and comply with established safety programs.

Qualifications

Required

  • 3+ years of professional Buyer role within a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong knowledge of procurement processes, supplier management, and price negotiation.
  • Proficiency in ERP systems.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and complex data.
  • Effective written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a diverse work environment with employees at all levels.
  • Demonstrated initiative, problem-solving ability, and attention to detail.
  • Positive attitude, strong work ethic, dependability, flexibility, and timeliness.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to move throughout office, warehouse, and production environments unassisted.
  • Reliable attendance, punctuality, and timely communication of planned and unplanned absences in accordance with company policy.

Preferred

  • Prior experience working with manufacturing equipment.
  • Basic computer hardware and software knowledge.

Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work in both office and production environments.
  • Frequent use of hands and fingers for keyboarding, data entry, and standard office equipment.
  • Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while performing computer-based work.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and move throughout facilities as required.
  • Ability to occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, including listening and speaking.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

Safety Equipment

When entering designated production areas, employees are required to wear steel-toed safety shoes and approved eye protection with side shields. Hearing protection is required only in posted areas of the production environment, in accordance with safety signage and company policy.


Benefit Disclaimer

Condux provides a competitive benefits package featuring medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) employer matching, short-term and long-term disability benefits, and an annual bonus opportunity.

description:

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

title: Program Manager
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
FLIPANY is disrupting the way health and wellness support is offered to communities that have been historically ignored. We serve nutritious food, encourage healthy eating and get people to move. Whether we are working with partners to connect families to food, teaching kids to dice veggies or kick a ball, or designing customized health and wellness programs, FLIPANY takes an active, “hands-on” approach. We incorporate life skills into all of our programs to increase the emotional wellbeing and resilience of the kids and families we serve. We push beyond boundaries and explore every opportunity to offer creative health and wellness initiatives that will inspire people to transform their lives forever.

Position Overview:

We are looking for someone who wants to be part of making their community healthier, connected and genuinely invested in the lives of the youth they serve.

FLIPANY serves youth, adults, and seniors across South Florida through four core areas of work: out-of-school meal programs (Afterschool Meal Program and Summer BreakSpot), senior meal programs, food pantries, and hands-on wellness and nutrition education delivered directly in the community. These include nutrition education and interactive, hands-on food and wellness activities. This position works directly with our community partners throughout Palm Beach County, including schools, after-school centers, community centers, and city-run sites.

This position manages contract deliverables and directly oversees the Program Coordinator. Together, the two roles are responsible for delivering 400 nutrition education sessions in Palm Beach County. In addition to classroom instruction, this role carries responsibility for funder compliance, budget tracking, and day-to-day supervision of program staff.

This role is ideal for a passionate individual who wants to mentor youth directly through social-emotional learning activities and wellness experiences that promote healthy lifestyle habits, while also building and leading the team that delivers this work.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • At least 2 years of experience working with groups of children, with a genuine passion for youth development.
  • Background in Child Development/Behavior, Psychology, or other Social Sciences through education or hands-on experience.
  • Valid Florida Driver's License and access to a reliable vehicle for travel to program sites.
  • Experience managing grant-funded or fee-for-service contracts, including deliverables and compliance requirements.
  • Prior experience supervising staff or contractors.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • A personal commitment to health and wellness, and the ability to model and communicate its value to youth and families in an authentic way
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong administrative and time management skills.
  • A natural relationship builder who collaborates effectively with youth, site staff, and partner agencies with a people-first approach.
  • Calm and adaptable under pressure, maintaining professionalism when unexpected situations arise.
  • Comfortable with technology (iPad, mifi), completing real-time tasks including documentation, surveys, and photo uploads efficiently in a field setting.
  • Accountable and reliable, managing multiple responsibilities and consistently meeting deadlines.
  • Available for occasional evenings and weekends for community outreach or fundraising events.
  • Skilled in contract management, with the ability to track deliverables, budgets, and timelines across multiple sites.
  • Skilled in coaching and supervising staff, delegating responsibilities, and holding a team accountable to shared targets.

Key Responsibilities:



  • Manage day-to-day delivery of assigned contracts, including scheduling, deliverable tracking, and progress toward a committed target of 400 sessions in Palm Beach County, delivered jointly with the Program Coordinator.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for contract-related questions from funders and partner sites.
  • Coordinate with Finance and the Senior Program Manager on budget tracking, invoicing timelines, and contract renewals.
  • Flag delivery risks or deferrals early so scheduling and staffing can adjust.
  • Directly manage and support the Program Coordinator's teaching schedule and workload, ensuring shared session targets stay on track.
  • Provide feedback and coaching to the Program Coordinator and any additional instructors, contractors, or staff.
  • Lead team meetings and conduct individual supervision as needed.
  • Delegate responsibilities, ensure adherence to systems, and promote accountability across the team.
  • Deliver in-person wellness and nutrition education classes to groups of 15–20 youth, following FLIPANY's program guidelines and curriculum.
  • Arrive prepared for each class with all materials, supplies, and equipment packed and ready, handling setup and cleanup at the site for each session.
  • Guide youth through hands-on activities including healthy cooking using tools such as blenders and skillets, gardening, nutrition education.
  • Maintain a positive and structured learning environment throughout each session, addressing behavioral challenges as they arise.
  • Plan for each class by reviewing curriculum, ordering supplies, and confirming site details and scheduling in advance.
  • Complete real-time class documentation including attendance, surveys, and photo uploads using a FLIPANY-issued tablet.
  • Maintain accurate mileage reports for all program-related travel.
  • Communicate proactively with site staff to ensure sessions run smoothly, build strong relationships with partner organizations, and ensure sites uphold program agreements.
  • Report back to the FLIPANY team on class progress, site issues, and cohort updates in a timely manner.
  • Maintain knowledge of FLIPANY's programs and services in order to connect youth, families, and site staff to additional resources and opportunities.
  • Support and supervise volunteers, interns, or AmeriCorps members assigned to assist in class delivery.
  • Participate in required training, curriculum review, and ongoing professional development as directed
  • Monitoring programs, conduct site visits, and ensure compliance with Federal Food program regulations.

Physical Requirements

Work is performed both indoors and outdoors. Exposure to extreme temperatures, extreme sunlight, noise, heights, dirt, dust and potentially hazardous chemicals is common. Work may be performed on uneven surfaces.

While performing the essential functions of this position, the employee must be able to lift, carry and/or push articles weighing up to 50 lbs.

The employee is frequently required to stoop, bend, kneel, crouch, stand, walk, sit and reach with hands and arms. Must have use of hands to finger, handle or feel and/or operate objects, tools or controls.

Must have the use of sensory skills in order to effectively communicate and interact with other employees and the public through the use of telephone and personal contact. Must be able to read, write and communicate in English. Must have the ability to see, read, talk and hear.

Physical capability to effectively use and operate various items of equipment; such as but not limited to a personal computer, calculator, copy machine and fax machine.

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

FLIPANY is a Drug Free Workplace and Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Part-Time F&B Inventory Specialist
description:
Company: Commonwealth Companies
Locations: W.A. Frost & Company, The Commodore Bar & Restaurant, and The University Club of Saint Paul
Location: Saint Paul, Minnesota
Employment Type: Part-Time
Department: Food & Beverage Operations
Reports To: Operations Management


Position Summary

Commonwealth Companies is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and dependable Part-Time Food & Beverage Inventory Specialist to oversee and maintain accurate food and beverage inventory across three hospitality venues:

  • W.A. Frost & Company
  • The Commodore Bar & Restaurant
  • The University Club of Saint Paul

This position is responsible for conducting physical inventory counts, maintaining accurate inventory records, monitoring product usage and costs, identifying discrepancies and waste, and providing management with timely inventory and cost reports.

The ideal candidate is analytical, comfortable working independently, highly accurate with numbers, and experienced with food and beverage inventory in a restaurant, hotel, club, catering, or hospitality environment.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Inventory Management

  • Conduct scheduled physical inventories of food, liquor, wine, beer, non-alcoholic beverages, and other designated F&B products across all three venues.
  • Ensure inventory counts are completed accurately, consistently, and according to established company procedures.
  • Maintain organized inventory records by venue, department, storage location, and product category.
  • Verify product quantities, units of measure, and inventory values.
  • Monitor inventory levels and identify unusually high or low stock levels.
  • Assist management in establishing and maintaining appropriate par levels.
  • Monitor slow-moving, obsolete, expired, or overstocked products.
  • Help ensure proper inventory rotation using FIFO (First In, First Out) practices.

Cost Control & Analysis

  • Track food and beverage inventory values and usage.
  • Assist management with calculating and monitoring food cost, beverage cost, and Cost of Goods Sold (COGS).
  • Compare physical inventory against purchases, transfers, sales, and expected usage.
  • Identify inventory variances, unusual consumption patterns, excessive waste, or potential loss.
  • Investigate significant discrepancies and report findings to management.
  • Assist management in identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve inventory efficiency and profitability.
  • Monitor product pricing and communicate significant vendor cost changes.

Receiving & Invoice Verification

  • Periodically review receiving practices to ensure deliveries are properly counted, inspected, and recorded.
  • Compare vendor invoices against products received when requested.
  • Identify discrepancies involving quantities, pricing, credits, substitutions, or missing products.
  • Assist management with maintaining accurate vendor and purchasing records.

Inter-Company / Inter-Venue Transfers

  • Maintain accurate documentation of food and beverage products transferred between W.A. Frost, The Commodore, and The University Club.
  • Ensure transfers are properly recorded against both the sending and receiving locations.
  • Reconcile transfer discrepancies as part of the inventory process.

Reporting

  • Prepare clear and timely inventory reports for management.
  • Provide inventory valuation and variance reports by venue and product category.
  • Report significant inventory discrepancies or unusual activity promptly.
  • Maintain historical inventory records to assist management in evaluating trends and operational performance.
  • Provide recommendations for improving inventory controls, organization, purchasing practices, and cost management.

Operational Expectations

The Inventory Specialist will work closely with chefs, bar managers, general managers, accounting, and operations management while maintaining independence and objectivity when conducting inventory.

The position requires regular travel between the three Saint Paul venues. Inventory may occasionally need to be conducted outside normal restaurant operating hours to ensure accurate counts and minimize operational disruption.

All inventory information, financial information, pricing, vendor information, and internal operating data must be treated as confidential.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and meet established deadlines.
  • Strong basic mathematical and analytical skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or similar spreadsheet software.
  • Ability to communicate discrepancies and concerns professionally and objectively.
  • Ability to travel between all three Saint Paul locations.
  • Ability to maintain confidential financial and operational information.

Preferred:

  • Previous restaurant, hospitality, food service, accounting, purchasing, or inventory-control experience.
  • Experience conducting restaurant food and beverage inventories.
  • Familiarity with restaurant POS and inventory-management systems.
  • Understanding of food cost, beverage cost, COGS, purchasing, receiving, and inventory variance.
  • Experience working with liquor, wine, beer, and restaurant food inventories.

Physical Requirements

This position requires physical inventory counts in kitchens, bars, coolers, freezers, storage rooms, and other operational areas. The employee must be able to:

  • Stand and walk for extended periods during inventory counts.
  • Bend, reach, crouch, and access shelving and storage areas.
  • Work periodically in refrigerated and freezer environments.
  • Safely lift and move products weighing up to approximately 30–40 pounds.
  • Use stairs and move between multiple storage and operational areas.

Schedule

This is a part-time position with hours primarily determined by the company's inventory schedule. The employee must be available to complete inventory according to established weekly, monthly, and/or period-end deadlines.

Some early morning, evening, or off-hours work may be required to complete accurate physical counts when operations are closed or inventory movement is minimal.

Key Performance Expectations

Success in this position will be measured by:

  • Accuracy and consistency of physical inventory counts.
  • Timely completion of inventory and management reports.
  • Accurate documentation of transfers between venues.
  • Identification and follow-up of material inventory variances.
  • Improvement in inventory organization and accountability.
  • Ability to identify waste, over-purchasing, excessive usage, and cost-control opportunities.
  • Consistent adherence to established inventory procedures across all three venues.

Position Objective

The primary objective of the Part-Time Food & Beverage Inventory Specialist is to provide management with accurate, independent, and timely visibility into food and beverage inventory and costs across all three venues, strengthening accountability, reducing waste and unexplained loss, and supporting informed purchasing and operational decisions.
